description: Obtaining Financial Assistance from the Asian Development Bank for Improving the Quality of Secondary Education in Government Schools
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-10-05
decision_details_body:
-Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2020‑04‑01 to obtain a loan amounting to US $ 400 million from the Asian Development Bank in order to implement Result Based programmes for the Education Sector.

	Accordingly, plans have been drawn to invest the said amount of money under the following sectors:
	
* 	Extensive reform in the secondary education curriculum and in assessment   methodologies.
  
* 	Developing a secondary school network fully equipped with facilities at  Divisional Secretariat Division level and thereby ensuring the access to high quality secondary education opportunities for all children.

* 	Increasing the number of National Schools up to 1000.

* 	Upgrading the National Colleges of Education to the degree awarding status.

* 	Ensuring the teacher balancing and teacher employment and thereby increasing the student achievement level.

	Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to  implement the above mentioned investment programme of US $ 400 million during the  period from 2020 - 2025 through the relevant  institutions connected to the Education Sector for the purpose of implementing of the Educational reforms adhering to the National Policy Statement 'Vistas of Prosperity and Splendour', was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendments to the Workmen's Compensation Ordinance No.19 of 1934 	(Chapter 139)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-10-05
decision_details_body:
-In the policy statement of “Vistas of Prosperity and Splendour” under the heading of “a Culture of Working for the Country”, it has been stated that action would be taken to amend the Workmen's Compensation Ordinance No.19 of 1934 and  increase the compensation payment entitled to the employees in the event of a sudden accident. 

	Accordingly, a draft Bill has been prepared by the Legal Draftsman to amend 	the relevant provisions of the Workmen's Compensation Ordinance in order 	to increase the compensation to be paid to the employees injured due to a 	sudden  accident and it has been observed that the said draft has to be to further 	amended in view of the following reasons. 

    • to increase the fine of Rs 1000 that could be imposed in terms of the existing provisions in a situation where employers fail to submit the statement of compensation to the Commissioner for Worksmen's Compensation in respect of an accident caused to an employee under section 42 of the  the Workmen's Compensation Ordinance.
      
    • to amend the  Schedule IV of the  the Workmen's Compensation Ordinance which indicates the amount of compensations as follows to suit the current situation:
      
          i 	to increase the minimum monthly wage applicable for the 	payment of compensation from Rs. 0 to Rs 10,000/- which 	prevails from Rs. 0 to 2,500/- at present.

          ii	to revise the maximum monthly wage applicable for the 	payment of compensation from Rs. 100, 000/- upwards which 	prevails from Rs. 20,001/- upwards at present. 
          
          iii	to increase the amount of compensation paid in the event 	of death (on the basis of the wage) from Rs. 1,140,000/- 	to 2,000,000/- which prevails from Rs. 181,665/- to 550,000/- 	at present.
          
          iv	to increase the amount of compensation paid in a permanent 	total 	disablement (on the basis of the wage) from 	Rs.1,200,000 to Rs. 2,000,000/- which 	prevails from 	Rs.196,083.80 to Rs. 550,000/- at present.
          
          v	to increase the amount of compensation paid in a temporary 	disablement 	(on the basis of half-monthly wage) from Rs. 	5,000 to  Rs. 47,500/- which prevails from Rs. 1,320 to Rs. 	5,500/- at present.
          
    • to fulfill the task of  recovering the compensation to confiscate the property through the Fiscal/Registrar attached to the Office of the Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation, in order to expedite the process of recovery of compensation.
      
    • to introduce a new insurance scheme for workmen's compensation. 


	Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Labour to further amend the 	draft Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman so as to incorporate the above 	amendments as well, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Promulgation of Regulations on maintaining 'Special Deposit Accounts' under the Foreign Exchange Act, No.12 of 2017
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-10-05
decision_details_body:
-Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2020‑04‑08 to make Regulations under the  Foreign Exchange Act, No.12 of 2017 to open and maintain current deposits in the name of 'Special Deposit Accounts' to deposit the foreign currency remitted to the country through  the banking system for a period of 06 months with the view to encouraging the influx of foreign exchange  into the country. Accordingly, the validity period of the Regulations due to expire on 2020‑10‑07 and as such, the Monetary Board of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka has made following recommendations so as to further retain the foreign exchange remitted to the Sri Lanka -

* 	Payment of interest  rates on normal term deposits for the 'Special Deposit Accounts'  renewed and maintained after maturity.
	
* 	Granting permission to transfer the income on maturity of the 'Special Deposit Accounts' to the other accounts in Sri Lanka.

* 	to credit the income of 'Special Deposit Accounts' of resident individuals but who are not eligible to open Foreign Currency Account (Non Government Organizations, Guarantee Companies etc.) on maturity, to a LKR account, subject to the condition that such income shall not be remitted outside Sri Lanka in the future.

	Accordingly, the proposal made by  the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, to promulgate  new Regulations in terms of section 7 of the Foreign Exchange Act to be read  with the section 29 therein, in addition to the Regulations published in the Gazette (Extraordinary) Notification No. 2170/4 dated 2020‑04‑08 and No. 2182/32 dated 2020‑07‑01 with regard to the Special Deposit Accounts and to present the said Regulations in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Ban on Cattle Slaughter in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-28
decision_details_body:
-As a country with an economy based on agriculture, the contribution of the cattle to develop the livelihood of the rural people of Sri Lanka is immense. Various parties have pointed out that the cattle required for traditional farming purposes is insufficient due to the rise of cattle slaughter and that the lack of sufficient cattle for the improvement of the local dairy industry enabling to enhance the livelihood of the rural community while reducing the large amount of foreign exchange outflow on imported milk powder has become an obstacle for the development of that industry. Accordingly, taking into account this situation, the Cabinet granted approval to implement the following proposals submitted by the Hon. Prime Minister.




*	To take necessary action, without delay, to amend the existing Animals Act No.29 of 1958, the Butchers Ordinance No.09 of 1893 and other relevant consequential laws and rules and regulations passed by the Local Authorities which are being implemented in the country at present pertaining to cattle slaughter. 
	
*	To take necessary action to import beef required for the people who consume beef and provide same at a concessionary price without delay. 

*	To implement a suitable programme regarding the aging cattle, which cannot be used for agricultural purposes effectively.

*	To ban the cattle slaughter in the country with immediate effect, subject to taking aforesaid steps.

description: The Light Rail Transit System Project (LRT) proposed to be implemented 	in the Western region of Sri Lanka under the financial assistance of the 	Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-28
decision_details_body:
-The Cabinet approval has been granted to implement the Light Rail Transit System Project within the Western region of Sri Lanka under the financial assistance of JICA. However, it has been observed that it would not be able to achieve the expected outcome of that project due to the following reasons. 



*	According to the initial plan of the project, it had been proposed to introduce a Light Rail Service with facilities to travel along the overland railway tracks as an alternative mode of transport for persons who come to the city of Colombo for employment and other requirements by using their private motor vehicles. 

*	However, the previous Government, changing the aforesaid plan, had taken the necessary basic measures to implement the proposed Light Rail Transit System on a railway track built on pillars that may cause huge environmental damage.

*	It has been found that if the project is implemented, a large number of buildings including houses and business premises will have to be demolished and a very high cost will have to be incurred for constructing the railway track on pillars.

*	It has been observed that it would not be possible to provide the required facilities through this train expected to be implemented under the proposed Light Rail Transit System as an alternative mode of transport to attract persons, coming to the city of Colombo for employment and other purposes by using their private motor vehicles.

*	Further, it has also been found that if the proposed Light Rail Transit System Project is implemented, a heavy operational cost will have to be incurred for the same. 

	Accordingly, taking into consideration the matters submitted by the Minister of Transport as the Minister in charge of the subject of implementing this Project at present, the Cabinet decided to cancel the Light Rail Transit System Project planned to be implemented in the Western region.

description: Awarding the long term contracts to import diesel for a period of 8 months
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-28
decision_details_body:
-The proposal made by the Minister of Energy to award the following long term procurement to import diesel for a period of eight months from 2020‑10‑15 to 2021‑06‑14 as recommended by the Special Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet. 

*	To award the procurement of 1,365,000 Bbls of Gas Oil with maximum sulphur percentage of 0.05 and 315,000 Bbls of Gas Oil with maximum sulphur percentage of 0.001 to M/s Emirates National Oil Company, Singapore (ENOC).

*	To award the procurement of 1,120,000 Bbls of Gas Oil with maximum sulphur percentage of 0.05 to M/s Emirates National Oil Company, Singapore (ENOC).

description: Procurement for constructing the North Central Main Canal and North 	Western Main Canal under the Mahaweli Water Security Investment 	Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-28
decision_details_body:
The Asian Development Bank has agreed to grant US$ 675 million for the Construction work of Phase 1 and the Feasibility Study of Phase 2 of the Mahaweli Water Security Investment Programme. 17 contract packages are due to be awarded under the Phase I of the project and out of which 10 contracts have already been awarded. As such, the following proposals made by the Minister of Irrigation pertaining to the procurement for constructing the North Central Main Canal and North Western Main Canal under this program, was approved by the Cabinet. 	

*	To take action to award the contract for the construction of the Mahakithula Inlet Tunnel, Mahakithula and Mahakirula Reservoirs and feeder Canal from Mahakithula reservoir to Mahakirula reservoir to China CAMC Engineering Co. Ltd. which has already submitted bids for the same, on the prices agreed upon through negotiations.

*	To take action to award the Contract for the construction of 28km long tunnel section through the Minneriya, Giritale, Hurulu Conservation Forests and Sanctuaries of 95.66 km long North Central Maha Ela Construction Project to be constructed to supply drinking water to the North Central Province and the Vavuniya District in the Nothern Province to China State Construction Engineering Corporation Ltd. which has submitted bids for the same, on the prices agreed upon through negotiations.

description: Provision of School Uniform Material Programme - 2021
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-28
decision_details_body: -The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2020‑06‑10 granted approval to provide school uniform materials through domestic textile manufacturers in place of giving vouchers for school uniforms. Accordingly, relevant procurement process has been initiated and only four domestic textile manufacturers have submitted bids. During the field visits, it has been observed that they have already manufactured approximately 40% of the total textile requirement and it has been confirmed that these manufactures have the capacity to meet the 	total school uniform material requirement by the end of January, 2021. Taking into account the matters submitted by the Minister of Education on providing school uniform materials, the Cabinet granted approval to take necessary action to purchase the total requirement of school uniform material from domestic manufactures and accordingly to provide the school children with uniform materials instead of vouchers.

description: Establishment of a Special Unit under the Ministry of Justice to strengthen 	the process of Administration of Justice
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-28
decision_details_body:
-It is manifestly clear that delays in the legal system in Sri Lanka creates a major 	impact on the people involved in litigation and the country's economy. In the 	year 2016, the National Law Conference Committee complied a report on the 	various issues causing delays in litigation, the adverse consequences of these 	issues, and the proposed solutions for the same. By the end of 2019, there were 766,784 pending court cases in all courts of the country and expeditious solutions need to be considered to address the situation.

	It has been identified that necessary action should be taken in the areas such as development of infrastructure, reform of the law, digitization of courts and capacity building. Accordingly, taking into consideration the proposal made by the Minister of Justice, the Cabinet granted approval to establish a Special Unit under the Ministry of Justice to implement a Law Reforms Programme within a period of 3 years with the contribution of the Legal Experts in the field of Law.

description: Amendment to the Code of Criminal Procedure Act No. 15 of 1979
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-28
decision_details_body:
-An Amendment to the Code of Criminal Procedure Act No.15 of 1979 had been presented to Parliament to authorize the Magistrate to dispense with the requirement of producing suspects or accused persons in person before the Magistrate for extending orders relating to committal to remand custody, in view of avoiding the repetition of unfortunate and violent incidents that occurred recently while transporting prisoners to the courts, However, approval could not be granted to the same due to the Prorogation of Parliament.

 	Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to further amend the Code of Criminal Procedure Act No. 15 of 1979 and to instruct the legal draftsman to prepare amending legislation accordingly, enabling to facilitate the accused and suspected persons to appear before courts by using contemporaneous audio visual links and to provide such facilities for the accused and suspected persons being rehabilitated under a judicial order in a different case, taking also into account the new trends that have arisen under the Covid-19 pandemic, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Draft legislation for the prohibition of Anti-Personnel Mines
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-28
decision_details_body: -On 2017‑12‑13, Sri Lanka acceded to the Convention on the Prohibition of the Use, Stockpiling, Production and Transfer of Anti-Personnel Mines and on their Destruction. In terms of the provisions of the Article 9 of the said Convention, Sri Lanka should draft legislation to implement the provisions of the said convention incorporating appropriate legal, administrative and other measures including the imposition of penal sanctions to prevent and suppress of any such act. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice, to instruct the Legal Draftsman to finalize the drafting process incorporating the observations by the Attorney General with regard to the draft that has been already prepared by the Legal Draftsman, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Pilot project for distributing eco-friendly fertilizer as subsidized fertilizer for the Maha season 2020/2021
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-28
decision_details_body: -Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2020‑02‑20 to allocate Rs 250 million for the implementation of a pilot project for providing organic fertilizer subsidy from the Yala season 2020, under the Chemical Fertilizer Subsidy Programme. Accordingly, paddy has been cultivated around 25,000 hectares in 14 Districts using compost manure, organic liquid fertilizer and bio fertilizer. This has reduced the use of chemical fertilizers by 30% - 50%. Taking into consideration the success achieved by implementation of the pilot project, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture to cultivate 48,000 hectares of paddy using eco-friendly fertilizer during the Maha season 2020/2021 was, approved by the Cabinet.

description: Printing activities of Government and Semi-Government Establishments to be undertaken by the Department of Government Printing
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-28
decision_details_body: -As the Official Printer of the Government, the Department of Government Printing has the potential of carrying out a significant portion of the printing requirements of Government and Semi-Government institutions. However, it has been found, that these institutions pay a large sum of money annually to local and foreign private companies for their printing works. Taking into consideration the above, according to the proposal made by the Minister of Mass Media the Cabinet decided that all Government and Semi-Government Institutions which do not have printing institutions under their Ministries should take steps to get their printing work which is not exceeding 25% of the value of printing requirements, done through the Department of Government Printing.

description: Working Capital requirement for the maintenance of the Buffer Stock of rice for the period from October 2020 to January 2021
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-28
decision_details_body: -Since rice production takes place in the country from October to January every year, the rice requirement during the said period is accomplished through the buffer stock of rice maintained from the rice produced during the other months. Accordingly, it has been estimated that a sum of Rs 2,241 million will be required to maintain the buffer stock of rice which is approximately 3% of the rice requirement for the period of four (04) months from October 2020 to January 2021, i.e. 25,000 metric tons including the cost of storage. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Trade for the issuance of a Letter of Comfort by the General Treasury enabling to obtain a working capital loan for a period of four (04) months from the People’s Bank to Lanka Sathosa so that the said activity can be carried out by the Lanka Sathosa, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding between the University of Peradeniya and the Department of Animal Production and Health (Joint Venture) with the Royal Veterinary College, UK for the implementation of the One Health Poultry Hub Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-28
decision_details_body:
-The University of Peradeniya and the Department of Animal Production and Health (Joint Venture) with the Royal Veterinary College of the United Kingdom have planned to implement a research project known as One Health Poultry Hub with the financial contribution of the Global Challenges Research Fund of the United Kingdom. 



This research project is expected to improve the production of poultry and eggs, to identify the issues that emerge when expanding the local poultry industry to the export sector and direct the production process to the correct pathway through technological and human resource development. The Global Challenges Research Fund of the United Kingdom has agreed to provide 700,000 Sterling Pounds for this project for a period of 05 years. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education for entering into the Memorandum of Understanding relating to the said research project between the said parties,was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Completion work of the project for urgent improvements in the water treatment plant of the Kirindi Oya Water Supply Scheme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-28
decision_details_body: -The Project for urgent improvement in the old water treatment plant of the Kirindi Oya Water Supply Scheme had been entrusted in the year 2019 with the State Engineering Corporation by the then subject Ministry of Housing. However, this project has not yet been completed to date and its present overall progress is 40%. For the construction work, the present capacity of the old treatment plant has been reduced by 50% and consequently the community in the area is confronted with extreme difficulties due to the inability to obtain sufficient water. As such, the proposal made by Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development and Housing, to entrust the responsibility of implementing the Project to the National Water Supply and Drainage Board with the intention of completing the project expeditiously and to provide the allocation for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Renovation and conservation of the Deegawapi Stupa
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-28
decision_details_body: -H.E the President has established a Presidential Task Force for the Management of Archaeological Heritages in the Eastern Province and the said Task Force has planned to establish a fund for the immediate renovation and conservation of the Deegawapi Stupa which is considered as the main Stupa in the Province. Accordingly, the proposal made by H.E the President to establish a Trust Fund to raise funds to fulfill the requirements relating to the renovation and conservation activities of the Deegawapi Stupa and to carry out these renovation and conservation activities through a Sub‑Committee appointed representing both the State and the Private Sector under the Chairmanship of the Secretary, Ministry of Defence, Major General (Rtd) Kamal Gunaratne and Supportive Committees under the supervision of the Presidential Task Force, was approved by the Cabinet

description: Taking further measures regarding the families in the houses reported to be prone to high risk due to a geographical instability in the district of Polonnaruwa
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-28
decision_details_body:
- Walls of 223 houses in 06 Grama Niladhari divisions of the Hingurakgoda Divisional Secretariat Division in the Polonnaruwa district have been unusually cracked due to a geographical instability in the interior of the earth causing the danger of the collapse of those houses. Out of the said houses 67 houses identified to have been severely damaged and uninhabitable, should be evacuated with immediate effect, and resettled in a suitable place. 


Approval of the Cabinet has been granted previously at its meeting held on 2017‑06‑27 for a methodology for the construction of permanent houses for families residing within high risk zones of earth slips and, accordingly taking into consideration the proposal made by the Minister of Irrigation and State Minister of Internal Security, Home Affairs and Disaster Management regarding the necessary measures to be taken on the said affected families, the Cabinet approved to take the following measures -


* 	Evacuation of families from the houses identified as high risk and settle them temporarily in another secure place.


* 	Provision of a rental allowance subject to a maximum of Rs.10,000.00 per month for a period of 06 months for each family so settled.


* 	Implementation of an accelerated housing scheme with required infrastructure facilities by the Ministry of Urban Development and Housing and provide houses from the said Housing Scheme to the families to be evacuated.


*	If the proposed housing scheme cannot be implemented within a short period of time, provide the following relief granted under the resettlement programme for the families who were evacuated due to high risk of landslides in terms of the Cabinet decision dated 2017‑06‑27 to the families to be evacuated from their places of living due to disaster situation in the Hingurakgoda Divisional Secretariat Division. 


i 	Granting Rs.1.6 million to purchase a land with a house.


ii	Granting Rs.0.4 million to purchase a land and Rs.1.2 million to build a house .


iii	If a land has been granted by the State, granting Rs.1.2 million to build a house on such land.

description: Proposal for the Central Bank of Sri Lanka to offer USD/LKR Buy-Sell 	Currency Swaps for tenors between one to two years
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-21
decision_details_body:
- The Central Bank of Sri Lanka has identified the need to facilitate the non‑resident 	investors to invest in Governments Securities and in other sectors with a view to encouraging foreign exchange inflows to the Country. Accordingly, the Monetary Board of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka has permitted to introduce the facility to offer USD/LKR Buy-Sell Currency Swaps for tenors between one to two years. As such, the arrangements submitted by the Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to pursue action as follows with the objective of hedging the foreign exchange risk that may occur to the Licensed Commercial Banks accordingly, was approved by the Cabinet. 

*	To carry out the near and the far legs of the swap under the same exchange rate. 

*	To permit premature unwinding of swaps at the prevalent exchange rate with a penalty.

*	This facility is applicable only if there is foreign exchange inflows into the country and subject to a minimum of US$ 25 million and a maximum of US$ 1000 million.

*	In the event the US$/ LKR exchange rate depreciates during the implementation of this programme, the loss that may cause to the Central Bank of Sri Lanka will be set off in future when transferring its dividends to the General Treasury enabling to treat the loss to the Central Bank as a cost to the General Treasury.

description: Design, Construction and Financing the balance work of the Housing Project at Elliot Place, Borella
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-21
decision_details_body: - The housing project consisting of 400 housing units at Elliot Place, Borella is being implemented by the Urban Development Authority for the middle income earners in the Government and private sector. However, since the said project did not proceed as planned due to financial problems in the company that was awarded the contract for the design, construction and financing of the project, the contract was terminated. This project has been identified as a priority project and, National competitive bids have been called to complete the balance work of the said project. As such, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development and Housing to award the said housing construction contract to M/s Access Engineering PLC, for a sum of Rs 9.37 billion (without tax), as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the Sri Lanka Disaster Management Act No.13 of 2005
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-21
decision_details_body: - Based on the recommendations and proposals of the disaster management professionals and also the experiences gained from the disasters that took place in the past, the Legal Draftsman is currently working on the preparation of a draft Bill to amend the Sri Lanka Disaster Management Act No.13 of 2005 as per the Cabinet approval given on 2016‑09‑13 so as to suit to the present day requirement. In the meantime, since, it has been observed that people evicted from their places of residence due to the damages caused to houses and high risk of landslides, resettle in the same locations again, the Cabinet at its meeting held on 2019‑02‑26 had decided that action has to be also taken to prevent this situation. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Irrigation and State Minister of Internal Security, Home Affairs and Disaster Management to instruct the Legal Draftsman to amend the Sri Lanka Disaster Management Act, No. 13 of 2005 incorporating the said provisions in the draft amendment Bill currently being prepared, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Prohibition of Obscene Publications Bill
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-21
decision_details_body: - Publication of obscene publications produced through information technology and other means using children has increased rapidly during the recent past. Although provisions are contained in the Penal Code and the Obscene Publications Ordinance to take action relating to the said matters, it has been found that those provisions are inadequate to deal with the current circumstances. Therefore, as a remedial measure, a document has been prepared by the Information and Communication Technology Agency of Sri Lanka (ICTA) and the Sri Lanka Computer Emergency Readiness Team (CERT), on the advice of the Attorney General incorporating the information required to draft a new Bill, and accordingly the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft a new bill based on the said document, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The Large Scale Water Supply and Sewerage Projects implemented by 	the National Water Supply and Drainage Board
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-21
decision_details_body:
- The Proposal made by the Minister of Water Supply to treat the following large 	scale projects implemented by the National Water Supply and Drainage Board	as special projects so as to exempt such projects from being charged taxes	under 	the relevant tax laws and accordingly to provide facilities for such	projects, was approved by the Cabinet.

*	Hemmathagama Water Supply Project

*	Ruwanwella Water Supply Project

*	Jaffna and Kilinochchi Water Supply Project

*	Rathmalana/ Moratuwa Wastewater Disposal Project

*	Kalu Gang Water Supply Expansion Project

description: Establishment of the Land Data Infrastructure and Land Information 	Service System
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-21
decision_details_body: - It has been planned to establish the administration networks in the Sri Lanka Survey Department using new technology thereby expediting the survey process and increasing productivity with a view to rendering the services of the Department more efficiently. Accordingly, it has been found necessary to install the Land Information Service System with developed infrastructure facilities enabling the parties using land information to use the said information for their services. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Lands to implement the project for establishing the 'Land Data Infrastructure and Land Information Service System' according to the recommendations submitted by the Information and Communication Technology Agency of Sri Lanka (ICTA), with an investment	of US$ 60.33 million under the Government Programme of Sri Lanka Korean EDCF Loan Funds, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Meeting of the Cabinet Sub-Committee on Cost of Living
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-21
decision_details_body:
- The first meeting of the Cabinet Sub-Committee on Cost of Living appointed by the Cabinet to provide policy and practical solutions to maintain the Cost of Living stable in the country was held under the Chairmanship of H.E the President on 2020-08-31. Accordingly, the decisions taken at the said Sub-Committee meeting pertaining to the following matters to ensure that essential goods including food items are available in the market without any scarcity and to monitor the stable maintenance of the Cost of Living were submitted to the Cabinet by the Minister of Trade and the Cabinet granted its concurrence for the same. 

* 	To focus more attention on the most affected categories, when taking measures pertaining to the reduction of the Cost of Living.

*	To maintain a stable local policy towards motivating the farmers to engage in cultivation and accordingly restrict the imports only to essential goods. 

*	To formulate a system to purchase the goods by the consumers at a reasonable price, providing suitable prices for the products of the farmers since the prices of goods would rise due to the pressure of the intermediaries.

*	To establish a seed bank as a solution to the dearth of various high quality seeds that can be grown locally and for the preservation of local seeds which are progressively getting extinguished.

*	To implement a mechanism for the distribution of products such as vegetables and fruits effectively to the consumers at an affordable price regulating the prices of the same. 

* 	To design and implementation of a programme under the guidance of the Ministry of Plantation, Ministry of Agriculture and the Ministry of Trade to directly purchase the produced from the farmers and sell them in towns in populated areas accordingly.

*	To suspend the import of additional crops which can be cultivated locally since there is a huge tendency of cultivating such crops by farmers, and give priority to promote the increase of production of local vegetables and to promote substitute crops for the crops to be imported.

*	To ensure the availability of sufficient stocks of rice in the market at the guaranteed price by the Government, while maintaining safe stocks of rice without leaving space to escalate rice prices until the paddy harvest of the 	Maha season reaches the market.

*	Due to the complete suspension of the importation of the required materials specially maize required for producing chicken feed, the price of maize has gone up resulting in the increase of the prices of chicken and eggs. Therefore, it has been permitted temporarily to import wheat to be used as a substitute for maize on import permits for the purpose of controlling the escalation of the prices of chicken and eggs. As such, a suitable programme will have to be expeditiously implemented by the responsible Institutions for providing the required lands, seeds, fertilizer and required technology to expand the maize cultivation in the country.

*	The Ceylon Fisheries Corporation to take measures to increase the market stalls and to expeditiously open the 40 stalls designed to be opened enabling the consumers to purchase fish at a reasonable price.

*	Expeditious action to be taken to increase the milk production and for such purpose, implement an arrangement to provide the milk farmers with required facilities and technical knowledge.

*	Since there is a tendency of a price increase of coconuts in the market, to implement a programme to sell coconuts in the populated towns by the Ministry of Plantation, enabling the consumers to	purchase them at a reasonable price.

description: Census of Population and Housing - 2021
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-21
decision_details_body:
- The Census of Population and Housing of Sri Lanka is conducted once in every 10 years and the Department of Census and Statistics, as authorized by the Census Ordinance, has planned to conduct the next Census in the year 2021. This Census will provide qualitative and timely data and information at Grama Niladhari Division level on population, its geographical distribution, various demographic and social characteristics of the population and housing condition required for national policy formulation and planning. Since the planned activities of the Census of Population and Housing - 2021 have been affected due to the COVID - 19 pandemic which prevailed globally as well as locally, the proposal made by the Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to conduct the same as follows, was approved by the Cabinet. 

*	to conduct the activities of listing stage of the Census from January to May, 2021 which had been scheduled to be commenced in July, 2020 

*	to conduct the enumeration stage from June to November, 2021

*	to carry out the data dissemination stage from November, 2021 to May, 2022

*	to conduct the post enumeration survey to establish the accuracy of census data collected at the enumeration stage, in the year 2022.

description: Action taken during the 45th Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-16
decision_details_body: - The Foreign Minister informed the Cabinet that the 45th Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council commenced on 2020‑09‑14 in Geneva, Switzerland and during the session the statements made  by the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights under the topic of “Global Human Rights Update” and by the United Kingdom on behalf of the Core Group of the Resolution 30/1 with reference to Sri Lanka and the response statement made clarifying the position of Sri Lanka on the allegations raised by the above  statements and the Cabinet took note the same.

description: Preparation of Budget 2021
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-16
decision_details_body:
- The Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, presented the policy frame work to be followed in the  preparation of the Budget for the year 2021, giving priority to the following:

* 	Allocation of resources to ensure the outcomes of the Government Policy document 'Vistas of Prosperity and Splendour' is achieved.

*	Allocation of resources to achieve the objectives stated in the Gazette Notification issued pertaining to the assignment of subjects and functions of the Cabinet Ministries and State Ministries.

* 	Provision of safe drinking water to all, implementation of the programme for the rehabilitation and development of 100,000km roads covering the entire country, giving priority to aquatic resources and irrigation sectors.

* 	Allocation of resources required for the Public Investment Programme creating an enabling environment for successful operation of business activities following the expenditure management methodologies under the prevailing circumstances since the State revenue for the 2021 is estimated to be approximately 10.2% of the Gross Domestic Production.

* 	Providing  assistance for the digitalization of the Government processes.

* 	Focus attention on the possibilities of adopting simple methodologies by 	reviewing the existing methodologies enabling to yield better effective results utilizing fewer resources.



Accordingly, the draft Appropriation Bill for the year 2021 is scheduled to be tabled in  Parliament during the second week of October 2020.

The proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, to take necessary action to draft the Appropriation Bill of the year 2021 based on the policies mentioned above, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Term contract for the import of Murban Crude oil for the period of eight (08) months from 2020/10/01 to 2021/05/31
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-16
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by the Minister of Energy to award the term contract for the procurement of the 8,400,000 +/-5% barrels of Murban Crude Oil for a period of eight (08) months from 2020‑10‑01 to 2021‑05‑31 to M/s Emirates National Oil Company (ENOC) of Singapore, as recommended by the Special Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement of Chemical Fertilizer - 2020 Maha Season - Month of October
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-16
decision_details_body: - International open competitive bids have been invited for the procurement of chemical fertilizer required at the end of the month of October during the Maha season 2020. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture to purchase 60,000 metric tons of Urea (Granular) from the Agrifert Liven International Ltd, at a sum of US$ 298.34 per metric ton, under a loan period of 180 days, as recommended by the Special Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding the contract of the construction of the Para - Clinical Building for inaugurating the Faculty of Medicine of the Sabaragamuwa University of Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-16
decision_details_body: - National competitive bids have been invited to construct the Para - Clinical Building of the Sabaragamuwa University of Sri Lanka on design and build basis, for the purpose of inaugurating the Medical Faculty of the Sabaragamuwa University of Sri Lanka. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to award the contract for the construction of the  Para - clinical building for the Faculty of Medicine of the Sabaragamuwa University of Sri Lanka to M/s Maga Engineering (Pvt.) Ltd., at a cost of Rs.1,013.87 million including the relevant Value Added Tax (VAT) as recommended by  the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the relevant labour legislation to raise the minimum age a worker can be employed to 16 years of age
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-16
decision_details_body:
- Approval of the Cabinet was granted at the meeting held on 2020‑06‑10 to amend the relevant labour legislation enabling to  raise the minimum age a worker can be employed  in service to 16 years of age so as to comply with the legal provisions describing the compulsory schooling education as 16 years. Accordingly, the Legal Draftsman has formulated the drafts to amend the  following Acts and Regulations:
	

*	Shop and Office Employees (Regulation of Employment and Remuneration) Act No.19 of 1954 (Chapter 129);

*	Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children  Act No.47 of 1956

*	Act for the amendment of the Minimum Wages (Indian Labour) Ordinance (Chapter 135)
*	Factories Ordinance No.45 of 1942

*	Regulations made under the provisions of the Employees Provident Fund Act, No.15 of 1958 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No.11573 datd 1958‑10‑31.

Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Labour to publish the said Draft Bills in the Government Gazette and thereafter to present the same in Parliament and also to present the Regulations made in terms of the provisions of the Employees Provident Fund Act, No.15 of 1958 in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment of the Children and Young Persons Ordinance and the Youthful Offenders (Training Schools) Ordinance
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-16
decision_details_body:
- In terms of the provisions of the Children and Young Persons Ordinance a child is defined as a person under 14 years. However, according to the Youthful Offenders (Training Schools) Ordinance persons between the age of 16 - 22 are stated as youthful persons. Further in regard to the offenses committed by the children below 16 years the Courts will direct them to the certified probationary schools monitored by the Department of Probation and Childcare Services for correction activities whereas in regard to the offenses committed by children over 16 years, the Courts either sentenced them prison or direct the young offenders to the Training Schools for Youthful  Offenders. However,  in terms of the provisions of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, persons below the age of 18 years should not be sentenced to prison.

Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice, to amend the Children and Young Persons Ordinance to define a child as a person under 18 years and simultaneously to amend the Youthful Offenders (Training Schools) Ordinance so as to define a youthful person as a person between the ages of 18 and 22 years, enabling to solve the existing legal contradiction, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Evidence Ordinance
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-16
decision_details_body: - Since some words and terms appearing in the Evidence Ordinance are completely outdated in today's context, approval of the Cabinet was granted at the meeting held on 2016‑07‑05 to amend the Evidence Ordinance by substituting new words and terms. Accordingly, the clearance of the Attorney General has been received for the draft Bill formulated by the Legal Draftsman and therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to publish the said Bill in the Government Gazette and thereafter present the same in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Programme for the control of Weligama Coconut Leaf Wilt and Rot disease
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-16
decision_details_body: - “Weligama Coconut Leaf Wilt and Rot disease” has spread in twelve (12) Divisional Secretariat Divisions of the Matara District, two (02) Divisional Secretariat Divisions of Hambantota District and two (02) Divisional Secretariat Divisions of the Galle District. It debilitates the palm resulting gradual reduction in the crop yield and as time goes by, the palm will be totally destroyed and it has been confirmed that the disease spreads to the healthy palms as well. Spreading the disease out of the diseased area has totally been controlled by the Disease Management Programme initiated and implemented in the year 2008 while, the disease is being managed successfully within the diseased area. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Plantations to further implement the said programme for the period from year 2021 to 2023, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of the Attanagalla Industrial Estate
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-16
decision_details_body:
- At present, 32 Industrial Estates functioning under the Ministry of Industries  operate throughout the country and private investors have invested approximately Rs.36,500 million in these Industrial Estates. The Government has incurred around Rs.4,517 million for the infrastructure development of these Industrial Estates and the number of employment opportunities generated by these estates is around 18,600.

Even though approximately 150 investors interested in commence the industries  in the Western Province, have submitted their applications, it has been found that they could not be provided with the necessary facilities within the 08 Industrial Estates located in the said Province. Therefore, it has been planned to establish a new Industrial Estate covering both  Gampaha and Kegalle districts and to give priority for manufacturing and assembling of electric and electronic accessories, packaging materials, value added agricultural products, rubber and plastic allied products, garments and allied products and pharmaceuticals and allied products in the said industrial estate and to allocate a space from the proposed  estate for recycling and research development activities.

Accordingly, the Cabinet, as a matter of policy granted approval for the joint proposal made by the Minister of Industries and the Minister of Lands to establish the aforesaid Industrial Estate as a Green Industrial Estate on a land called “Pethiyakanda Watta”of 194 acres in extent  situated at both Attanagalla and Warakapola Divisional Secretariat Divisions belonging to the Land Reform Commission and it was also decided to assign the Department of National Planning to conduct a detailed evaluation in respect of this matter.

description: Construction of 300MW Second Combined Cycle  Liquefied Natural Gas	(LNG) Power Plant at Kerawalapitiya
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-16
decision_details_body: - It has been identified that in order to remedy to the power crisis that could arise 	in the country in the future, it would be appropriate to construct 300 MW LNG	Power Plant at Kerawalapitiya and the construction and implementation of the 	same as an independent Power Project through private investments on Built	Own Operate Transfer (BOOT) business model.  Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Power to take necessary	action to identify a suitable investor following the international competitive	bidding process enabling to complete the project within a period of three	years, was approved by the	Cabinet.

description: Printing and supplying of Passports and Confidential Documents	required for the Government 	through the Government Printing	Department
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-16
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet considered the proposal made by the Minister of Mass Media to	purchase machinery required for the printing of passports and	confidential 	documents required for the Government by the Government	Printing Department itself 	enabling to retain the foreign exchange outflow	within the country, since they are currently being printed by foreign printing	institutions and decided to assign the Department of National Planning to	conduct a detailed evaluation of the project.

description: Submission of the Gazette Extraordinary Notifications published under the Sri Lanka Export Development Act, No.40 of 1979 in Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-16
decision_details_body:
- The proposal made by the Minister of Trade to submit four Gazette	Extraordinary Notifications issued for the following purposes under the Sri	Lanka Export Development Act, No.40 of 1979 in Parliament, was approved	by the Cabinet.

*	Exemption of the payment of CESS on the importation or importation and supply or importation and donation of products such as medicines, chemicals, health care equipment and machinery required for the prevention of COVID‑19 on the request of the Ministry of Health, Tri -Forces and the COVID Centre.

*	Levying the CESS on the importation of Portland Cement on the basis of unit rate in place of advalorem basis.

*	Removal of CESS levy on importation of cement clinkers.

*	Imposition of CESS levy on importation of certain parts required for footwear manufacturing, filament bulbs and flexible packaging materials.

description: Relief assistance to the affected families of Amphan Cyclone
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-16
decision_details_body: - Amphan Cyclone which lasted for 04 days from 16th May, 2020 to 19th May 2020 has severely damaged the banana and papaya plantation of 2,374 farmers in Kopay, Tellipallai and Karaweddi Divisional Secretariat Divisions of the Jaffna District and the District Secretary/Government Agent, Jaffna has reported that the total loss of the damage was Rs.52.98 million. Accordingly, the Cabinet decided to implement a mechanism in coordination with the Ministry of Agriculture, the Ministry in charge of the subject of Disaster Management and the District Secretariat, Jaffna and to grant an additional allocation of Rs.52.98 million to the District Secretary/Government Agent, Jaffna, required for the same through the Ministry in charge of the subject of Disaster Management as per the proposal of the Minister of Fisheries to provide relief to the said farmers, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of Regulations issued under the Imports and Exports	(Control ) Act, No.01 of 1969 in Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-16
decision_details_body:
- The Cabinet granted approval at its meeting held on 2020‑04‑01 for the proposals made by H.E. The President pertaining to streamlining the imports and restoring the economic activities with a view to easing the pressure caused to the foreign exchange due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Accordingly, H.E. the President appointed the Tariff Determination Committee to submit recommendations on action to be taken pertaining to strengthening and reviving the national economy pursuant to the policy statement of “Vistas of Prosperity and Splendor” and as per the recommendations of the said Committee, the importing goods were classified into 03 categories to streamline the import as an interim measure and action was taken as follows:

*	temporary suspension of the importation of non-essential goods  and commodities that could be cultivated or manufactured domestically and motor vehicles.

*	allowing importation of selected commodities under the suppliers' credit facility or on no foreign exchange basis.

*	allowing importation of selected goods necessary for domestic industries, agriculture, export processing and domestic consumption.
      
	As such, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the	Minister of Finance to submit four (04) Gazette Extraordinary Notifications	publishing the Regulations promulgated under the Imports and Exports	(Control) Act, No.1 	of 1969 in Parliament for implementing the aforesaid	measures, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Declaring Monday as the ‘Public Day’ of the State Institutions.
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-09
decision_details_body: - 	Even though Wednesday has already been declared as the ‘Public Day’ for  the public to have their needs attended to through the State institutions, representations have been made that, it would be more convenient to the Public, if Monday is nominated as the ‘Public Day’.  Accordingly, the Cabinet of Ministers decided to declare Monday as the ‘Public Day’ hereafter and that  officials of all the State institutions to compulsorily remain in their offices to fulfil the requirements of the Public during that day.

description: Printing of school textbooks required for free distribution in the year 2021
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-09
decision_details_body: - In the year 2021, 400 types of school text books required for free distribution have to be printed and the proposal made by the Minister of Education for printing of 13,890,000 copies from 106 types of school text books at a sum of Rs.1,093.71 million from the State Printing Corporation, and 25,541,500 copies from another 294 types at a sum of Rs.2,059.01 million by printing presses of the private sector selected through the open competitive procurement procedure, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Accelerated programme to supply fertilizer without a shortage during 2020/21 Maha Season
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-09
decision_details_body:
- During the preceding period the constant changes to the fertilizer subsidy policy, unsettlement of payments to the respective companies which import fertilizer and release of low quality non‑standardized fertilizer to the market have resulted the farmers to face much hardships. Therefore, evading such situation, the following measures have been planned, to implement the mechanism properly to distribute fertilizer to the farmers from the Maha Season 2020/21.



*	To implement the programme to distribute fertilizer free of charge to the paddy farmers further in the same manner as it was implemented and to implement the programmes to popularize environmental friendly fertilizer among paddy farmers.

*	To expeditiously import 230,000 metric tons of fertilizer required by the farmers for the Maha Season 2020/21 through the State Fertilizer Companies .

*	To grant permission to import 300,000 metric tons of fertilizer required further to the fertilizer companies which agreed to import such fertilizer considering the fact that only 40,000 metric tons are available in the possession of the fertilizer companies to fulfill the fertilizer requirement of 332,000 metric tons required for the crops other than paddy during the Maha Season 2020/21.

*	To grant permission for the other qualified fertilizer companies as well, to import fertilizer for Maha Season 2020/21, subject to a maximum of 5,000 metric tons.

*	To provide an opportunity for any farmer to purchase a 50 kg bag of fertilizer required for the crops other than paddy, at a subsidized rate of Rs.1,500/- in the open market. 

As such, the joint proposal made to implement the above programme by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance and the Minister of Agriculture, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Repair and use or Disposal of the vehicles of the Government Institutions which are not in running condition

decision_details_body: - It has been observed that a considerable number of vehicles which are not using at present due to lack of proper maintenance are available in the Government  institutions whereas 4,116 vehicles have been identified for repair and use while the number of vehicles that can be discarded amounts to 5,588 as at 31st August 2020. description: Procurement, Construction and Commissioning of Three (03) Fuel Storage Tanks at Kolonnawa Installation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-02

Ltd to a sum of Rs.942.47 million (excluding VAT), as recommended by the Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Purchase of Coal for Puttalam Coal Power Plant under Spot Market

Ltd, to a sum of US$ 16.18 Million, as recommended by the Special Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The National Policy on Natural Gas in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-02
decision_details_body: - A decision was taken at the Cabinet Meeting held on the 12th of February 2020  to appoint a committee of Experts to examine the draft National Policy on Natural Gas in Sri Lanka and submit necessary amendments. Accordingly, the amended ‘National Policy on Natural Gas in Sri Lanka' prepared by the committee comprised of 17 experts appointed for the  purpose was submitted to the Cabinet by the Minister of Energy and the Cabinet decided to grant approval in principle for the same.

description: Allocation of land blocks from Regional Industrial Estates to set up industries
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-02
decision_details_body: - The Ministry of Industries implements the ‘Regional Industrial Estates Development Programme’ with the objective of promoting the industries at regional level. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Industries for the allocation of plots of lands for the inauguration of industries in the industrial zones of Ratmalana, Kalutara, Millewa, Nalanda, Ulapane, Makandura, Uva Paranagama and Batticaloa for 09 investors on a lease period of 35 years, considering to the recommendations submitted by the relevant Regional Industrial Services Committees, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining allocations from the General Treasury for the recurrent expenditure of the Sri Lanka Rupavahini Corporation, Sri Lanka Broadcasting Corporation (SLBC) and the Independent Television Network
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-02
decision_details_body:
- Due to the decrease of income generation with the spread of COVID-19, the Sri Lanka Rupavahini Corporation, Sri Lanka Broadcasting Corporation and Independent Television Network have faced with difficulty to settle the salaries  and other essential expenses of such institutions. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Mass Media to obtain the provisions for essential recurrent expenditure of those institutions for a period of 04 months from September to December 2020 from the General Treasury, was approved by the Cabinet.

	It was also decided by the Cabinet that strategic plans should be prepared to increase the revenue of these institutions and be implemented expeditiously with the concurrence of the General Treasury.

description: Appointment of an Expert Committee for the formulation of a National Trade	Policy
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-02
decision_details_body: - It has been observed that the National Trade Policy approved by the Cabinet of Ministers on 2017‑08‑01, has not been formulated properly in consultation with all relevant parties. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Trade to appoint an Expert Committee representing all relevant parties to formulate a new National Trade Policy in line with the present, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The 20th Amendment to the Constitution and drafting of a New Constitution
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-02
decision_details_body:
- As a short-term measure to address the anomalies and shortcomings caused by th 19th Amendment to the Constitution of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka made in the year 2015, the Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2020‑08‑19 decided to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare the draft of 20th Amendment to the Constitution. Accordingly, the Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman was presented to the Cabinet by the Minister of Justice. As such, the Cabinet, having taken into consideration the opinion of the Attorney General to the effect that the said Bill is not inconsistent with the 13th Amendment to the Constitution and that it could be passed by the vote of not less than 2/3 majority of Parliament in terms of Article 82 (5) of the Constitution, granted approval to publish the draft Bill in the Government Gazette and thereafter submit the same in Parliament for approval.
 
	Further, the Cabinet of Ministers also decided to appoint the following Committee of Experts to prepare a preliminary draft for a new Constitution taking into account the proposal made by the Minister of Justice as decided by the Cabinet at its meeting held on 2020.08.19.

decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-09-02
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2020‑05‑27, granted approval to implement  a housing project enabling to make available houses affordable for the middle income salary earners employed in the public and private sector. description: The Interim Report in relation to the total power failure in the National Power System on 17th August 2020
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-08-26
decision_details_body:
- The interim report of the Committee appointed by the Minister of Power to examine and report the total power failure which occurred in the national power system on 2020‑08‑17 was brought to the notice of the Cabinet. The Committee has identified the non‑availability of a risk management mechanism for operations and maintenance and further submitted 11 more recommendations including the urgency of having a more reliable operational and maintenance mechanism for risk prevention. Further, the Committee has reported that the cause for the total power interruption on 2020‑08‑17 was due to a mistake made by the officer‑in‑charge of the general maintenance at the Kerawalapitiya Grid Sub Station, at that time.

The Cabinet further noted the information submitted by the Minister of Power, that an in‑depth study is being conducted on the matters stated in the above committee report and expeditious action will be taken to make aware the Cabinet of Ministers of the activities recommended in such study and the estimated investment  required for the implementation of such activities.

description: Amendment of Tax Legislation - Policy Measures for Economic Revival
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-08-26
decision_details_body:
Followed by a proposal made by H.E the President, the approval of the Cabinet was granted at its meeting held on the 2019‑11‑27 for the introduction of a simple, transparent and efficient tax system to all the stakeholders in the economy including consumers, working population, entrepreneurs and tax paying community. Morefully, the Government has also taken  measures to provide fiscal and monetary stimulus to all the stakeholders in the economy including low - income earners, entrepreneurs, micro, small and medium entrepreneurs, those engaged in tourism and the farmers in order to minimize the adverse impacts caused to the production activities as well as to the employments due to the COVID - 19 pandemic. The Central Bank of Sri Lanka with the intention of easing the financial burden on the entrepreneurs has taken measures to increase the liquidity of the financial market.

It is expected that these measures will bring back the economy to normalcy in the second part of the year 2020. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Finance to publish the Bills drafted by the Legal Draftsman to amend the following Acts in compliance with the above, in the Government Gazette and thereafter present the same in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

i. 	Nation Building Tax Act, No.9 of 2009
ii. 	Economic Services Charge Act, No.13 of 2006
iii. 	Ports and Airports Development Levy Act, No.18 of 2011 
iv.  	Finance Act, No.35 of 2018

Further, the Cabinet approved the proposal made to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft legislation to amend the following Acts.

i.  Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017.
ii. Value Added Tax Act, No. 14 of 2002.

description: Procurement of a Data Management System for Reserve Management of the	Central Bank of Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-08-26
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet granted its approval on 2019‑06‑07 to procure a new data management system to meet the existing requirements in the management of the foreign reserves of the country and productively facilitate to the future developments as well. Accordingly, bids have been invited through the International Competitive Bidding process to supply, install, commission and maintain the said data management system. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Finance to award the above procurement to SimCorp Pte. Limited of Singapore as per the recommendation of the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee on the said bid, and the views and the recommendations of the Information and Communication Technology Agency of Sri Lanka (ICTA) pertaining to the proposed procurement, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of reports published by the Ministry of Finance to Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-08-26
decision_details_body:
- The following reports have been published by the Ministry of Finance and accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Finance to submit the said reports  to Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet. 

 i.	Pre-election Budgetary Position Report

In terms of the provisions of Section 16 (2) of the Fiscal Management (Responsibility) Act, No.3 of 2003, the Pre-election Budgetary Position Report is required to be tabled in Parliament by the Minister of Finance within 02 weeks of the first session of the new Parliament.
	ii.	Annual Report - 2019 of the Ministry of Finance

In terms of the provisions of Section 13 of the Fiscal Management (Responsibility) Act, No.3 of 2003, the Final Budgetary Position Report is required to be released to the public  by the Minister of Finance prior to lapse of 05 months after the end of the financial year and thereafter tabled in Parliament.

	iii.	Mid-Year Fiscal Position Report 2020

In terms of the provisions of Section 10 of the Fiscal Management (Responsibility) Act, No.3 of 2003, the Mid-Year Fiscal Position Report is required to be released to the public by the Minister of Finance  by the last day of June in each financial year and thereafter tabled in Parliament.

	iv.	 Annual Report - 2019 of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka

In terms of the provisions of Section 35 of the Monetary Law Act, the Monetary Board of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka should submit a report containing the state of the economy, condition of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka and the policies and measures adopted by the Monetary Board during the year to the Minister of Finance within 04 months of the commencement of the following year and thereafter the same should be submitted to Parliament.

description: Construction of Flyovers over the Railway Line at Uttharananda Mawatha near 	the Slave Island Railway Station
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-08-26
decision_details_body: - A huge traffic congestion has been observed during peak hours due to the location of  railway lines across Uttharananda Mawatha and Akbhar Mawatha at Slave Island area. Accordingly, a project has been proposed to implement a one-way traffic plan by constructing flyovers	to avoid the said traffic congestion.  As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Highways to implement the said 	project and invite bids from qualified domestic contractors for the construction of 03 flyovers under the same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Appointment of the Cabinet Sub-Committee on Cost of Living
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-08-26
decision_details_body:
- The proposal made by H.E the President to appoint  the Cabinet Sub-Committee on Cost of Living under the chairmanship of H.E the President and comprising of the Hon. Prime Minister, Minister of Trade, Minister of Agriculture, Minister of Fisheries and Minister of Plantation, in order to maintain the stability of Cost of Living by taking into account the issues such as constant fluctuations in the market 	demand and supply, climate effects, seasonal changes in production and international prices, was approved by the Cabinet. 
	
	Further, the Cabinet granted its approval for the following State Ministers to be 	attended to the deliberations of the above Cabinet Sub-Committee.

*	State Minister of Paddy and Grains, Organic Food, Vegetables, Fruits, Chillies, Onion and Potato Cultivation Promotion, Seed Production and Advanced Technology Agriculture. 

*	State Minister of Co-operative Services, Marketing Development and Consumer Protection.

*	State Minister of Coconut, Kithul, Palmyrah and Rubber Cultivation Promotion and Related Industrial Product Manufacturing & Export Diversification.

description: Upgrading the General Hospital, Kalutara and the Base Hospital, Homagama as Teaching Hospitals
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-07-22
decision_details_body: - Presently, plans are being made for the establishment of a Medical Faculty of the University of Moratuwa and it is expected to commence the academic activities expeditiously. The proposal submitted by the Minister of Health and Indigenous Medical Services to upgrade the General Hospital, Kalutara and the Base Hospital, Homagama as Teaching Hospitals enabling the establishment of the Professorial Unit of proposed Medical Faculty at General Hospital, Kalutara and the relevant clinical training at the Base Hospital, Homagama, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Regularizing and make efficient the State Bank system to Strengthen the National Economy
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-07-22
decision_details_body: - State banking system and their affiliated institutions have to operate regularly and effectively in order to overcome the challenges encountered by the Sri Lankan economy amidst COVID-19 pandemic. However, it appears that actions have been taken deviating from the fundamental objectives of establishing said state banks and violating the provisions and procedures stipulated in relevant Acts during the past. The Cabinet granted approval to the proposal submitted by the Hon. Prime Minister for the appointment of a Committee chaired by the former High Court Judge Sisira Ratnayake and comprised of experts in the relevant fields to identify such incidents and to recommend the legal and administrative measures in order to avoid such situations in future.

description: Appointment of a Committee for the preparation of a strategic mechanism for implementing a Common Watershed Management Approach in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-07-22
decision_details_body: - The proposal submitted by Hon. Prime Minister for the appointment of a committee comprised of experts in the field of water management headed by Prof. C. M. Madduma Bandara, Environmentalist for the preparation of a proposal on making strategies enabling to build up cooperation among all the relevant stakeholders with the view to increasing the available water quantity with better quality for present and future purposes by reviewing all the relevant policies on effective management of watersheds in Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement of Chemical Fertilizer - Maha season 2020 - (September Supply)

description: Procurement of Reinsurance cover on Strike, Riot, Civil Commotion and Terrorism Fund for the year 2020/2021
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-07-22
decision_details_body: - The National Insurance Trust Fund provides an insurance cover for the strike, Riot, Civil Commotion and Terrorism Fund for the General Insurance Companies in Sri Lanka. A reinsurance cover is obtained by the National Insurance Trust Fund from the reputed reinsurers/reinsurance brokers once again for the said insurance cover. (Lead Reinsurer - M/s Chaucer Syndicate 1084) at a total cost of Rs.116.39 million for a period of 18 months from the date of awarding of the relevant contract, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement of Retrocession cover on 30% Compulsory Reinsurance Cession on the Reinsurance programme of the General Insurance Industry of Sri Lanka for the year 2020/2021
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-07-22
decision_details_body: - The National Insurance Trust Fund provides a 30% Compulsory Reinsurance Cession for the General Insurance Industry of Sri Lanka. Further, the National Insurance Trust Fund obtains a retrocession from reputed reinsurers /reinsurance brokers for the purpose. Accordingly, the international competitive bids have been invited for obtaining the reinsurance cession for the year 2020 / 2021 and the proposal submitted by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Economy and Policy Development for awarding the reinsurance coverage to M/s J. B. Boda & Co. (S) Pte. Ltd. (Lead Reinsurer - M/s Everest Reinsurance Company) at a total cost of Rs.985.5 million for a period of 18 months from the date of awarding of the relevant contract, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Winding up of the functions of the Interim Board set up until the Southern Development Bill is passed
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-07-22
decision_details_body: - At the Cabinet meeting held on 30th March 2016, approval had been granted to appoint an Interim Board comprising of a Chairman and 09 members and recruit the required staff for that Board, until the Southern Development Board is legally constituted by an Act of Parliament. However, the Southern Province Development Board bill has not been tabled in Parliament up to date. Some of the projects implemented by the Interim Board have already been completed while all other remaining projects are scheduled to be completed by the year 2020. Therefore, the Cabinet of Ministers approved the proposal made by the Minister of Industrial Export and Investment Promotion for winding up the functions of the Interim Board set up until the Southern Province Development Board Bill is passed and for obtaining the required allocations for the completion of work of the projects to be completed.

description: Extension of the validity period of the Treasury Guarantee issued for the establishment of Letters of Credit to import coal for the Coal Power Plant at Norochcholai
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-07-22
decision_details_body: - The validity period of the Treasury Guarantee issued to the People’s Bank by the General Treasury with regard to the import of coal by the Lanka Coal Company to the value of Rs.11 billion, is to expire on the 2020‑08‑31. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Power & Energy to extend of the date of validity of the said Treasury Guarantee by another one year effective from that date, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Issuing Free Grants for lands of re located houses in the implementation of the Upper Kothmale Hydro Power Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-07-22
decision_details_body: - The Upper Kothmale Hydro Power Project which was inaugurated in 2006, completed its construction works in 2012. By the August 2014, houses for displaced families due to the implementation of the hydro power project and alternative locations for shops and workshops have been constructed and handed over to the beneficiaries and the activities relating to the payment of the compensation too has been completed. However, the right to the lands of the relocated families has not been granted so far.
