description: Completion of the Construction of the City Traffic Building for the Sri Lanka Police
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body: - The construction work of the 11 storied city traffic building for the Sri Lanka Police at Mihindu Mawatha in Colombo 12 has been commenced and construction works of 3 storeys had been completed under its first contract.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Sajith Premadasa, the Minister of Housing and Construction, to award the contract for the completion of the balance construction work to M/s. CML-MTD Construction Ltd., for a sum of Rs.388.5 million, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of the Nadukuda Grid Substation and augmentation of the 	Mannar Grid Substation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Ranjith Siyambalapitiya, the Minister of Power and Renewable Energy, to award the contract for the construction of the Nadukuda Grid Substation and augmentation of the Mannar Grid Substation under the Green Power Development and Energy Efficiency Improvement Investment Programme for strengthening the transmission network of the Ceylon Electricity Board, to M/s. Seimens Ltd., India, for a sum of Rs.2,697.96 million, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of four (04) Grid Substations under the Renewable Energy Absorption Transmission Development Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body: - Four (04) Grid Substations and the related transmission lines have been planned to be installed in the areas of Nawalapitiya, Ragala, Wewalwatta and Maliboda to provide interconnections to electricity generated in mini hydro power plants to be amalgamated into the main network in the future. The proposal made by Hon. Ranjith Siyambalapitiya, the Minister of Power and Renewable Energy, to award the contract for design, civil works, installation of the relevant equipment and commissioning, to M/s. Ceylex Engineering (Pvt) Ltd., for a sum of Rs.1,233 million, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of the Renal Care Treatment unit at the General Hospital, Trincomalee
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body:
- The District of Trincomalee too has been identified as a District in which the Chronic Kidney Diseases unknown aetiology (CKDu) is widely spread. Hence, the Government is pursing action to construct a Renal Care Unit at the General Hospital, Trincomalee with dialysis, wards, clinic and laboratory facilities for the purpose of identifying this Chronic Kidney Disease at the early stage and preventing the deaths occurring due to same. 

The proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine, to award the contract for the construction of the Renal Care Unit to M/s. Electro Metal Pressings (Pvt) Ltd., at the cost of Rs.249.32 million, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of a building complex for the Stroke Unit at the District 	General Hospital, Polonnaruwa
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body:
- Stroke is a leading cause for adult disability and it is the forth major cause of deaths in the hospital system. Although stroke can be cured with proper treatment and rehabilitation facilities, apart from the Rehabilitation Hospital at Ragama, no other hospital in the Island is equipped with an advanced Stroke Unit with proper facilities.   

As such, the government is in the process of constructing a building complex for the development of the stroke unit of the District General Hospital, Polonnaruwa also inclusive of the Neurology, Rheumatology, Physiotherapy and Rehabilitation Units with the objective of improving the treatment facilities necessary for the stroke patients. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine, to award the contract for the construction of the said building complex to M/s. Link Engineering (Pvt) Ltd. for a sum of Rs.348 million, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of the Cardiothoracic Complex (Phase II) at the Lady Ridgeway Hospital
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body:
- The government is in the process of further developing the health care services provided by the Lady Ridgeway Hospital (LRH) which is the main tertiary care institution in Sri Lanka for pediatric treatment.  Therefore, it has been planned to commence the construction work of the Cardiothoracic Complex (Phase II) for providing advanced qualitative Cardiothoracic treatment and for the improvement of  facilities for medical research.  

Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine, to award the contract for the construction of the said treatment unit to M/s. Electro Metal Pressings (Pvt) Ltd. for a sum of Rs.159.94 million, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of the Renal Care Unit at the General Hospital, Hambantota
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body:
- The District of Hambantota has been identified as a District in which the Chronic Kidney Diseases unknown aetiology (CKDu) is widely spread. Hence, the Government is pursing action to construct a Renal Care Unit at the General Hospital, Hambantota with dialysis, wards, clinic and laboratory facilities for the purpose of identifying this Chronic Kidney Disease at the early stage and preventing the deaths occurring due to same. 

The proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine, to award the contract for the construction of the Renal Care Unit to M/s. RN Constructions (Pvt) Ltd., at the cost of Rs.210 million, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of a Research Unit for the Sri Lanka Anti-Doping Agency
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body:
- The Sri Lanka Anti-Doping Agency has been established under the provisions of the Convention Against Doping in Sports Act, No.33 of 2013 with the objective of preventing the use of prohibited substances, conducting research in that regard and co‑operating with other international organizations operating against prohibited substances.   

Presently, a building is being constructed for this agency in the premises of the Sugathadasa Sports Stadium. The proposal made by Hon. Dayasiri Jayasekara, the Minister of Sports, to construct a laboratory research unit within the premises of the building being constructed for the Sri Lanka Anti-Doping Agency with the objective of minimizing the risk of Sri Lankan Sports men and women being subject to the allegations of using prohibited substances and to provide the equipment needed for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development of Infrastructure Facilities in Sports
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body:
- The objective of the government is to improve the sports skills of the youth and take them to international level, by paving the way for sports to the village. The government is pursuing action to construct 'Provincial Sports Complexes' to cover all provinces in the country and to construct 'District Sports Complexes' covering the rest of the 16 districts except in the districts where the Provincial Sports Complexes will be established and most of its construction work has already been completed. Moreover, these Provincial Sports Complexes should consist of hostel facilities and the sports men and women residing in the areas away from those Provincial and District Sports Complexes, should be provided with sports infrastructure facilities. 

Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Dayasiri Jayasekara, the Minister of Sports, to construct 08 hostels with accommodation for 100 sports men and women at a time, close to the 08 Provincial Sports Complexes located in Polonnaruwa, Kilinochchi, Kurunegala, Badulla, Digana, Ratnapura, Matara and Trincomalee at the estimated cost of Rs.1,087 million and to construct fully fledged 06 indoor stadiums in the 06 identified areas located away from the Provincial and District Sports Complexes at the estimated cost of Rs.1,050 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Hosting of International Conferences relevant to the field of Agriculture
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body:
- The Ministry of Agriculture has organized to host two International Conferences in Sri Lanka in collaboration with the Asian Productive Organization (APO), African‑Asian Rural Development Organization (AARDO) and the Centre for Integrated Rural Development for Asia and Pacific (CIRDAP) of which Sri Lanka is a Member. 

With a view to reviewing policy programmes and plans required for Disaster Risk Management and Climate Change Adaptation and developing sustainable development strategies suitable to face Disaster Risk Management in Agriculture and Climate Change Adaptation, the proposal made by Hon. Duminda Dissanayake, the Minister of Agriculture, to conduct a workshop under the theme of 'Disaster Risk Management in Agriculture and Climate Change Adaptation', from 11th to 15th of September 2017 and another International Conference with the objective of gaining knowledge on the safety of major food items found in the global market, new development methods and identifying advanced food safety standards on Strengthening of Food Safety Standards from 31st October to 02nd November in 2017, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The Government Policy on the usage of Liquid Natural Gas (LNG) for  Electricity Generation and the Construction of required infrastructure for the purpose
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body:
- The Cabinet appointed a Cabinet Sub‑Committee on 18.07.2017 under the Chairmanship of Hon. (Dr.) Sarath Amunugama, the Minister of Special Assignments, to determine the government policy relevant to the infrastructure facilities required for the usage of LNG for Electricity Generation and the Construction of required infrastructure focusing attention on ensuring the energy security of Sri Lanka, diversification of fuel options used for electricity sector and the minimizing of electricity generation cost.  

The Cabinet granted approval to implement the recommendations made by the said Sub‑Committee to accept as a matter of policy for the usage of natural gas as a fuel for generating electricity in Sri Lanka by the year 2019 and to operate the Natural Gas Electricity Plants with the capacity of about 1000MW, and to improve expeditiously the infrastructure facilities for unloading and re‑transforming  of LNG.

description: Implementation of a Middle Income Housing Development Project at Ragama for Government Employees
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body: - The objective of the Middle Income Housing Development Project implemented by the government is to construct 500,000 houses required by the Middle Income Groups within the next 05 year period.  It has been identified that the majority of the middle income employees belong to the Government and the Semi‑government Sector. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Patali Champika Ranawaka, the Minister of Megapolis and Western Development, to implement a housing project with 400 housing units by developing a 03 acre land situated in the Ragama area belonging to the Land Reclamation and Development Corporation, with the objective of providing affordable houses to the employees of the Government and the Semi‑government Sector under the above project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Improvement of road infrastructure in the Homagama Region (Tech City)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29

description: 70th Independence Day Celebrations
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Vajira Abeywardena, the Minister of Home Affairs, to appoint a Ministerial Sub Committee under the Chairmanship of Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe, the Prime Minister, to organize and monitor the necessary activities of the 70th Independence Day Celebrations falling on the 04th of February 2018, and the cultural event to coincide with the celebrations, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development of selected hospitals in the Northern Province
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body: - A project to develop selected hospitals in the Northern Province has been proposed with the objective of providing qualitative health service to the people in the Northern Province and to further upgrade the health infrastructure facilities in the resettled areas. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine, to develop the District General Hospitals of Killinochchi, Mannar and Vavuniya and the Base Hospitals of Point-Pedro and Mankulam, with the financial assistance of the Government of Netherlands and the financial provision from the Consolidated Fund, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: International Symposium on Traditional and Complementary Medicine, Educational Exhibition and Trade Fair (TradMed International)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body: - Expert attention has been focused to develop the evidence based practices of traditional medical system in diagnosis, management and prevention utilizing modern science and technology, diagnostic tools, Bio‑medical information system and improvement of products with quality and standard. The proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine, to host an International Symposium and an Educational Exhibition and a Trade Fair during 23rd to 25th November 2017, named TradMed International 2017 - Sri Lanka,  in Colombo, Sri Lanka, with the objective of sharing the expertise and noval trends, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Promotion of Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics in Sri Lanka (STEM Education)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body:
- It is absolutely important to have a labour force skilled in Science,Technology, Engineering and Mathematics to make Sri Lanka a country with a high income receiving economy, through a knowledge based economy driven by innovation.  There seems to be an international trend also for job markets in the fields of computer, mathematics, architecture, engineering, product design, robotics and other emerging technologies such as Nano‑Technology, biotechnology and the knowledge obtained through the STEM education would be beneficial in obtaining a highly paid job. Several developed countries in the globe are taking action to promote STEM education as a measure to improve the industrial sector in their countries. 

Accordingly, taking into consideration a proposal made by Hon. Susil Premajayantha, the Minister of Science, Technology and Research, the Cabinet decided to appoint a Cabinet Sub‑Committee comprising of the Ministers of Education, Higher Education, Skills Development and Vocational Training,  Science, Technology and Research, to design a strategic action plan in order to promote Science,Technology, Engineering and Mathematics in Sri Lanka and to introduce other similar fields which give rise to innovation to the education system.

description: Improvements to the Bandarawela, Water Supply Scheme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body:
- More than 2000 families in the Bandarawela and Ella Divisional Secretariat Divisions have been affected due to the water level in their wells being low as a result of the water ingress during the tunneling construction of the Uma Oya Multipurpose Development Scheme. With the result, the demand for pipe water connections by the families who used their own wells have increased and along with that, the capacity of the Bandarawela Water Supply Scheme has to be enhanced.
 
Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Rauff Hakeem, the Minister of City Planning and Water Supply, to implement a project to increase the water capacity of the Bandarawela Water Supply Scheme by additional 2,000 cubic meters per day enabling to make 1,000 new connections including the affected areas of Egodagama, Weheragalathanna, Udaperuwa, Kinigama and Heeloya, at an estimated cost of Rs.225 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Revision and re-declaration of the boundaries of Wedithalathivu nature reserve
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body:
- Wedithalathivu nature reserve with an extent of 29,180 hectares, declared as a nature reserve under the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No. 1956/13 of 2016‑03‑01 is a natural reserve found in the wet lands of Sri Lanka with a vital mangrove Eco‑system. The project to establish ''an aquaculture industrial zone'' in Manthai-West Divisional Secretariat Division in the Mannar District is immensely important out of the different projects that have been designed by the Government, with a view to increasing the export income of fish products up to  US$ 1.3 billion by 2020. The land in extent of 1,491 hectares identified to establish the said aquaculture industrial zone, being included in the said Wedithalathivu nature reserve has proved to be a hindrance to the implementation of the project.  

Accordingly, the joint proposal made by Hon. Gamini Jayawickrema Perera, the Minister of Sustainable Development and Wildlife and Hon. Mahinda Amaraweera, the Minister of  Fisheries and Aquatic Resources Development, to conduct a proper environmental impact assessment and subject to the results of same and in accordance with the provisions of the Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance to exclude the plot of land identified as suitable to establish the proposed Aquaculture Industrial Zone from the Wedithalathivu Nature Reserve and re-declare the boundaries of the said Reserve, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining 100 Ambulances for the Government Hospitals under the Austrian soft loan scheme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body: - In establishing a qualitative health care service, it is important to provide a safe and efficient mode of transport of patients to the nearest hospital with the required health facilities. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe, the Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs, to launch a project to provide 100 ambulances  with essential life saving equipment, to the selected Government hospitals and to enter into a Loan Agreement with the Raiffeisen Bank of Austria to obtain a soft loan amounting to Euro 9.8 million for the project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Filling of the Teacher vacancies in schools in the Northern Province
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body: - As a result of the conflicts that prevailed over 30 years, a severe shortage of teachers exists in the Northern Province and the dearth of teachers of Sinhala medium has become a major issue. As a remedial measure, the proposal made by Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe, the Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs, to absorb the teachers who have fulfilled the basic qualifications in terms of the Teachers' Service Minute, from among the teachers recruited on contract basis and serving in the Sinhala medium schools in the Northern Province during the difficult time of conflict, to the permanent Teachers' Service, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Study on Longshore Sediment Transport (LST) on the Southern, Western and Eastern coast of Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body:
- The South and West coastal zone of about 370km from Colombo to Hambantota in Sri Lanka is a significantly important Economic Zone that generates 75% of the total income receivable from the tourism industry and 50% of the income receivable from the fisheries industry. The coastal zone exposed to the South West monsoon has been subject to sudden erosion and long term depreciation of shoreline due to adverse climate changes. Besides this, the rapidly developing Eastern coast of Sri Lanka along with the growing tourism industry is susceptible to disastrous situations such as tornadoes, storms and long term coastal erosion.

	The sea erosion caused to the coastal lines has created serious economic, social and environmental issues. Further, with the probability of the risk of increasing the sea level and the speedy sea erosion occurring due to the frequency and intensity of other natural disasters, the coastal community and the development activities carried out in the coastal zone will undoubtedly face severe threats. Therefore, the proposal made by H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to carry out a study on Long shore Sediment Transport - LST which has been the main cause of sea erosion, for the purpose of formulating strategies for the effective management of the Eastern, Western and Southern coastal lines of Sri Lanka, and to obtain necessary funds was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Providing facilities to carry out the field work of the Forest Department and the Department of Wildlife Conservation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body:
- The Ecosystem Conservation and Management Project (ESCAMP) has been implemented with a view to improving various sensitive eco systems in selected locations for conservation and providing the benefits to the communities living in close proximity to the areas through sustainable management of such eco systems. Under this project, Sinharaja, Nuckles, Kanneliya and Hurulu Reserves and the National Parks of Yala, Lunugamwehera, Bundala, Udawalawa and Galoya will be subject to conservation with also the participation of the people living around them.  

Accordingly, the proposal made by H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to purchase vehicles required for the field work of the Forest Department, Department of Wildlife Conservation and the Sustainable Development Secretariat with a view to enhancing the institutional capacities of those institutions for the successful implementation of the project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Providing relief to the householders adversely affected due to the Uma Oya Multi-Purpose Development Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-29
decision_details_body:
- Cabinet granted approval to take the following action with the objective of providing further relief to the householders adversely affected, as recommended by the Cabinet Committee appointed to examine and provide relief to the persons affected due to the leakage of the main tunnel of the Uma Oya Multi-Purpose Development Project, 

*	to pay a monthly rental of Rs.10,000/- to Rs.25,000/-, as recommended by the Government Valuer, subject to a maximum period of 06 months, to the families who have been evacuated  from their residences affected, until resettlement in alternative lands.

*	to provide of dry rations as provided presently, to the affected families for a further period of 06 months.

description: Implementation of the decision taken for the prohibition of the importation, production and usage of polythene, with effect from 01st September 2017
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet decided to implement the decision taken at its meeting held on 2017-07-11 to prohibit the importation, production and usage of certain types of polythene with effect from 01st September 2017 without any change and to appoint a Committee comprising of officials representing the relevant institutions to pursue action to gradually encourage the polythene producers, persons engaged in polythene associated packaging industries and wholesale traders of polythene who will be affected by the prohibition, towards other options.

description: Providing relief to the people affected by the prevailing dry weather and safeguarding their livelihood
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body:
- The Note presented to the Cabinet by H.E. the President to the effect that the following measures have been taken to provide relief to the people affected by the prevailing dry weather and emphasizing the fact that such relief measures should be implemented uninterruptedly during the forthcoming 02 months as well, was noted by the Cabinet. 

*	providing of potable water for 240,338 families residing in 117 Divisional Secretariat Divisions in 20 affected Districts.

*	providing of a dry ration worth of Rs.5,000/- per month as drought relief.

*	implementation of a programme for providing water for wildlife. 

*	issuing of an advance through the District Secretaries to the Cooperative Societies faced with financial difficulties.

description: Construction of the memorial of the Most. Venerable Maduluwawe Sobitha Thero
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, to construct a memorial in memory of the Most. Venerable Maduluwawe Sobitha Thero for the magnificent role played by the prelate in stabilizing true democracy, religious harmony and national reconciliation based on the principles of Good Governance, and to provide the financial contribution needed for the purpose by the Government, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Re-laying of the synthetic running track of the Sugathadasa National Sports Complex
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Dayasiri Jayasekara, the Minister of Sports, to award the contract for the re‑laying of the 400 meter Class 1 synthetic running track and the 200 meter synthetic running track of the Sugathadasa National Sports Complex to Access - Conica JV for a sum of Rs.269.33 million, as recommended by the Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (CAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Providing a Group Health Insurance Scheme for school children
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body:
- An allocation of Rs.2,700 million has been made by the Budget 2017 for the implementation of a programme to provide an Insurance Coverage worth of Rs.200,000/- for each school child, free of charge, for all the school children in the country counting 4.5 million within the age group between 05 to 19 years. The proposed Insurance Coverage will provide Rs.10,000/- for outpatient services and Rs.100,000/- for hospitalization. In addition, this Insurance Coverage will make a payment of Rs.100,000/- to the parents for the sudden death of a school child and Rs.75,000/- to the school child for the sudden death of either the mother or the father of the student. Further, a Rs.100,000/- for the permanent total disability of a school child and a Rs.50,000/- to Rs.100,000/- for the partial disability could be obtained as  compensation under this scheme.   

	Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Akila Viraj Kariyawasam, the Minister of Education, to implement this Insurance Scheme by the Sri Lanka Insurance Corporation, subject to an annual installment of Rs.2,348 million, as recommended by the Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (CAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Operation of Core Category Duty Free Concessions at the Terminal 01 of the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA), Katunayake
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala de Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, to award the contract of Core Category Duty Free Concession Space 2 in the arrival and departure restricted areas of Terminal 01 of the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA), Katunayake, for a period of the proceeding 05 years to M/s. Dufry AG of Switzerland, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Installation of a Roof Mounted Solar Power System in the Navy General Hospital,  Welisara (Colombo)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body: - The major hospital belonging to the Sri Lanka Navy is the hospital at the Welisara Naval Complex which comprises of 200 beds. As such, the proposal made by H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Defence, to install a 450 Kw Grid Tie Roof Mounted Solar Power System  linked to the National Electricity Transmission Network, with a view to  mitigating the high cost spent for the electricity in maintaining this hospital, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Release of lands for resettlement at Keppapilavu in the Mullaitivu District
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body: - The Government has given priority for the resettlement of the people in their own villages, who were displaced due to the conflict situation which prevailed in the Northern and Eastern provinces. The Security Forces assist in the matter  by establishing their Camps in other locations, which had been located previously in the lands possessed by the civilians.  Hence, 432 acres of private lands situated in the Keppapilavu village in the Mullaitivu District in the possession of the Security Forces have already been released by now and the Army Commander has agreed to release a further 111 acres of private lands for the resettlement of displaced persons.  Accordingly, in order to release the occupied extent of lands, the proposal made by Hon. D.M. Swaminathan, the Minister of Prison Reforms, Rehabilitation, Resettlement and Hindu Religious Affairs, to secure the funds required for the establishment of the Army Camps in other locations which had been previously situated in those lands, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Payment of compensation to the families of those who died and the injured persons due to the unfortunate incident which occurred in  Beruwala and Aluthgama on 2014-06-15 and  2014-06-16
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body: - As a result of the unfortunate incident which occurred in the areas of Beruwala and Aluthgama on 2014‑06‑15 and  2014‑06‑16, three (03) persons died and 12 persons were injured. Taking into consideration the humanitarian aspects  related to the victims of the incident, the proposal made by Hon. D.M. Swaminathan, the Minister of Prison Reforms, Rehabilitation, Resettlement and Hindu Religious Affairs, to pay compensation of Rs.02 million each to the family of each person who died and to pay compensation up to the maximum of Rs.500,000/- to each person injured, due to the incident, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Commemoration of the 70th Anniversary of the Parliament of Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body:
- The Parliamentary system which has commenced on 14th October 1947 in this country, completes 70  years and as such arrangements have been made to conduct a Summit of Speakers of Parliament of all the countries of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) and to ceremonially open the new session of Parliament of Sri Lanka to commemorate “70 years of Parliamentary Democracy of Sri Lanka”.  

	Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Gayantha Karunathilaka, the Minister of Lands and Parliamentary Reforms, to secure a sum of Rs.03 million required for the compilation of a trilingual souvenir in Sinhala, Tamil and English with historical information, data and photographs related to the Parliament from 1947 up to the present day to coincide with the commemoration, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Court Automation Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body: - The core issue existing within the judicial sector in Sri Lnka is the delay in the dispensing of cases. Measures are being taken by the Government to provide a solution to the issue under four pronged strategies namely, law reforms, judicial infrastructure development, court automation and capacity building. Of these, under the 'Court Automation' File Management System, it is expected to establish digital facilities in Courts for filing of cases and the efficient management of case files for which Rs.500 million has been allocated in the budget estimate of 2016. Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Wijayadasa Rajapaksa, the Minister of Justice, to call for proposals from the institutions which possess technical and financial capacity, with a view to expediting the project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Renovating the Ran Viyana of the Sri Dalada Maligawa
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body: - The Ran Viyana which was an offering made by the former President R. Premadasa in the year 1987 with due respect to the Sri Dalada Maligawa was renovated with gold plating in the year 2002 and it has now become discoloured  needing further renovation. Accordingly, taking into consideration a joint proposal made by Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe, the Prime Minister and Hon. (Dr.) Wijayadasa Rajapaksa, the Minister of Buddhasasana, to renovate the Ran Viyana at an estimated cost of Rs 44.89 million utilizing the budgetary provision set apart under the Expenditure Head of H.E. the President for the year 2017, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of houses for 600 families below the poverty line under the financial aid of the Government of India
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body:
- The survey carried out on housing requirements in the year 2016 has revealed  that 216,197 families do not have either a house or a land to build a house of their own. A programme for providing housing facilities for these families are now being successfully implemented by the Government. Under this programme, the Government of India has agreed to grant financial aid for the construction of houses for 600 families below the poverty line.

Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Sajith Premadasa, the Minister of Housing and Construction, to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to obtain a sum of Rs 300 million granted by the Government of India and to implement a project for the construction of 600 houses targeting the families below the poverty line covering the 25 Districts of Sri Lanka under the  'Semata Sevana Grama Shakthi Model Village Project', was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Relocation of the Buildings situated insecurely in the Wellawatta Canal Reservation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body: - During the field inspection carried out in the area, after the collapse of an unauthorized building constructed within the Wellawatta Canal Reservation,  it was observed that the Sri Sugatha Viharaya as well as a Children's Orphanage attached thereto has been constructed insecurely in close proximity to the canal reservation.  As such, the proposal made by Hon. Patali Champika Ranawaka, the Minister of Megapolis and Western Development, to vest a portion of land belonging to the Sri Lanka Land Reclamation & Development Corporation (SLLR&DC) situated in the Attidiya area in Dehiwala, with the Viharaya, to re‑construct the Sri Sugatha Viharaya and the Children's Orphanage, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Allocation of a land located within the 'Ape Gama Premises' in Battaramulla for the construction of 'Amaradewa Asapuwa'
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body: - Considering the incomparable contribution made to the Sri Lankan musical field by Pandith W.D. Amaradewa, the renowned Artist, it has been proposed to establish the  'Amaradewa Asapuwa' to conserve his musical creations and the musical tradition for the benefit of the future generation.  As such, the proposal made by Hon. Patali Champika Ranawaka, the Minister of Megapolis and Western Development, to allocate a land in extent of 100 perches situated within the 'Ape Gama Premises' in Battaramulla to construct the 'Amaradewa Asapuwa', was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Planning for a cherished little baby - Awareness Programme for Sub-fertility
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body:
- According to the information available with the Ministry of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine, it is found that more than 15% of the couples suffer from sub‑fertility and at times this situation turns out to be a psychological and a life crisis. Although, Sri Lanka has achieved the maternal and child care health service indexes close to the level of the developed countries, it is observed that the focus made on the management of sub‑fertility is not quite adequate. 

Therefore, the facilities such as psychological counseling for couples suffering from sub‑fertility, proper guidance and early referral at times of need have to be established within the Government health care services.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine, to commemorate the National Family Planning Day which falls on the 26th of September under the theme of planning for a cherished little baby, focusing attention of the general public as well as the health care workers on the problem of sub‑fertility, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Revision of charges for the parcel transport by the Department of Railways
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body: - The charges for the transport of parcels by the Department of Railways has not been subject to revision during the past 09 year period and the charges for same by the Department are quite low when compared with the charges made by other parties for the transport of parcels.  As such, the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala de Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, to increase the present charges for the transport of parcels by 50%, other than the charges for the parcels for non‑commercial and consumption purposes, with the objective of enhancing the revenue earned by the Department of Railways by parcel transport, without causing an extra burden to the general public,  was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Reformulate the bus fare policy of passenger transportation to be compatible with the present
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body: - The policy which is adopted presently for the revision of the annual bus fare is  one which was prepared in the year 2002 and therefore, the need for the formulation of a new policy for the purpose has now emerged to suit the present day social and economic trends with the inclusion of new criteria as well.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala de Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, to appoint an Expert Panel comprising of the officers of the relevant institutions for the formulation of a new policy to be used for the revision of bus fares after discussions with the Bus Owners Associations and the Bus Travellers Associations, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Upgrading the qualitative aspect of service of the passenger transportation in three-wheelers and student transportation in school vans
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body:
- According to the Reports of the Department of Motor Traffic, as reported, the number of three‑wheelers registered in the country by the end of the year 2016 is over 11 lakhs and the number of school vans used for the student transportation is over 30,000. Taking into consideration the need to upgrade the qualitative aspect of the service of the passenger transportation in three‑wheelers and student transportation in school vans which presently is carried out in a disorderly manner and without a proper regulatory system, the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala de Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, to adopt the following measures in accordance with the recommendations of the Officials' Committee appointed to make recommendations for a methodology to be adopted in this regard, was approved by the Cabinet. 

*	action to be taken considering this matter as a subject matter within the purview of the Provincial Council in terms of the provisions of the Constitution.

*	establishment of a National Technical Committee to provide the necessary technical support for the preparation of  instructions and a set of rules and regulations inclusive of the minimum standards required for upgrading of the qualitative aspect of the service of the two transport services.

*	adoption of a system to encourage the use of taxi service for safe transportation discouraging the three‑wheeler service considered as a mode of transport lacking in safety, as the long term policy of the Government in regard to public transport.

description: Proper procedure for registration of Subscriber Identification Module (SIM) cards
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body: - It has been observed that when purchasing SIM cards,  a large number of active connections without the proper documentation containing the correct information of the owner of the SIM card are presently in the network of the companies which provide cellular mobile phones. It is essential to register the mobile phone subscribers with information required to ensure the identity of the legitimate subscriber, in order to control the various crimes and fraudulent acts committed with the use of mobile phones, in the interest of the national security and public order. The Telecommunication Regulatory Commission of Sri Lanka (TRCSL) has already made a request from the cellular mobile companies which supply mobile phones to adopt the procedure of registering SIM cards after obtaining a duly completed application form and a copy of the National Identity card including the other necessary documents of the person using the SIM card. As such, the proposal made by H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, for the  Minister in‑charge of the subject to issue an Order under the Sri Lanka Telecommunication Act, No.25 of 1991 to implement the registration procedure in a proper manner and to authorize the TRCSL to implement same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The Fourth Asian Electoral Stakeholders Forum - 2018
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-22
decision_details_body:
- 'The Asian Network for Free Elections' (ANFREL) is a Non‑Governmental Organization engaged in the implementation of appropriate programmes and projects to identify and remedy the common election related issues in countries of the Asian Region and to ensure the establishment of the rule of law in such countries. The Election Commission of Sri Lanka has agreed to co‑host the 'Fourth Asian Electoral Stakeholders Forum' in Sri Lanka in 2018, which is organized by the above Network.  

The Forum being held in Sri Lanka will provide an opportunity for the public officers and other stakeholders who directly or indirectly involve in the electoral process to enhance their knowledge and skills and also by sharing the experiences of the other countries in the Asian Region to enhance the competencies in the electoral process of Sri Lanka linked with the institutional capacity building to conduct the electoral process efficiently and productively.  Accordingly, the proposal made by H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, to host the Fourth Asian Electoral Stakeholders Forum in Sri Lanka in 2018 and to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding between the Election Commission of Sri Lanka and the Asian Network for Free Elections for co-hosting same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Granting  a house rent allowance of Rs.50,000/- each for the house owners who were displaced  due to the collapsing of the solid waste disposal site at Meethotamulla
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-15
decision_details_body: •- Due to the collapsing of the solid waste disposal site at Meethotamulla in Kolonnawa on 2017-04-14, the families who were deprived of their dwelling houses and the dwelling houses of those faced with a grave threat were evacuated from their residences and by now, 91 families out of them have been provided with alternative houses. A further number of 60 families have opted to get the alternative houses offered. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Anura Priyadharshana Yapa, the Minister of Disaster Management to pay the house rent allowance of Rs.50,000/- for the 141 families inclusive of the above 60 families, displaced to date, due to the disaster, for the month of August 2017 as well, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: New projects proposed to be implemented from the year 2018 for the Development of the Plantation Sector
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-15
decision_details_body: •- The proposal made by Hon. Navin Dissanayake, the Minister of Plantation Industries, to obtain funds amounting to a sum of Rs.730 million from the General Treasury for the implementation of 10 projects proposed, commencing from the year 2018 for the enhancement of the performance of the plantation sector by the Rubber Research Institute, Coconut Cultivation Board, National Plantation Management Institute and the 'Thurusaviya' Fund which are functioning under the purview of the Ministry of Plantation Industries, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Port Access Elevated Highway Project - Construction of a new seventeen - storey office building and four workshops for the Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-15
decision_details_body: •- The proposed Port Access Highway Project is scheduled to be commenced by February, 2018 and the access road running across the buildings belonging to the Sri Lanka Ports Authority and the section where the facilities of the SLPA are located, has been planned to be commenced by December, 2018. In place of the buildings of the SLPA required to be removed due to the implementation of this project, a new office building with 17 storyes and 04 workshops are scheduled to be constructed. As such, with a view to commencing the construction work without any delay, the proposal made by Hon. Lakshman Kiriella, the Minister of Higher Education and Highways, to call for proposals from the Central Engineering Consultancy Bureau for providing consultancy services and to award the contract having evaluated the same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Accelerated Programme for the development of Middle Income Housing and Infrastructure
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-15
decision_details_body:
•- The Accelerated Programme for the Development of Middle Income Housing and Infrastructure, centered around Expressways, Highways and Railway lines in Urban and Semi-Urban areas has been launched by the Government with the participation of the private sector with the objective of providing housing for 'Middle Income Wage Earners'. Four projects of this type have already been commenced close to the towns of Wadduwa, Homagama, Jalthara and Ragama and several more projects as well are due to be implemented in the future. 




Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Sajith Premadasa, the Minister of Housing and Construction, to vest several state owned plots of lands situated in the districts of Gampaha, Kalutara, Kurunegala, Puttalam, Matale, Badulla and Matara with the National Housing Authority for the proposed housing development projects to be implemented in the future, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Providing relief to tea smallholders affected by floods and landslides
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-15
decision_details_body: •- Due to the floods and landslides that occurred in May 2017 in the districts of Galle, Ratnapura, Matara, Hambantota, Kalutara, Colombo and Kegalle, the cultivated lands of small tea holders in extent of 457.37 hectares have been fully damaged and 1,823.10 hectares have been partially damaged.  As such, the proposal made by Hon. Navin Dissanayake, the Minister of Plantation Industries, for the implementation of a programme to provide plants and fertilizer required to re-cultivate the damaged tea small holdings and to provide financial assistance to uplift the living standards of the affected tea small holders, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendments to the Tea, Rubber and Coconut Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act, No.2 of 1958
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-15
decision_details_body:
•- The Tea, Rubber and Coconut Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act, No.2 of 1958 was enacted with the objective of controlling the fragmentation of the coconut lands not less than 4 hectares in extent and tea and rubber lands not less than 20 hectares in extent.  According to the provisions in the Act, the Certificate of Consent issued by the Tea, Rubber and Coconut Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Board should be obtained when fragmenting such lands or when such lands are transferred as a single unit.  



It is a timely requirement to have some flexibility in using these lands for various large scale projects.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Navin Dissanayake, the Minister of Plantation Industries, to amend the Tea, Rubber and Coconut Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act, No.2 of 1958 incorporating provision to reduce the limit for fragmentation or transfer of coconut lands as a single unit to 02 hectares (05 Acres) and the limit for fragmentation or transfer of tea and rubber lands as a single unit to 08 hectares (20 Acres), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the National Aquaculture Development Authority of Sri Lanka Act, No.53 of 1998
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-15
decision_details_body:
•- The National Aquaculture Development Authority (NAQDA) of Sri Lanka has been  established under the Act, No.53 of 1998 with a view to promoting and regulating the aquaculture industry of Sri Lanka. Presently, action is pursued for the expansion of the aquaculture industry in Sri Lanka on a commercial scale and concurrently, for the sustainability of the industry, it is essential to have a strong legal framework for the regulation, conservation and management of the aquaculture industry.  Further, the provisions required for imposing punishments in respect of the offences identified in the management of the aquaculture industry and issuing of licenses for the importation of aquaculture related species, material and equipment and operational activities will have to be incorporated in the Act. 



Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Mahinda Amaraweera, the Minister of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources, to amend the National Aquaculture Development Authority of Sri Lanka Act, No.53 of 1998 vesting the powers necessary with the National Aquaculture Development Authority to suit the present day requirements and to appoint a Committee to study the matters and submit proposals and recommendations relating to same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Outstanding levy to be paid for luxury, semi-luxury and semi-luxury dual purpose vehicles
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-15
decision_details_body:
•- In terms of the Finance Act, No.16 of 1995, the owners of the luxury vehicles (diesel motor vehicles exceeding 2,500 Cylinder Capacity (CC) and petrol motor vehicles exceeding 2,000 CC), semi-luxury vehicles (diesel motor vehicles between 2,201 CC and 2,500 CC, diesel jeeps exceeding 2,200 CC, petrol cars between 1,801 CC and 2,000 CC and petrol jeeps exceeding 1,800 CC) and semi-luxury dual purpose vehicles (diesel cabs exceeding 2,200 CC and Petrol Cabs exceeding 1,800 CC) are liable to pay an annual levy up to  07 years from the date of first registration of such vehicles belonging to the said categories.  The first installment will be charged by the Department of Motor Traffic at the time of the registration of the vehicle and the balance installments could be paid to the department or the insurance company.  In the event of default of payment of the levy a 50% of penalty is to be charged for the outstanding levy. At this point of time, the total outstanding levy exceeds Rs.350 million. 



    Taking into consideration that the delay for the payment of the levy could be attributed to reasons beyond the control of the owners of the vehicles, the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala de Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, to grant a grace period of 03 months from 2017-09-01 to 2017-11-30 to recover the outstanding levy on the luxury, semi-luxury and semi-luxury dual purpose vehicles and to charge only 5% of the relevant penalty from the owners of the vehicles who pay the outstanding levy during the grace period granted, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendments to the Motor Traffic Act
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-15
decision_details_body: - The Government is contemplating expeditious action essential to ensure road safety by minimizing the traffic accidents increasing day by day. As such, the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala de Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, to publish the draft bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman in the Government Gazette to amend the relevant sections and Second Schedule to the Motor Traffic Act for the introduction of the timely needed amendments to the same and accordingly, to vest the powers with the Magistrates and police officers for the practical implementation of the proposed 'Drivers Demerit Points System',  the declaration of special qualifications to be possessed by a  driver who drives vehicles transporting dangerous chemicals, emergency service vehicles and public transport vehicles, regulation of the relevant speed limits for motor vehicles, the introduction of electronic technological methods for the payment of spot fines, the introduction of new vehicle Classes for the registration of special vehicles including the vehicles used by differently abled persons, the revision of fines to be imposed under the general penalty for any offence etc. for which a punishment has not been specified under the Motor Traffic Act and subsequently, to present it in Parliament,  was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining vehicles and machinery for the institutions under the purview of the Ministry of Sustainable Development and Wildlife
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-15
decision_details_body: - Having taken into consideration, the proposal made by Hon. Gamini Jayawickrema Perera, the Minister of Sustainable Development and Wildlife, to obtain vehicles and machinery essential for enhancing the performance of the Department of Wildlife Conservation, the Department of National Zoological Gardens and the Department of National Botanical Gardens which come under the purview of the Ministry of Sustainable Development and Wildlife, Cabinet approval was granted to provide an allocation for the purpose in the year 2018 and 2019 and as the initial step to allocate a sum of Rs. 500 million in the year 2018.

description: False Media Reports disseminated to the effect that the Samurdhi Allowance will be curtailed
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-15
decision_details_body: •- Due to the false media reports disseminated, a wrong impression has been created in the minds of the general public that the Samurdhi allowance has been suspended in the case of some Samurdhi beneficiaries.  The Cabinet noted that the government has not taken a decision to either suspend or curtail the Samurdhi allowance of any Samurdhi beneficiary and this fact had recently been reiterated by H.E. the President.

description: Prevention of Forest Reserves from wild fire and provision of water for the Wild Animals due to the severe drought prevailing
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body: - Due to the prevailing severe drought in Sri Lanka the wild animals are subject to a great distress and the wild fire that occur in the forest reserves has paused a threat of loosing their habitats. As such, the proposal made by Hon. Gamini Jayawickrema Perera, the Minister of Sustainable Development and Wildlife to provide 10 tractor water bowsers to the Department of Wildlife Conservation, to protect the forest reserves from fire and to supply the water required for the wild animals, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Demolishing of buildings, equipment and machinery found in the premises of the Kantale Sugar Industry Ltd
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet has granted approval to re‑commence the production activities of the Kantale Sugar Industry Ltd. under a Public Private Partnership which has presently been closed down for a period of nearly 23 years.  Bids have been called for demolishing all disposal buildings and selling goods and equipment prior to releasing the premises of the industry. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Gayantha Karunathilaka, the Minister of Lands and Parliamentary Reforms to award the contract to the bidder who offered the highest sum of Rs.540 million as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Award of the contract for the construction of a new bridge across the Kelani river
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Lakshman Kiriella, the Minister of Higher Education and Highways to award the contract for the construction of a bridge 380 meters in length with 6 lanes and its access roads for a sum of Rs.9,896 million as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement of the drugs used for the treatment of patients with immunity deficiencies
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine to award the contract for the procurement of 6,500 Vials of Human Immunoglobulin for IV use BP, 5-6g, an essential drug used for the treatment of patients with immunity deficiencies, for a sum of US$ 637,000 as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of the Pambahinna Water Supply Scheme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Rauff Hakeem, the Minister of City Planning and Water Supply, to award the contract for the construction of the Pambahinna Water Supply Scheme implemented with the objective of providing pipe bone safe drinking water to the people residing in the Pambahinna, Muththettuwegama, Puwakgahawela, Karagasthalawa, Kinchigune and Kumbalgama in the Ratnapura District and the University of Sabaragamuwa, for a sum of Rs.1,019.47 million as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Improvement of the Navigational Services Complex Building at the Bandaranaike International Airport, Katunayake
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala de Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation to award the tender for the construction of the proposed new extension to the Navigational Services Complex Building at the Bandaranaike International Airport, Katunayake for a sum of Rs.201.39 million as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Issuance of a certified copy of the judgment or the final decree free of charge  to each party to the case
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body: - The Civil Procedure Code and the Code of Criminal Procedure contain provisions to the effect that a certified copy of the judgment or the final decree can be issued to each party to the case upon payment of a fee.  However, it has been observed that the parties to certain cases do not possess the money necessary to obtain copies of such judgment or final decree. As such, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Wijayadasa Rajapaksa, the Minister of Justice, to amend the Civil Procedure Code and the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, incorporating provisions to enable the issuance of a  certified copy of a judgment or a decree free of charge to each party to the case, for ensuring the dispensation of justice and for the betterment of the judicial system, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Display the Ozone Friendly Tea Logo on Sri Lanka Cricket sportswear
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body:
- The Montreal Protocol on Ozone Depleting Substances decided in the year 1992, to limit the consumption of Methyl Bromide or Bromo-Methane hazardous to the ozone layer.  Accordingly, Sri Lanka has been successful in completely eliminating the use of this chemical as a pesticide, particularly in the tea plantation by focusing on alternative technical methods and it has come under international praise.   

As a mark of this achievement, the Sri Lanka Tea Board has introduced the  'Ozone Friendly Tea Logo' created by it and the proposal made by H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to have a discussion with the relevant institutions to display the logo in the official sportswear of the Sri Lanka Cricket Team, with a view to promoting Sri Lanka as an Ozone friendly tea manufacturing country in the international market, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Management of the price decline in pepper
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body: - The farmers engaged in pepper cultivation have faced various difficulties due to the decline in the price of pepper in the local and international markets.  Therefore, with the objective of ensuring the security of the livelihood and the revenue of the farmers engaged in pepper cultivation, the Cabinet decided to   appoint a Ministerial Sub‑Committee headed by the Hon. Minister of Finance and Mass Media comprising of Hon. Minister of Primary Industries; Disaster Management; Development Strategies and International Trade; Industry and Commerce; and Irrigation and Water Resources Management, as its members to study the matter and submit a Report to the Cabinet without any delay.

description: Implementation of the Western Region Megapolis Initiative through the respective Project Offices
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09

description: Establishment of the Amaradeva Aesthetic and Research Centre
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body: - The musical influence and the creations of Dr. Pandith Amaradeva who was instrumental in creating a local culture of music unique to the native features based upon the North Indian music, mingling with local folk music can be considered as a national heritage of the country. With a view to preserving that heritage to be experienced and admired by the future generations as well, the Government has proposed to establish the 'Amaradeva Asapuwa' with all essential components and infrastructure related to music. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Mangala Samaraweera, the Minister of Finance and Mass Media to establish the 'Amaradeva Asapuwa' as 'Amaradeva Aesthetic and Research Centre' by an Act of Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: New Development Projects in the Health Sector
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body:
- Due to the long term investments carried out in the health sector by the Government of Sri Lanka, health service has achieved improvements in the health outcomes and approximately 100% of preventive health care, 90% - 95% of in-patient care and 40% - 50% of out-patient care are being provided  by the Public Sector. Health indexes are maintained on par with the developed countries and accordingly, the health services in Sri Lanka should be further upgraded with a view to making the population more healthy while also carrying out the health services free of charge uninterruptedly. 
 
Accordingly, the Government has planned to improve the facilitates of the peripheral hospitals in order to minimize the overcrowding of major hospitals while also ensuring the optimal distribution of physical and human resources and for the construction of ward complexes for paediatrics, oncology, surgical, maternal, neonatal and oral health, operating theaters, drug stores and clinics in remote areas enabling easy access for the public to have specialist healthcare. Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine to seek funds to initiate and implement several diverse projects which cost around Rs.28,000 million in the year 2018, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Modernization activities of the Sri Lanka Planetarium
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body: - The Sri Lanka Planetarium which is one of the largest Planetariums in the world with a 23 meter diameter dome has seating facilities to accommodate 500 visitors per session. This planetarium constructed using the pre-fabricated concrete plates technology has not been subject to modernization during recent times. As such, the proposal made by Hon. Susil Premajayantha, the Minister of Science, Technology and Research, to refurbish the dome and the surrounding sections of the Planetarium buildings identified as necessary to be refurbished expeditiously, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Guidelines to be adopted when resettling the families displaced due to floods and landslides and the plans to be used when constructing houses for such families
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body: - The Government has initiated a programme for granting houses to the families who were deprived  of their dwelling places due to the floods and landslides that occurred in several Districts including Ratnapura, Kalutara, Galle and Matara due to the adverse weather conditions which affected the Island in May 2017. Under this programme the National Building Research Organization has prepared Guidelines and the Housing Plans to be adopted for the houses under construction for the resettlement of the displaced families. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Anura Priyadharshana Yapa, the Minister of Disaster Management to implement the programme for the resettlement of the displaced families due to floods and landslides in accordance with the said Guidelines and the Housing Plans, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Preservation of the Kandyan Heritage
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body:
- The preservation of the ancient historic places subject to destruction located in the Central and Uva Provinces which are the centres of the Kandyan Heritage, the rehabilitation of the small tanks, anicuts and irrigation systems, which had largely contributed to the upcountry economy and for the protection of folk art and Janakala techniques including traditional Kandyan dancing forms, the metal, lacquer and cane industry and the flax plant production, rush and reed handicrafts, is of vital importance. 

	Accordingly, it has been proposed to implement various projects including the implementation of the project for developing the Traditional Kandyan Village, renovation of rural tank and irrigation canals, rehabilitation of ancient historic places and the promotion of art techniques, including the establishment of museums and cultural centres. Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. S.B. Dissanayake, the Minister of Social Empowerment, Welfare and Kandyan Heritage, for the establishment of a Statuary Board by an Act of Parliament  titled the 'Kandyan Heritage Protection Authority' was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Consideration of the operational activities of the Mattala Rajapaksa International Airport under the Public Private Partnership Framework
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body: - The accumulated loss of the Mattala Rajapaksa International Airport as at 31st December 2016 which runs at a loss presently, is US$ 112.9 million (equivalent to Rs.15,600 million). In the circumstances, carrying out the operational activities of this Airport further incurring losses is a substantial financial burden on the Government. As such, with a view to converting the Mattala Rajapaksa International Airport into a high revenue deriving Airport under the Public Private Partnership framework, proposals have been invited from Investors dealing with the aviation related ventures.  However, no proposals have yet been received to cover the entire operation of the Airport, Management and Maintenance. In the meantime, a proposal has been submitted by the Government of India to commence a joint venture focusing attention not only on the commercial Air Services of the Mattala International Airport, Aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul, and flying schools but also in the areas of its operation, management, maintenance and the development.   Accordingly, the proposal made by  Hon. Nimal Siripala de Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, to appoint a Committee comprising of several senior Secretaries to Ministries to make a further study on the matter, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Revision of the fines imposed on traffic offences committed under the Motor Traffic Act
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body:
- Having identified 7 violations of traffic rules which severely affect the fatal road accidents to a large extent, it was proposed in 2016 to increase the fines imposed on these traffic offences, up to a minimum of Rs.25,000/- with a view to minimizing road accidents.  However, taking into consideration the protest made by the Bus and Three-Wheeler Associations the President appointed an Officials' Committee to inquire into the increasing of fines imposed under the Motor Traffic Act and accordingly, the proposal made by  Hon. Nimal Siripala de Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation to implement the following recommendations made by the said Committee, was approved by the Cabinet. 
*	Increase of the minimum fine up to Rs.25,000/- in respect of the following traffic offences:

-	driving a vehicle without a valid driving license

-	employing in service persons who do not possess a driving license

-	driving vehicles under the influence of liquor or drugs

-	crossing a railway line haphazardly

-	driving a vehicle without a valid insurance cover
*	Revision of the minimum fines presently imposed in respect of the following traffic offences:  

-	high speed driving 
	(imposing a spot fine - of Rs.3,000/- for driving a vehicle at high speed above the 20% limit of the maximum speed stipulated; of Rs.5,000/- for driving a vehicle at high speed above the 20% limit and less than 30% limit of the maximum speed stipulated; of Rs.10,000/- for driving a vehicle at high speed above the 30% limit and less than 50% limit of the maximum speed stipulated; and of Rs. 15,000/-; for driving a vehicle at high speed above the 50% limit) 
 
- 	Overtaking from the left
	(the minimum spot fine for this offence is increased up to Rs.2,000/-)
-	driving a motor vehicle carelessly or without due regard to others or without due diligence
	(a minimum fine of Rs.10,000/- is imposed for the offence)



-	driving a motor vehicle recklessly or in a dangerous manner or at a dangerous speed 
	(a minimum fine of Rs. 10,000/- is imposed for the offence)

-	driving vehicles by underaged persons
	(the minimum fine of Rs. 5,000/- imposed on this offence presently is increased up to Rs. 30,000/-) 

- 	the increase of the minimum fine imposed under the general penalty for any offence for which a punishment has not been specified under the Motor Traffic Act up to Rs.2,500/-.

*	Imposing a spot fine of  Rs. 2,000/- for using a mobile phone while driving.

*	Expediting of the implementation of a driver score card system.

*	Installing of CCTV cameras in the places where many road accidents occur and taking legal action against the offenders based on such information.

*	implementation of the proposal for the use of electronic facilities for payment of spot fines for traffic offences expeditiously.

*	proper display of the speed limit sign boards on expressway and highways. 

*	implementation of an integrated timetable and the operation of the SLTB buses and the private buses or to adopt a suitable procedure expeditiously. 

*	Establishment of institutions to regulate the three-wheelers and the buses and vans transporting school children.

*	Establishment of a public transport service ensuring the safety of passengers.

*	Use of modern technological equipment to minimize the various irregularities caused by some of the officers who enforce the traffic rules and to ensure transparency in the enforcement of traffic laws.

description: Construction of an Airport Hotel at the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body: - With the objective of providing a better service for the air travellers and tourists, two blocks of lands owned by the the Airport and the Aviation Services Limited (Sri Lanka) at the Bandaranaike International Airport, Katunayake was set apart for two investors for the construction and operation of a star class Airport Hotel consisting of a minimum of 100 rooms.  However, one of the investors has decided not to proceed with his proposal.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala de Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation to call for proposals to select another suitable investor to construct and operate a hotel in the said block of land, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining Funds for the implementation of the Rooftop Solar Power Generation Project by installing solar power systems on roof tops
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body: - The target of the Government is to generate 200 MW of electricity by the end of the year 2020 through Solar Power generation while plans have been made  to enhance the power generation up to 1000 MW by the year 2025. In order to achieve this target, concessionary loans will be provided to install Rooftop Solar Power Generation Systems under the 'Solar Power Generation Project'.  The Asian Development Bank has consented to assist this programme by providing concessionary loan assistance for developing solar rooftop market infrastructure, to arrange sub‑projects to obtain loans and to increase the capacity and awareness of commercial and domestic consumers including the stakeholders. As such, the proposal made by Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe, the Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs, to conduct negotiations in this regard and to enter into the relevant Agreements, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Parliamentary Budget Office
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-09
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe, the Prime Minister to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft the necessary legislation for the establishment of  a 'Parliamentary Budget Office', with the main objective of providing services and facilities for the Members of Parliament, including an independent and non‑partisan analysis of budget cycles, fiscal policy and financial proposals, when the Parliament exercise effective control over Public Finance in terms of the provisions of the Constitution, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Providing relief to the people affected by the prevailing dry weather conditions
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2017-08-01
decision_details_body:
