Gamini Jayawickrema Perera, the Minister of Sustainable Development and Wildlife, to provide redress through increasing the existing compensation up to Rs. 200,000/- for a death, Rs. 200,000/- for permanent disability (regardless of the existing age limit), Rs. 75,000/- for injuries, and Rs.100,000/- for house and property damages, caused due to a wild elephant attack, and in order to minimize the delays caused when approving such compensation, to entrust the responsibility of payment of compensation to a Committee headed by the District Secretary and to establish an Appeal Committee headed by the Director General of Wild Life to consider the appeals submitted by the parties dissatisfied with the decisions of the said Committee pertaining to payment of compensation, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Creating an Accelerated Economic Transformation in Sri Lanka - Setting up a Central Programme Management Unit
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-09-13
decision_details_body: - Setting up of a unit dedicated to track, monitor and take timely corrective actions in respect of development activities, is considered most critical to achieve the objectives of enabling an accelerated economic development across the country and transforming the country's economy into a sustainable social market economy. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe, the Prime Minister, and the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs, to obtain the assistance of McKinsey & Company of USA, which is a foreign consultancy firm with proven experience and capability of setting up of similar CPM Units in rapidly transforming economies such as Malaysia, for setting up of a CPMU in Sri Lanka to carry out the desired objectives, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Financial Assistance from the Asian Development Bank for the Proposed Capital Market Development Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-09-06
decision_details_body: - With a view to mobilizing financial resources required for the economic development through the capital market of Sri Lanka productively, the proposal made by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, to conduct negotiations to obtain a policy based loan assistance of US$ 250 million from the Asian Development Bank (ADB), for the development an  efficient, stable and transparent capital market comprised of a strong, legal and regulatory framework, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of Section 4 of the Central Expressway from Kurunegala to Dambulla (60 km)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-09-06
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet has already granted its approval to rehabilitate 150 km of the existing roads and to construct 100 km of new roads, under the 'Rajarata Navodaya' Development Programme.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Lakshman Kiriella, the Minister of Higher Education and Highways, to implement the proposed project of constructing Section 4 of the Central Expressway, 60 km in length, commencing from Kurunegala and running up to Dambulla, under the 'Rajarata Navodaya' Development Programme,  was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Maduru Oya Right Bank Development Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-09-06
decision_details_body: - Maduru Oya Reservoir constructed in the year 1982 is one of the major reservoirs constructed under the Mahaweli Accelerated Development Progrmme.  It was expected through the above reservoir to develop 39,000 ha of land in the Mahaweli System 'B' based on the districts of  Polonnaruwa and Batticaloa, for agricultural purposes. Although, the Maduru Oya Left Bank development activities were initiated and completed, the development of the Right Bank area has not been implemented so far due to the inadequacy of the financial provisions.  Accordingly, with a view to expediting the supply of drinking water, provision of irrigation water and development of infrastructure facilities for the socio‑economic development in the districts of Polonnaruwa and Batticaloa, where development had stalled due to the impact of prolonged conflict, the proposal made by H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to implement the Maduru Oya Right Bank Development Project during the period of 2017-2020, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Completion of the Construction Work of Polpithigama Police Station
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-09-06
decision_details_body: - The construction work of the  Polpithigama Police station, belonging to the Police Division of Nikaweratiya and with 130 Police personnel in service, had been initiated in the year 2007, but however, has been suspended midway due to various reasons.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Sagala Rathnayake, the Minister of Law & Order and Southern Development, to complete the construction work of the Polpithigama Police Station, at a total estimated cost of Rs.49.7 million, also incorporating the subsequently identified requirements, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Project for the Construction of Thambalagamuwa Police Station
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-09-06
decision_details_body: - The Thambalagamuwa Police Station, which functioned as a Police Post to provide public security in the areas of Muthur, Seruwawila and Trincomalee in the Eastern Province and subsequently established as a Police Station in the year 2004, is presently housed, with 155 Police personnel in service, in two buildings obtained on a rental basis, with minimum facilities.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Sagala Rathnayake, the Minister of Law & Order and Southern Development, to construct a new building for the said Police Station, in a  land belonging to the Police Department, at an estimated cost of Rs.90.4 million, to enable it to provide a better public service, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of a new Inland Water Transport System through Private-Public Partnership
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-09-06
decision_details_body: - In a backdrop where there is a steady escalation of traffic congestion in the city, it has been identified that a rapid and economical transportation service based on reservoirs and canals could be provided for the areas where bus or railway transportation services are inadequately deployed.  Therefore, using the existing canal system and sea, an efficient transportation service that links the East-West and North-South areas of Colombo, could be provided.  Accordingly, three inland water transport lines, namely Wellawatta - Battaramulla (through the canals), Fort - Union Place (along the Beira Lake) and Mattakuliya - Hanwella (along the Kelani River) have been identified by the Megapolis Transport Committee as potential routes for the purpose.  As such, the proposal made by Hon. Patali Champika Ranawaka, the Minister of Megapolis and Western Development, to carry out a feasibility study with regard to the construction of an Inland Water Transport System under a Private‑Public Partnership system, identifying a suitable private investor, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: 'Let's Awaken Polonnaruwa' District Development Programme -  Implementation of Priority Water Supply Projects
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-09-06
decision_details_body: - With the objective of providing safe drinking water for the upliftment of the living standard of the people of Polonnaruwa District, the proposal made by Hon. Rauff Hakeem, the Minister of City Planning and Water Supply, to implement nine (09) water supply projects under the 'Let's Awaken Polonnaruwa' District Development Programme and to get the required sum of Rs.6,464.36 million set apart for the purpose, for the years 2017 and 2018, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Memorandum of Understanding on the Establishment of a Political Consultation Mechanism between Slovenia and Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-09-06
decision_details_body: - With a view to promoting, strengthening and expanding bilateral relations including political, economic, consular, technological and scientific and cultural cooperation between Slovenia and Sri Lanka, the proposal made by Hon. Mangala Samaraweera, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, to sign the above Memorandum of Understanding between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Sri Lanka and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Slovenia, during his official visit to be made to Slovenia from  04th to 08th September, 2016, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Relocation of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-09-06
decision_details_body: - The Republic Building situated in Colombo Fort area, where the Ministry of Foreign Affairs is presently located, is a building constructed in the British Colonial Era and it has been identified as a heritage that should be preserved.  Accordingly, it is essential to shift  the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to another place and the proposal made by Hon. Mangala Samaraweera, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, to get a land in extent of 2 Acres, situated at Jawatta Road, Colombo, allocated for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which has been identified as suitable to construct a new building for that Ministry, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Enforcement and Regulation of the activities related to the International Conventions pertaining to Wildlife Conservation, in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-09-06
decision_details_body: - By now, Sri Lanka has signed several International conventions relating  to Wildlife Conservation, however, specific legal provisions have not been provided for the formal implementation of the activities related to the said Conventions.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Gamini Jayawickrema Perera, the Minister of Sustainable Development and Wildlife, to amend the Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance, in order to enable the Minister to make necessary regulations for the implementation of  International Conventions related to wildlife conservation signed by Sri Lanka, locally, including the activities relating to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Declaration of 'The National Marine Resources Conservation Week'
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-09-06
decision_details_body: - The accumulation of non-decayable substances on beaches and marine regions directly or through canals causes adverse effects to the marine  ecosystems as well as to the related industries such as fishing and  tourism. Therefore, it is essential to formulate a systematic arrangement with public participation to protect the marine ecosystems as well the sustainability of  the related industries.  As such, the proposal made by H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to declare the period from Saturday of the 3rd week to Saturday of the  4th week of September of every year as the 'National Marine Resources Conservation Week' simultaneously to the International Coastal Clean up Day, from this year onwards, to implement the coastal clean up and conservation programme with the participation and contribution  of the general public, school children, government and non-governmental organizations from 17th to 23rd of September, 2016 and also to conduct its national celebration at the coastal stretch of Mattakkuliya, Colombo, on 17th of September, 2016, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Proper Management of the use of Polythene to minimize environmental issues caused by Polythene
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-09-06
decision_details_body: - The use of plastic and polythene related products is a common occurrence  in present day society and as such, a number of social, environmental, health and economic issues have emerged due to the improper use,  disposal and burning of such products.   The per capita use of plastic and polythene in Sri Lanka is approximately 0.5 kg per day and around five (05) lakhs of tonnes of polythene is imported to Sri Lanka annually.  Certain countries in the world have totally banned the use of polythene while some other countries have allowed the use of only  selected types of plastic material.  Taking into consideration, matters such as the need to control the adverse environmental effects caused due to the addition of plastic and polythene related products that take a long time to decay, to the environment as well as the engagement of a large number of employees in plastic and polythene related industries, the proposal made by  H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, for the appointment of a Committee of Experts to formulate a National Policy and an Action Plan pertaining to the use of polythene, plastic and biodegradable plastic in Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Controlling the Importation and the use of non-eco-friendly Asbestos in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-09-06
decision_details_body: - Asbestos is used for numerous products such as roofing sheets, floor tiles, cement pipes, brake pads of vehicles, paper and ropes. The importation of blue asbestos (Crocidolite) to Sri Lanka, which was identified as a carcinogen by the World Health Organization (WHO),  has been banned since the year 1987 and by now all types of asbestos, including white asbestos (Chrysotile) which is most commonly used in Sri Lanka, have been identified as carcinogens by the WHO.  Around 80% of the white asbestos imported to Sri Lanka is used to manufacture roofing sheets.  Accordingly, with a view to minimizing the adverse effects caused to health through asbestos and improving public health, the proposal made by H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to move towards cost effective substitutes and limit  the import, use and production of asbestos related products from 01-01-2018 and to formulate an action plan to totally ban the production of asbestos related products in the country by 01-01-2024,   was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Declaration of the Year 2017 as the Year of Poverty Alleviation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-30
decision_details_body: - As per the pledge made through the Election Manifesto for the Presidential Election-2015, to create “a nation that is suitable to live in” (Pathirupa Desa) and according to the United Nations (UN) Sustainable Development Goals, the special focus of the Government is drawn towards poverty alleviation. It is important that the economic development agenda of the Government does not solely target economic growth but also to focuses attention on areas such as social security, reducing the disparity in income distribution, people being socially marginalized due to various reasons and the prevailing development disparities at provincial and district levels. Therefore, it is essential to give priority to rescuing people from poverty and fields related to that within the economic and social policy followed by the Government. Accordingly, identifying the necessity of having a macro arrangement for the purpose and giving priority to working with a collective approach, the proposal made by H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena,  to declare the forthcoming Year 2017 as the 'Year of Alleviation of Poverty' and to monitor this programme through a Committee headed by H.E. the President and the Hon. Prime Minister and comprised of the relevant Ministers and other stakeholders, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development Policy Funds (Private Sector Development, Governance Improvement and Fiscal Consolidation)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-30
decision_details_body: - Focusing attention on the financial stability of Sri Lanka, development of public resources management and facilitating the competitiveness of private sector, the Japanese International Cooperation Agency (JICA) has agreed to provide funds for the implementation of government development measures to attain economic stability. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Prime Minister Ranil Wickremasinghe, in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs, to sign the Exchange of Notes with the Government of Japan, to obtain development policy funds of Japanese Yen 10,000 million (approximately Rs.14,453.2 million) under the terms and conditions favourable to the country and to enter into a loan agreement with the JICA, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Ratification of Paris Agreement by Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-30
decision_details_body: - 178 countries including Sri Lanka have placed their signatures to the Paris Agreement on Climate Change at the United Nations (UN) Headquarters, on 22nd April 2016.  It is expected to significantly reduce the impact and risk of Climate Change by making every effort to keep the increase of global temperature level well below 2 0C, relative to the pre-industrial era level, and not exceed 1.5 0C.  It is important for Sri Lanka, being an island nation which may be prey to adverse impacts of climate change such as prolonged droughts, flash floods, rise in sea levels, landslides and inundation of low lands, to become a party to such  Agreement and therefore, the proposal made by H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, for the ratification of said the Paris Agreement by Sri Lanka and to proceed with related future action, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishing Japan-Sri Lanka Joint Comprehensive Partnership (JCP) Secretariat in Colombo and Tokyo
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-30
decision_details_body: - A declaration on Joint Comprehensive Partnership was agreed upon by the Governments of Japan and Sri Lanka, during the Prime Minister's official visit to Japan in October 2015, covering the sectors of Advanced Agriculture, Science and Technology for Industry, Quality Infrastructure and Regional Development, Education and Human Resources Development and Civil Safety and Security.  Accordingly, with a view to facilitating for the purpose, the proposal made by Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe, the Prime Minister, and the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs, for the establishment of Japan-Sri Lanka Joint Comprehensive Partnership (JCP) Secretariat in Colombo and in  Tokyo, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Using a Standardized term for the Sri Lanka 'Police' Department
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-30
decision_details_body: - The Police of Sri Lanka has been denominated under various terms during different eras. Under the Police Ordinance, No.16 of 1865 and the Departmental Orders it has been known as 'Sri Lanka Police Force', after 1945 it has been termed as the 'Sri Lanka Police Department' and since the year 1972 it has been known as the 'Sri Lanka Police Service'. The Sri Lanka Police Department commemorates its 150th anniversary this year and in this context, considering the need to use a standard term to address that department, the proposal made by Hon. Sagala Ratnayaka, the Minister of Law & Order and Southern Development, to use the name 'Sri Lanka Police' hereinafter for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of the Prison Complex, Jaffna - Phase II
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-30
decision_details_body: - It has been designed to implement the project on construction of the Prison Complex in Pannai, Jaffna, to accommodate 1,000 detainees. The construction work of the Phase I of the project has been completed and declared opened with accommodation facilities for 130 inmates. Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. D.M Swaminathan, the Minister of Prison Reforms, Rehabilitation, Resettlement and Hindu Religious Affairs, to commence the construction work of Phase II of the project, at an estimated cost of Rs.623.32 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of Short Term Priority Water Supply improvements for 3 BOI Zones and surroundings in Ranpokunugama, Kirindiwela and Biyagama areas of Gampaha District and Koggala area of Galle District
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-30
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Rauff Hakeem, the Minister of City Planning and Water Supply, to carry out the necessary improvements to the existing water supply schemes in the relevant areas, treating them as national priority projects, at an estimated cost of Rs.1,531.9 million, to ensure an adequate supply of drinking water to the people living in the BOI Zone of Biyagama, Wathupitiwala and Koggala and suburbs in the Biyagama area and the areas of Ranpokunagama, Kirindiwela and Habaraduwa, was approved in principle by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of Three Water Supply Schemes for the provision of drinking water to the people of the areas affected due to the water leakage that occurred in the main tunnel of Uma Oya Multipurpose Development Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-30
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet has already granted approval for the implementation of three (03) water supply schemes for the provisions of purified drinking water to the people living in the areas of Weheragalatenna, Makul-ella and Kurundugolla which were affected due to the water leakage that occurred in the main tunnel of Uma Oya Multipurpose Development Project. Accordingly, the construction activities of the said projects have been commenced and it has been revealed that the number of beneficiary families including the families living close to the water resources have increased up to 2,400 from 1417.  Therefore, the proposal made by H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to revise the cost involved for the above mentioned 03 water supply schemes as Rs.317.24 million, and implement the said projects expeditiously, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Task Force on Legal and Judicial Causes of Prison Overcrowding
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-30
decision_details_body: - 	The joint proposal made by Hon.(Dr.) Wijayadasa Rajapaksa, the Minister of Justice; and Hon. D.M. Swaminathan, the Minister of Prison Reforms, Rehabilitation, Resettlement and Hindu Religious Affairs, to establish a Task Force co-chaired by the Secretary, Ministry of Justice;  and the Secretary, Ministry of Prison Reforms, Rehabilitation, Resettlement and Hindu Religious Affairs with the representation of the representatives of other institutions including the relevant Departments, to identify the legal and judicial causes of prison overcrowding and to obtain proposals on amendments to be made to the existing laws and procedures from the above Task Force, for the reduction of overcrowding prevalent in the Prisons, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Prevention of Coastal Erosion that occurs in the areas of Oluvil and Ninthavur in the Ampara District
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-30
decision_details_body: - As per a proposal made by Hon. Rauff Hakeem, the Minister of City Planning and Water Supply, an Officials' Committee has already been appointed to study and submit recommendations on finding long term solutions for the prevention of severe coastal erosion that takes place in an area of around 550 meters of coastal stretch situated north of Oluvil Port in the Ampara District and providing relief to the people affected by  the said erosion. The Sri Lanka Ports Authority has already initiated the conservation activities of an area of 150 meters along this coastal stretch and the balance portion of about 400 meters has to be conserved very early.  Since long term conservation methodologies will take time, the proposal made by Hon. Arjuna Ranatunga, the Minister of Ports and Shipping, to carry out expeditious steps of raising obstructing sand mounds along the coastal stretch and the erecting stone ridges as remedial measures, with the assistance of the Coast Conservation and Coastal Resources Management Department, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development of Farms belonging to the National Livestock Development Board (NLDB) under the Public-Private Partnership Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-30
decision_details_body: - There are 31 crop and livestock farms across the island belonging to the National Livestock Development Board (NLDB) that contribute to the provision of necessary patronage to small scale farmers, national dairy production, meat production and the egg production process. Although the 04 large scale diary farms of the NLDB situated in Central and Southern Provinces have been developed, investing a large sum of money, it has been found difficult to obtain necessary funds to develop other farms with similar potential. Therefore, the focus of the Government has been drawn towards the development of such farms in collaboration with the private sector.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. P. Harison, the Minister of Rural Economy, to amend to the State Agricultural Corporation Act, No.11 of 1972, incorporating the legal provisions required for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Leasing out of a block of land of 10 Acres at Muthurajawela for a Project for generating Energy out of Solid Waste
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-30
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Patali Champika Ranawaka, the Minister of Megapolis and Western Development, to lease out a block of land in extent of 10 acres situated in Muthurajawela area, belonging to the Sri Lanka Land Reclamation and Development Corporation, to a private company, on a 30 year lease basis, for the implementation of a project for energy generation out of solid waste, as a solution to the issue on generating of solid waste disposal, was approved by the Cabinet in principle.

description: Registration of Motor Cycles which are being driven without registration
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-30
decision_details_body: - Motor Cycles which are not registered in the Department of Motor Traffic can be commonly found in the country. These motor cycles which are frequently used in areas where public transport facilities are low, render a sufficient contribution to the agricultural economy of the rural areas while many of such motor cycles are also used by self-employed persons. Although, such motor cycles make a sufficient contribution to the rural economy, the Government annually loses a considerable income due to non-registration and it has been identified that it would be appropriate to grant an opportunity to register these motor cycles by imposing a surcharge, in order to suppress frauds, corruption and thefts and establish the rule of law in the country.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala de Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, to allow registration as a concession after inspection of motor cycles without legal documents, to implement it in a manner without causing prejudice to legitimate motor cycle importers and in conformity with the provisions of the Motor Traffic Act and to grant this relief only for a period of four (04) months, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining Membership of International Sustainable Tourism and Eliminating Poverty (ST-EP) Organization
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-30
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. John Amarathunga, the Minister of Tourism Development and Christian Religious Affairs, to obtain the membership of International Organization on Sustainable Tourism - Eliminating Poverty (ST-EP) by Sri Lanka which is proposed to be established under the patronage of UN World Tourism Organization (UNWTO), with the main objectives of facilitating knowledge management and project development for economic improvement through tourism promotion, undertaking researches and projects for achieving sustainable tourism development through elimination of poverty and contributing for the protection of culture and nature through public‑private partnership, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of the National Media Centre
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - On implementing the state mechanism, the timely dissemination of complete, reliable and accurate official information to the general public is a main responsibility of the Government, and it has been further ensured through the  provisions of the recently enacted Right to Information Act. As a one more step in this direction, with a view to ensuring the implementation of the principles of  Good Governance in a more enhanced manner, the proposal made by Hon. Ranil Wickramasinghe, the Prime Minister, for the establishment of a 'National Media Centre', which would function as the Official Media Spokesman of the Government in disseminating official government information to both electronic and print media and coordinating information, while obtaining the views of the general public for policy formulation, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of Quarters for the Married Special Task Force (STF) Officers
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - The provision of housing facilities for married officers engaged in security activities such as maintaining law and order in the City of Colombo and suburbs, controlling riots and commotions that arise on various occasions, and providing  quick relief in disaster situations has become an urgent need and accordingly, in order to provide housing facilities for the said officers, the proposal made by Hon. Sagala Ratnayaka, the Minister of Law & Order and Southern Development, to construct a housing complex, at an estimated cost of Rs.388 million, utilizing the space and facilities available at the Kalapaluwawa Camp of the Special Task Force (STF), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Award of Contract for the Construction of Habarana-Veyangoda 220kV Transmission Line
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Ranjith Siyambalapitiya, the Minister of Power and Renewable Energy, to award the contract for the construction of Habarana- Veyangoda 220 KV Transmission Line - (Lot B), funded by the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), as per the recommendation of the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of a New Three-Storeyed Building for the Divisional Secretariat, - Haliela
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - The Divisional Secretariat, Haliela, situated in Badulla District, comprises of 57 Grama Niladhari Divisions and has a population exceeding 90,000. The Haliela Divisional Secretariat Office is presently housed in a very old building with minimum space and facilities, and as a result, the general public who come to receive its services are faced with various difficulties. Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Vajira Abeywardena, the Minister of Home Affairs, to construct a three-storeyed building for the Divisional Secretariat, Haliela, at an estimated cost of Rs.176 million, in order to provide an efficient and effective service to the people of Haliela area as well as to provide a conducive work environment to the staff, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Ratnapura Expressway Project - Obtaining of Proposals for the Procurement of Civil Work Contracts
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - The feasibility studies, preliminary designs and the environment impact assessments are underway, in respect of the proposed Ratnapura Expressway, 73.9 km in length, which is designed to run from Kahatuduwa Interchange of the Southern Expressway to Pelmadulla. The Export and Import Bank (EXIM) of China has agreed to provide funds for the civil construction works of this expressway.  As per the recommendation of the Cabinet Committee on Economic Management (CCEM), the expressway is scheduled to be constructed under four (04) sections and accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Lakshman Kiriella, the Minister of Higher Education and Highways, to call for bids on technical and financial proposals in respect of each road section, from the companies recommended by the Chinese Government, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development of Infrastructure Facilities of the Sri Lanka Institute of Advanced Technological Education, Jaffna
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Lakshman Kiriella, the Minister of Higher Education and Highways, to award the contract for construction of a four (04) storied building complex for the Sri Lanka Institute of Advanced Technological Education, Jaffna, as per the recommendation of the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Central Expressway Project - Construction of Phase 03 from Pothuhera to Galagedara (32.5 km) and the Receipt of Bids and Proposals
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Lakshman Kiriella, the Minister of Higher Education and Highways to call for bids and proposals as per recommendations of the Cabinet Committee on Economic Management (CCEM), to select a suitable contractor and a consultant for the construction activities of Phase 03 of the Central Expressway from Pothuhera to Galagedara (32.5 km), to be constructed under the financial assistance of Japan International Cooperation Corporation Agency (JICA), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of Roads in the Downstream Development Areas under the Moragahakanda - Kaluganga Development Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - In order to resettle the families affected by the Moragahakanda - Kaluganga Development Project as well as to reap the full benefits of the project, it is of utmost importance to develop the irrigation and infrastructure facilities in the downstream area of the said reservoirs. Therefore, the proposal made by H.E. the President, Hon. Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to award the contracts for the construction of Moragahakanda-Wellawela Road (6.37 km), Medirigiriya-Kantale Road through Agbopura (8.5 km) and the construction of internal roads within the new Laggala Town (road surfacing), which are essential road development works, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Supply of Uniform and other Clothing Material for the Sri Lanka Army, Navy,  Air Force and Civil Security Force for the Year 2016
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - The textile requirements of the three forces and the other institutions under the Ministry of Defence have been met by local textile manufactures since the year 2005 and the relevant activities are carried out by the Domestic Textile Allocation Committee (DTAC) established under the Ministry of Industry and Commerce. Accordingly, the proposal made by H. E. the President, Hon. Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Defence, for the purchase of uniform material and other textile requirements of the Sri Lanka Army, the Sri Lanka Navy, the Sri Lanka Air Force and the Civil Security Force for the year 2016, from the relevant local textile manufactures, as recommended by the Domestic Textile Allocation Committee (DTAC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining Fishnet Products required for distribution among the fishermen from the Northsea Ltd.
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - The joint proposal made by Hon. D.M. Swaminathan, the Minister of Prison Reforms, Rehabilitation, Resettlement and Hindu Religious Affairs and Hon. Mahinda Amaraweera, the Minister of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources Development, to purchase from North-Sea Ltd., a 100% State owned Company, the fishing nets required annually by the Department of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources for subsidy distribution among fishermen, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: International Religious Conference - To be held in Colombo in November 2016
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - Considering the timely need to create peaceful co-existence, religious tolerance, multi-cultural reflection as well as reconciliation among the races, through religious harmony and understanding, the Cabinet has already granted approval to hold two International Religious Conferences in Sri Lanka.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. M.H.A. Haleem, the Minister of Posts, Postal Services and Muslim Religious Affairs, to provide the funds required for the organizing activities of the International Religious Conference to be held in Colombo in November 2016, under the theme 'Role of Religion in Pluralistic and Democratic Societies in South and South East Asia: Perspectives of Islam' with the participation of high level local and foreign dignitaries including Heads of State of 16 Countries, was approved in principle by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of the Proposed Dedicated Economic Centre, Vavuniya at Two Places and the Obtaining of Consultancy Services
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - The responsibility of selecting a suitable place for the construction of the Dedicated Economic Centre, Vavuniya, in accordance with the Budget proposal 2016, was vested with the District Development Committee of Vavuniya.  Considering the representations made by various parties and the necessity of  completing the salient construction work concerned within the year by utilizing the relevant budgetary allocations, the proposal made by Hon. P. Harison, the Minister of Rural Economy, as per the recommendation of the Cabinet Committee on Economic Management (CCEM), to construct two Dedicated Economic Centres at Mankulam in the Mullaitivu District and at Mathauwaithakulam in the Vavuniya District, instead of one Dedicated Economic Centre,  was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Enhancing the Financial Subsidy for Tea, Rubber and Coconut Fertilizer 	Sectors
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - As recommended by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Management, the Government has taken action to grant a financial subsidy for fertilizer, proportionate to the annually cultivated land, to Smallholders who own a cultivated land in extent of 01 hectare or less in the tea, coconut and rubber sectors. Accordingly, there will be an entitlement to a financial subsidy of Rs.15,000/-, per hectare for tea; Rs.9,000/- per hectare for coconut and Rs.5,000/- per hectare for rubber.  With a view to providing subsidies for a larger number of interested beneficiaries, the proposal made by Hon. Navin Dissanayake, the Minister of Plantation Industries to increase the current approved ceiling on the extent of land to be eligible for Rubber and Coconut subsidy, from 01 hectare up to 02 hectares,  was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on promotion of cooperation in the Fisheries Industry
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Mahinda Amaraweera, the Minister of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources Development, to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Bureau of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region of the People’s Republic of China and the National Aquaculture Development Authority of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka, for the purpose of promoting cooperation between the two countries in respect of fisheries activities, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining Indian Grant Assistance for the Development activities in the District of Hambantota, under the ‘Wewak Samaga Gamak’ Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - The Government of India has agreed to provide a grant of Rs.300 million to Sri Lanka, for the development of fisheries and other livelihood development activities associated with the District of Hambantota.  It is expected to use a  portion of the said grant, under the ‘Wewak Samaga Gamak’ Programme, for the development of model fishing villages. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Mahinda Amaraweera, the Minister of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources Development, to sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Republic of India, to provide support assistance for the livelihoods of the fishing and agricultural communities in the Hambantota District, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Transferring of Government Pilgrims Rest Building constructed under the Matale Aluvihara Sacred Site Planning Scheme to the Matale Aluvihara Temple
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - With a view to providing lodging facilities for the pilgrims who visit the Matale area, the responsibility for the upkeep and maintenance of the Matale Pilgrims' Rest Building constructed by the Government under the Matale Aluvihara Sacred Site Planning Scheme had been vested with the Aluvihara Rajamaha Vihara for a period of 05 years from the year 2009.  Accordingly, with a view to providing facilities for the pilgrims who visit the said Viharaya, the proposal made by Hon. Patali Champika Ranawaka, the Minister of Megapolis and Western Development, to vest the responsibility for the upkeep and maintenance of the said Pilgrims' Rest Building with the Aluvihara Rajamaha Vihara, for a further period of 05 years, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Allocation of funds for the completion of partially completed projects
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Patali Champika Ranawaka, the Minister of Megapolis and Western Development, to obtain provision of Rs.516.8 million required to complete the projects being implemented by the Urban Development Authority (UDA), which are currently at a standstill, such as the construction of Battaramulla- Polduwa By-Pass Road, improvement of the drainage system in the Imaduwa Town, construction of Trade Complexes of Tangalle and Angunukolapelessa, Middeniya Town Development programme; and the projects for the construction of Lunugamvehera and Walasmulla Bus Stands implemented by the District Secretariat Hambantota and to complete the balance work of such projects through the original contractors themselves, with a view to providing benefits to the people of the areas concerned, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Agreement between Sri Lanka and Georgia on Visa Exemption for Holders of Diplomatic and Official Passports
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - With a view to furthering the friendship between the two countries and to improving diplomatic and official tour facilities, the proposal made by Hon. S.B. Navinne, the Minister of Internal Affairs, Wayamba Development and Cultural Affairs, to enter into an agreement between Sri Lanka and Georgia on Visa Exemption for Holders of Diplomatic and Official Passports, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Liberalization of Bitumen Trade
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23

description: Liberalization of Lubricant Industry
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23

description: Federation of Asian Bishops’ Conference
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - The Federation of Asian Bishops whose headquarters is located in Hong Kong works to ensure that there is a proper coordination among the Catholic Community in activities related to Catholics in the Asian Countries. The Committee Meeting of this Federation is held once in four years and it has been planned to hold a meeting this time in Negambo from 28th November to 4th December, 2016.  Eight (08) Cardinals and over one hundred and fifty (150) Bishops representing all countries in Asia are scheduled to participate in that meeting. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. John Amarathunga, the Minister of Tourism Development and Christian Religious Affairs, for the Government to provide its contribution to hold that meeting in Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Strengthening the Secretariat for Coordinating Reconciliation Mechanisms
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-23
decision_details_body: - With a view to effectively implementing the decisions, programmes and processes related to the reconciliation process, the 'Secretariat for Coordinating  Reconciliation Mechanisms (SCRM)' was established towards the end of year 2015, in accordance with a Cabinet decision. The SCRM is tasked with the design and implementation of Sri Lanka's reconciliation mechanisms. Furthermore, this Secretariat acts within the Sri Lanakan reconciliation process as the intermediary body that facilitates between policy makers and policy implementers.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Ranil Wickramasinghe, the Prime Minister, to obtain human resources and funds required for this office, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of a community based power generation programme known as 'Soorya Bala Sangramaya' (the Battle for Solar Energy generation)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-16
decision_details_body: - Presently about 50% of the electricity in Sri Lanka is generated through   renewable energy  sources and the Government anticipates to increase that production up to 60% by the year 2020 and up to 70% by the year 2030.  Accordingly, it will be necessary to construct Wind Power Plants of about 600 MW and Solar Energy Plants of about 3,000 MW within the next 10 years.  In this process, it has been planned to implement a small solar power plant promotion programme known as 'Soorya Bala Sangramaya' (the Battle for Solar Energy generation), with the participation of electricity consumers and electricity producers,  especially through construction of small solar panels on the roof tops of houses.  Under this programme, it is expected to convert at least 20% of electricity consumers to be electricity producers and make payments for the excess electricity so generated.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Ranjith Siyambalapitiya, the Minister of Power and Renewable Energy, to implement this project as a national programme, within the next 10 years, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining Development Proposals for enhancement and upgrading of the Institute of Engineering Technology at Katunayake
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-16
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet has already granted its approval for the project on upgrading  the Institute of Engineering Technology at Katunayake and accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Mahinda Samarasinghe, the Minister of Skills Development and Vocational Training, to obtain development proposals from the institution recommended by the Government of Austria which provides funds for the purpose, as the suitable supplier for the implementation of the project, to appoint a Technical Evaluation Committee (TEC) and a Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (CAPC) to evaluate said development proposals and to implement this project within a maximum cost of Euro 9.5 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of the Building No.54 at the  Katukurunda Training School of the Special Task Force as a two storied building
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-16
decision_details_body: - The Training School at Katukurunda functions as the main training school of the Special Task Force functioning under the Sri Lanka Police Department.  A number of trainings such as training on VIP security, training on Riots Control, training on Search and Bomb Disposal are being carried out in this Training School.  In addition, training is also provided for both local and foreign groups of security personnel.  The building which is presently used to provide hostel facilities for the officers who are engaged in training at this Training School is very old and can provide accommodation facilities for only 100 officers.  As such, in order to enable the school to provide hostel facilities to 200 trainee officers at a time, the proposal made by Hon. Sagala Ratnayake, the Minister of Law & Order and Southern Development, to construct a new two storied building with modern facilities, for the Katukurunda Training School of the Special Task Force, at an estimated cost of Rs.101.49 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining Additional Financing for the Local Government Enhancement Sector  Project (Pura Neguma) Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-16
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Faiszer Musthapha, the Minister of Provincial Councils and Local Government, to take action for the provision of safe drinking water to the relevant areas in the districts of Anuradhapura and Polonnaruwa in the North Central Province, Matale district in the Central Province, districts of Badulla and Moneragala in the Uva Province and districts of Puttalam and Kurunegala in the North Western Province, where the Chronic Kidney Disease (CKDu) is mostly prevalent, to improve the infrastructure facilities and the basic service delivery at Provincial Levels on priority basis and to maintain the reforms and capacity building activities of all the Local Government Authorities which fall within the purview of the project, at a sustainable level, under the Local Government Enhancement Sector Project, at an investment of US$ 67.84 million provided by the Asian Development Fund (ADF) and the Government of Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Cultural Cooperation Agreement between the French Republic and the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-16
decision_details_body: - The joint proposal made by Hon. S.B. Navinne, the Minister of Internal Affairs, Wayamba Development and Cultural Affairs and Hon. Akila Viraj Kariyawasam, the Minister of Education, to enter into an agreement between the Ministry of Culture and Communication of the French Republic and the Ministry of Internal Affairs, Wayamba Development and Cultural Affairs and the Ministry of Education of the Democratic, Socialist, Republic of Sri Lanka, for the cooperation in the field of cultural heritage in order to exchange the knowledge and experiences in the fields of architectural heritage, preservation  of archaeological sites and Museums of Sri Lanka and France, to enable Sri Lanka to obtain the assistance of new technology and experts in France in order to address the shortcomings prevailing in the field of Archaeology and Museums, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Helanco Hotels & SPA (Pvt) Ltd - Reduction of Stated Capital
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-16
decision_details_body: - A sum of Rs.18.5 billion was invested by Sri Lanka Insurance Corporation,  Employees Provident Fund (EPF) and Litro Gas Lanka Ltd., in the equity of Canwill Holdings (Pvt) Ltd., for the purpose of construction of Grand Hyatt Colombo Hotel through its fully owned subsidiary Sinolanka Hotels & Spas (Pvt) Ltd. and the construction works of the hotel were commenced in the year 2012.  While its construction activities were being done, having made a decision to invest Rs.4 billion to construct another hotel called 'Hyatt Regency' in Hambantota area, under the Helanco Hotels & SPA (Pvt) Ltd. which is affiliated to the said company, a sum of about Rs.315 million has been spent for the purpose, although no such construction activities had taken place.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Kabir Hashim, the Minister of Public Enterprise Development, to invest the funds set apart for the  construction works of the 'Hyatt Regency' Hotel, for the balance construction work of the Grand Hyatt Colombo Hotel, was approved by the Cabinet. It was also decided to take action to examine into the  matters pertaining to the use of funds of the public institutions for commercial enterprises outside their basic objectives.

description: Provision of New Infrastructure Facilities for the Regional Courts
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-16
decision_details_body: - Most of the Magistrate Courts and District Courts located in provincial areas / out of Colombo are housed in very old buildings with minimum facilities and due to that reason it has become difficult to conduct   the process of administration of justice without obstructions.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Wijayadasa Rajapaksa, the Minister of Justice, to construct new buildings for Courts situated in the areas of  Gampola, Ruwanwella, Mullaitivu and Passara and also to establish a Circuit Magistrate's Court at Mankulam, at an estimated cost of Rs.1,172 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Re-development of the Chilaw Fishery Harbour
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-16
decision_details_body: - The re-development of the Fishery Harbour at Chilaw, situated near the estuary of the Deduru Oya, is a long awaited request made by the fishermen of the area and accordingly, its renovation work is now being carried out.  Presently, 1,110 OFRP and 35 Multi-Day Boats are engaged in deep sea and coastal fishing around the fishery harbour at Chilaw and  the lagoon basin is used as an anchorage by such boats. The main issue at stake here is that when the boats are sailing through the estuary of the Deduru Oya, as an entrance channel, such boats fall into a vulnerable position.  Especially, during the time of rough seas, many losses of lives and property have been caused due to boat accidents that took place around the estuary area.  As a result, fishing activities of the people have been limited to the period in which the calm sea conditions prevail.  As a remedial measure, construction of a breakwater and the removal of sand deposited in the area associated with the access channel and the estuary should be done, as recommended by a feasibility study made in this regard, and accordingly the proposal made by Hon. Mahinda Amaraweera, the Minister of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources Development, to obtain funds of  Rs.550 million required for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development Project on Stage II of the Public Bus Stand at Anamaduwa
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-16
decision_details_body: - Anamaduwa town is a service centre which serves many agricultural based rural areas in the Puttlam District.  Especially, the service provided through the Anamadurwa town as a sales centre for the agricultural products produced in the surrounding areas and as a service centre for   supplying of input goods to a large catchment area is remarkable. The Anamaduwa Bus Stand is located in the centre of the town and provides transport facilities to around 15,000 passengers daily.  The Anamaduwa Bus Stand Development Project is identified as a priority project under the Anamaduwa Draft Development Plan and its construction works have been commenced in the year 2012 with Provincial Council funding and a part of construction has been completed. Since this project is implemented mainly for the upliftment of the quality of urban facilities, in order to benefit the public, the proposal made by Hon. Patali Champika Ranawaka, the Minister of Megapolis and Western Development, to complete the balance works of the project by the Urban Development Authority (UDA) and to get a provision of  Rs.25 million allocated for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: National Policy on Durable Solutions for Conflict-Affected Displacement
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-16
decision_details_body: - It is essential to have a national policy on durable solutions for conflict-affected displacement.  As such, the National Policy on Durable Solutions for Conflict-Affected Displacement has been developed as a result of an extensive consultation conducted with the relevant Ministries, national, provincial and district level stakeholders, UN agencies, civil society organizations and the displaced communities. The policy underlines the Government's commitment to rebuild the lives of the conflict-affected families using a rights-based approach. The policy emphasizes that ensuring durable solutions goes beyond resettlement, encompassing safety and security, access to housing, water sanitation and health-care and primary education, acquiring a decent standard of living, and  access to livelihoods etc,. Further, when integrating such families into society,  durable solutions should be provided enabling them to enjoy the same rights as other citizens, irrespective of gender, ethnicity, age, language, political belief, religion, cast or place of displacement, etc.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. D. M. Swaminathan, the Minister of Prison Reforms, Rehabilitation, Resettlement and Hindu Religious Affairs, to adopt the above National Policy, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Permission under Section 22(4) of the Exchange Control Act for Remittance of Export Proceeds
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-16
decision_details_body: -  In terms of the provisions of  the Exchange Control Act, export proceeds should be repatriated to Sri Lanka, within a period of 90 days from the date of exportation of goods. Taking into consideration the requests made by the respective stakeholders, the proposal made by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, to extend that  period up to 120 days, with effect from 01st of August 2016 and to grant a grace period of 30 days from the completion of 120 days, prior to initiating legal action, was approved by the cabinet.

description: Holding of the Second Global Health Consultation on Migration Health from 25th to 28th October 2016, in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-16
decision_details_body: - H.E the President Maithripala Sirisena, recognizing the importance of conducting a global consultation on Migration Health for the second time, has proposed to conduct the second session on Migration Health, in Sri Lanka, with the objective of emphasizing the important common issues in protection of Migration Health that should be addressed by the global community.  Accordingly, the proposal made by (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine, to conduct the Second Global Health Consultation on Migration Health from 25th to 28th October 2016, in Sri Lanka, with the participation of about 40 countries, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Developing an integrated Rural Development Mechanism
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-16
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Prime Minister, Ranil Wickremasinghe, in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs, to establish a Steering Committee comprising of Secretaries to the Ministries of National Policies and Economic Affairs; Finance; Home Affairs; Rural Economy; Provincial Council and Local Government or their representatives, for the to implementation of an integrated rural development mechanism, avoiding shortcomings such as the lack of coordination, duplication of work, overlapping of functions that may arise in implementing the Rural Infrastructure Development projects by various Ministries, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining the Services of Retired Technical Officers of the Three Armed Forces for the Development Programmes implemented under the Ministry of National Policies and Economic Affairs
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-16
decision_details_body: - Two major Rural Infrastructure Development Programmes are being implemented under the Ministry of National Policies and Economic Affairs, covering all the districts in the country.  In addition to the said projects, various other projects are also being implemented by various Ministries through  the District Secretariats.  Although, the services of about 700 Technical Officers at District and Divisional Secretariat level, are required for the preparation of  project estimates and monitoring of the projects which are presently being implemented, only about 300 Technical Officers are presently employed in service and that has imposed a constraint on the completion of the said projects within the specified period. Therefore, with a view to duly complete the rural development projects, presently being implemented islandwide, the proposal made by Hon. Prime Minister Ranil Wickremasinghe, in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs, to obtain the services of Technical Officers retired from the Three Armed Forces, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of an Internationally recognized Standard for Plugs and Socket Outlets
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-16
decision_details_body: - In terms of the provisions of the Sri Lanka Electricity Act, No. 20 of 2009, the Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL) is required to take action to protect the public from dangers that may arise from the generation, transmission, distribution, supply or use of electricity. The deaths reported in Sri Lanka in the year 2012, due to accidental electrocution were 180 and it is a very high figure when compared with the international indexes. The Commission has implemented various awareness campaigns and a number of direct interventions to minimize the number of deaths occurred due to electrocution, as much as possible, by the year 2020. Accordingly, the number of deaths by accidental electrocution was reduced down to 77 in the year 2015.  The use of numerous types of plugs and sockets, sub‑standard electrical equipment,   adapters and extension cords has been identified as the major cause for the electrocutions and fires. Therefore, taking into consideration the views expressed by the general public, professionals and other relevant institutions, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister, Ranil Wickremasinghe, in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies  and Economic Affairs, to adopt the internationally recognized type G as the unique and single standard for the plugs and socket outlets in Sri Lanka hereafter and to allow all existing wiring, as well as plugs and sockets presently in use or sold within the next two years, which do not comply with said standards to remain in service, until the end of their useful life, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Providing Solutions for the problems emerged with the regulations / control of the use of chemicals affecting the Ozone Layer
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-16
decision_details_body: - The Government of Sri Lanka has taken action for the gradual removal of the ozone depleting substances from use and for the introduction of ozone friendly alternative substances and technologies, in terms of the provisions of Vienna Convention and Montreal Protocol on protection of the ozone layer.  Accordingly, methodologies to limit the import of  Hydrochloroflurocarbons (HCFCs) chemicals, which have a direct impact on global warming and an import quota system were introduced in the year 2013.  As a result, availability of these chemical substances in the market has been limited and this could have an adverse impact on the services and maintenance work carried out utilizing these substances, especially on the refrigeration and air conditioning sector. Therefore, the proposal made by H. E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to appoint a Committee comprising of the representatives of the relevant Ministries, Departments and agencies, to review the proposals, presented as short term and long term solutions to bring the situation under control and submit  recommendations to the Cabinet, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The Project on conservation of degraded agricultural lands in the Districts of Kandy, Badulla and Nuwara Eliya
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-16
decision_details_body: - The damages caused to land or 'Land Degradation', is caused due to  diverse factors including soil erosion, and it has become a serious environmental issue prevailing in Sri Lanka. More than 50% of the agricultural lands in the Central Highlands have been subject to degradation and the highest rates of degradation could be seen in the districts of Kandy, Badulla and Nuwara Eliya. Due to this reason, having taken into consideration the adverse effects caused to the ecosystem and especially, to the farming community whose livelihood has been agriculture, the attention of the Government has been focused towards preventing this situation through sustainable land management. Accordingly, the proposal made by H. E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to implement a project for the prevention of land degradation of the agricultural lands in the districts of Kandy, Badulla and Nuwara Eliya, during the period of 2016-2020, utilizing the funds of US$ 9,740,000 provided by the Government of Sri Lanka and the Grant of US$ 1,344,657 provided to Sri Lanka through the Food and Agriculture Organization, by the Global Environmental Facility (GEF), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Granting of State Lands to the Landless War Heroes
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-16
decision_details_body: - Various Welfare projects were implemented in accordance with the state policy of looking after the deceased, missing and disabled war heroes of the Tri Forces, the Police Department and the Civil Security Department, who were engaged in active service to defend the sovereignty of Sri Lanka.  Accordingly, the policy of granting a block of land for them for their settlement, in terms of the State Land Ordinance is being already implemented and the proposal made by H. E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Defence, to provide further relief to the war heroes who contributed immensely to the successful conclusion of operations, making necessary amendments to the methodology of granting State lands, to overcome the existing shortcomings, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Proposed amendments to the Regulation of Insurance Industry	Act, No. 43 of 2000
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-01
decision_details_body: - The Insurance Board of Sri Lanka (IBSL) was established by the Regulation of Insurance Industry Act, No. 43 of 2000, to facilitate the development, supervision and regulation of the Insurance Industry in Sri Lanka and the said Act was amended thereafter by the Acts of No. 27 of 2007 and No. 03 of 2011. Cabinet approval was granted in the year 2013 to make some amendments including changing the name 'Insurance Board of Sri Lanka' to the 'Insurance Regulatory Commission of Sri Lanka' and accordingly the draft Amendment Bill for the purpose has been prepared by the Legal Draftsman. Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, to instruct the Legal Draftsman to proceed with finalizing the above Amendment Bill, incorporating the further amendments recommended by the Insurance Board of Sri Lanka, in order to enable the local and foreign Insurance Companies to function on a level playing field, and to submit the draft Bill so prepared to Parliament, after obtaining the clearance of the Attorney General for same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of Short Term Priority Water Supply Improvements 	in Matara District
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-01
decision_details_body: - Two separate water supply schemes each for the Matara and Weligama Municipal / Urban Council areas and Pradeshiya Sabha areas in Matara district are being implemented and the capacity of the said two water supply schemes is insufficient to meet the daily increasing consumer demand. With a view to providing a solution to this situation, it has been decided to implement the 'Matara Stage IV Water Supply Project' and the said project will be completed in the year 2019. Until then, with a view to introducing short term expeditious solutions to the issues existing in the Matara and Weligama Water Supply Schemes in the Matara district,  the proposal made by Hon. Rauff Hakeem, the Minister of City Planning  & Water Supply, to implement the tasks related to the improvement of the production capacity of the Malimbada and Halalla Water Treatment Plants (WTPs), at an estimated cost of Rs.477 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Granting of Loans for Small and Medium Enterprise (SME)	Sector Development and Employment Generation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-01
decision_details_body: - A sum of Rs.19,875 million has been allocated through  the Budget - 2016, for the Rural Awakening Programme which has been designed to develop all Grama Niladhari Divisions of the country, by enhancing the livelihood and infrastructure facilities throughout the country. Therefore, the proposal made by the Prime Minister, Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe, in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs, to implement a programme named 'Small and Medium Enterprise (SME) Sector Development and Employment Generation', to implement a suitable loan scheme for the SME Sector, with a view to generating more and more employment opportunities therein, using Rs. 4,000 million out of the provisions so allocated, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Reconstruction / restoration of war damaged temples and places 	of worship in Northern and Eastern Provinces
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-01
decision_details_body: - A large number of temples/places of worship of historical and cultural importance in the provinces of North and East, have been damaged due to long drawn out conflict that prevailed in the said provinces, and requests have been made to grant the reconstruction activities of such temples/places of worship, directly to the Boards of Trustees of the temples/places of worship in such provinces, without following the tender procedure. Cabinet noted the information submitted by the Prime Minister, Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe, in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs, to the effect that action has been taken to grant the reconstruction/restoration activities of the war damaged temples/places of worship in the Northern	and Eastern Provinces, directly to the Board of Management/Trustees of the relevant temple/place of worship, under the direct supervision of the relevant District Secretaries and Divisional Secretaries, having considered the nature of such reconstruction activities and the material and financial aid received from diverse local and foreign sources as well as the contribution of labour for the purpose.

description: Establishment of Human Resource Services Agency (HRSA)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-01
decision_details_body: - The approval of the Cabinet has already been granted for the incorporation of the Human Resource Services Agency under the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007, in accordance with the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister, for the establishment of the HRSA, with a view to obtaining the services of the professionals to the Government, for the formulation of national policies and efficient implementation of the development programmes.  Accordingly, the proposal made by the Prime Minister, Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe, in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs, to obtain a grant of Rs. 5 million from the Consolidated Fund to meet the initial capital requirement of the said Agency and to seek covering approval for obtaining the assistance of a Private Legal Firm, for the activities related to the  incorporation of such Agency, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of the Tri Forces Central Ammunition Armoury and Commercial Explosive Armoury Complex in a low density 	area
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-01
decision_details_body: - The explosive ammunition used for the operational activities in the Northern and Eastern territories during the period of the army missions in the said areas, have been stored in different places temporarily and the approval of the Cabinet had been granted in the year 2011, to construct  an armoury complex in a low density area, in accordance with the international standards, for the storage of the ammunition in an appropriate manner. Since it would be appropriate to store explosives at a place with a minimal population, the proposal made by H. E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Defence, to establish a formal armoury complex in Oyamaduwa area in the District of Anuradhapura, in accordance with the international standards, for the storage of explosives belonging to the Tri Forces and commercial explosives, which are being currently stored at different places, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Granting of State Land on Long Term Lease towards the Construction of a 'Resource Centre' for the Sri Lanka Administrative Service (SLAS) Officers
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-01
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by the Prime Minister, Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe, to grant a block of land located in Battaramulla area, to the Sri Lanka Administrative Service Association (SASA), for the construction of a Resource Centre for the officers of the Sri Lanka Administrative Service (SLAS), which is recognized as the premier and most important  public service involved in the process of implementing public policies at National, Provincial and Regional levels, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Port City Development Project/The Proposed Finance City Project - Changes suggested to the Original Agreement signed in September 2014
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-08-01
decision_details_body:
- A summary of the proposed changes to be included in the Original Agreement signed in September, 2014 is given below. 
Freehold land 

*	As per the Original Agreement signed by the previous Government in  September, 2014, 20 hectares of land were to be granted to the CHEC Port City (Pvt).Ltd. (the Project Company) on a freehold basis, with the balance land to be granted on a 99 year lease.

*	According to the new Agreement negotiated by this Government, any freehold land will not be granted and all the lands will be allocated to the Project Company will be granted on a 99 year leasehold basis.  The Project Company may lease out this 20 hectares of land for another 99 years if not required by the Government.
	Role of  Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA) and Urban Development Authority (UDA)

*	The Original Agreement signed by the previous Government required the SLPA Act to be amended so that the SLPA would receive 62 hectares of land from the Project Company for its own use and development.  This is restricted to the objectives of the Ports Authority as stated in Section 6 of the Act. Though at that time the then Government claimed that Sri Lankan land could be used for real estate development, such a grant of powers is not mentioned under Section 6.

*	Under the new Agreement, the SLPA will not undertake real estate development and its responsibilities would be limited to activities dictated under the present SLPA Act.  It was therefore decided that the UDA is the most appropriate authority to whom the reclaimed land would be allocated.
Role of Ministry of Megapolis and Western Development 

*	Under the original agreement the Ministry of  Ports and Shipping undertook to fulfill all obligations of the Government including amending the SLPA Act.

*	The Ministry of Megapolis and Western Development (on behalf of the Government), the UDA, together with the Project Company, will now sign a new Tri Partite Agreement replacing the original agreement signed by the previous Government on 16th September 2014.
Legal status of the land to be reclaimed  

*	Under the Original concessionary agreement signed by the previous Government, the status of the reclaimed land was unclear.  It was not part of the District of Colombo.   Therefore, it did not come under the territory of Sri Lanka under Article 5 of the Constitution.  The new law will make it part of the Administrative District of Colombo and it will come under the Financial City Corporation distinct from the Colombo Municipal Council.
