As a solution to this situation,  the proposal made by Hon. Arjuna Ranathunga, the Minister of Ports and Shipping, to develop and regulate the coastal passenger transportation activities through the Director General of Merchant Shipping and to introduce appropriate  amendments to the Boat Ordinance, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The  Accelerated Programme for the Development of Middle Income 	Housing & Infrastructure
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-21
decision_details_body: - As per the approval granted by the Cabinet, the project proposals have been called for the implementation of the Project of the Development of Middle Income Housing and Infrastructure, in eight (08) plots of land, belonging to the National Housing Development Authority (NHDA), situated in different areas of the Island, with the participation of local and foreign investors and the developers. Accordingly, the Cabinet noted the information/matters submitted by Hon. Sajith Premadasa, the Minister of Housing and Construction, that, it has been recommended by the Steering Committee appointed to implement this project, to implement the housing projects in the areas of Panadura, Homagama (Jalthara Stage II), Yakkala and Ragama and to recall project proposals for the housing projects in the areas of Kundasale, Homagama, Galle and Nittambuwa.

description: Conducting the 3rd Meeting of Expert Group on Natural Rubber 	Price Stabilization of the Association of Natural Rubber Producing 	Countries (ANRPC) in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-21
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Navin Dissanayake, the Minister of Plantation Industries, to facilitate the holding of the 3rd Meeting of the Expert Group on Natural Rubber Price Stabilization of the Association of Natural Rubber Producing Countries, which is an international organization comprising of 11 natural rubber producing member countries, including Sri Lanka, in the year 2016 in Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Recommencement of the Construction Activities of Walasmulla Sathi Pola
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-21
decision_details_body: - The construction work of Walasmulla Sathi Pola, has been completed up to the foundation level and it has been temporarily halted due to non-availability of funds for the project.  Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Patali Champika Ranawaka, the Minister of Megapolis and Western Development, to continue the remaining construction activities of the project, with the assistance of the Construction Unit of Sri Lanka Army, who conducted the preliminary construction activities of the project, subject to an estimated cost of Rs.50 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining Technical Assistance for the Implementation of Weliwita Water Supply Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-21
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Rauff Hakeem, the Minister of City Planning and Water Supply, to obtain technical assistance of the International Finance Corporation (IFC) of the World Bank Group for the construction of the Weliwita Water Supply Project, which is the first ever water supply project constructed in Sri Lanka under the Public - Private Partnership Basis, and to appoint a Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC) and a Project Committee for the implementation of the project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of Wastewater Disposal Infrastructure for Chilaw Town and the Puttalam Town and the Wastewater Disposal  System for Maharagama -  Boralesgamuwa Areas
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-21
decision_details_body: - The joint proposal made by Hon. Rauff Hakeem, the Minister of City Planning and Water Supply and Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, to implement the project for the development of Wastewater Disposal Infrastructure for the Chilaw Town and the Puttalam Town and the Wastewater Disposal System for Maharagama -  Boralesgamuwa areas, and to obtain a loan of US$105 million from the EXIM Bank of China on concessionary terms, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment of the Sri Lanka Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka Act
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-21
decision_details_body: - Identifying the challenges and the limits faced by the Sri Lanka Buddhist and Pali University and also with a view to safeguarding the future safety of the University, the proposal made by Hon. Lakshman Kiriella, the Minister of Higher Education and Highways, to amend the the Sri Lanka Buddhist and Pali University Act, No. 37 of 1995, to suit the present global trends, without any prejudice to the objectives of the Act and also to achieve them in a more realistic manner, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: 'Project on Construction of Defence Headquarters Complex at Akuregoda' – (Presenting the Report of the Committee appointed to inquire into the Consultancy Firms and related Payments
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-21
decision_details_body: - The Officials' Committee appointed to investigate into the matter concerning the consultancy firms and the related payments of the Defence Headquarters at Akuregoda, has observed that the Cabinet has not been informed of the accurate facts regarding the selection of consultancy firms and making relevant payments to such firms.  Accordingly, as per the recommendation made by the said Committee, the proposal made by H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, not to obtain the services of the private firm which provided consultancy services for the construction of the project hereafter and to review the consultancy fee made to the said firm, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Strengthening of the Co-ordination between the Provincial Councils and the Line Ministries
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-21
decision_details_body:
- At the commencement of the Cabinet Meeting with the participation of the Chief Ministers of Provinces, the difficulties encountered in  implementing the activities of Provincial Councils efficiently and effectively were discussed and during the discussion attention was paid to  matters such as recruitment of teachers for schools under the Provincial Councils, filling of the vacancies of principals and teachers, the difficulties encountered when obtaining the resources necessary for Provincial Councils and waste disposal management.  Emphasis was also laid on the necessity of implementing development projects with a close co-ordination between the Provincial Councils and the Line Ministries.  

As per the methodology introduced through the 2016 Budget proposals, the budgetary provisions for the Provincial Councils are allocated through the Expenditure Head of the Ministry of Provincial Councils and Local Government.  At the previous Cabinet Meeting held with the participation of the Chief Ministers of Provinces, it had been decided  to adopt the methodology previously followed till the end of the year 2015, instead of the new methodology. Accordingly, the Cabinet granted approval to amend the Appropriation Act, No.16 of 2015, to enable the General Treasury to allocate provisions directly to each Provincial Council.

description: Annual Report of the Ministry of Finance - 2015
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-14
decision_details_body: - In terms of Section 13 of the Fiscal Management (Responsibility) Act, No.03 of 2003, the Minister of Finance is required to submit a Report on the Final Budgetary Position (Annual Report) to Parliament and to the public before 31st of May of the subsequent year.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, to present in Parliament, the Annual Report of the Ministry of Finance for the year 2015, containing the updated information of the Government's Fiscal Position, consisting of 13 Chapters, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Reintroduction of Capital Gains Tax (CGT) Regime
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-14
decision_details_body: - During the last few decades, there has been a massive increase in the private capital of the country. The increase in prices of lands attributable to the large infrastructure developments such as road development carried out through Government funds have enabled the land owners to make significant capital gains free of taxation. This has resulted in an increase in the inequality of income distribution.  In order to rectify this situation, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Management has agreed to reintroduce the Capital Gains Tax and accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe, the Prime Minister, in his capacity as the Chairman of the Cabinet Committee on Economic Management, to draft a New Capital Gains Tax Regime, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding contracts for Eighteen (18) Civil Work Contract Packages in the Provinces of North Central and the North Western and the Kalutara District
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-14
decision_details_body: - The Asian Development Bank funded Integrated Road Investment Programme is implemented with a view to improving the access routes  between rural areas and socio-economic centres.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Lakshman Kiriella, the Minister of Higher Education and Highways, to award the 18 contract packages relevant to the civil work of 18 road sections scheduled to be implemented for the rehabilitation and improvement of rural roads so as to cover all the Districts of North Central and the North Western Provinces and also the Kalutara District, under this programme, as per the recommendation made by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development of Infrastructure Facilities at the Universities of Peradeniya, Kelaniya, Colombo, Jaffna, Rajarata, Visual & Performing Arts, Eastern and the Institute of Agro-Technology and Rural Sciences of the University of Colombo
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-14
decision_details_body: - The Government has given a high priority to develop the available space and infrastructure of the State universities, to fulfill the requirements of the present students and also of the future students who expect to follow the Technology Degrees and other Degree Courses. By the end of the year 2016, it is expected to enroll 1825 students to follow the Technology Degree Courses while the University Grants Commission has taken steps to enroll students at an average annual growth rate of 5 % from the year 2017 onwards. Instructions have already been issued to commence these Degree Courses in future in other Universities as well.  Accordingly, with a view to producing competent graduates to cater to the international job market and the existing development needs in the economy, the proposal made by Hon. Lakshman Kiriella, the Minister of Higher Education and Highways, to improve the infrastructure facilities such as faculty buildings, computer units, libraries and research buildings in 08  universities, at an estimated cost of Rs.484 million in the year 2016, Rs.3,381 million and Rs.1,074 million in the year 2017 and 2018 respectively,  was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The development of the Airport at Palaviya in Puttalam
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-14
decision_details_body: - The availability of an efficient internal air transport system which integrates the entire country with the international airports is essential for a country. In addition to the two international airports available in Sri Lanka at Katunayake and Mattala presently, there are 14 domestic airports of different sizes at Ampara, Anuradhapura, Baticaloa, Hingurakkgoda, Palali, Iranamadu, Koggala, Katukurunda, Palaviya, Ratmalana, Sigiriya, Trincomalee, Weeravila and Vavuniya so as to cover 07 out of the 09 Provinces in the Island.  The Budget - 2016 has proposed  to establish three new domestic airports in the districts of Badulla, Kandy and Puttalam under public-private partnership, especially for the promotion of tourism in such Districts.  With a view  to developing the tourism industry prevalent in the Kalpitiya area which is becoming a tourist destination, simultaneously, the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala de Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, to develop the Palaviya Airport which is currently non-utilized, acquiring a land of  26 hectares in extent, at an estimated cost of Rs.750 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Allocation of Land for Establishment of a Tyre Factory at Gonapola, Horana
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-14
decision_details_body: - The annual income earned by Sri Lanka from the export of Pneumatic and Retreated Rubber Tyres and Tubes amounts to US$ 471 million and that has been accounted as 61.9% of the total rubber exports. Therefore, in order to further enhance the industries in this field, the proposal made by Hon. Malik Samarawickrama, the Minister of Development Strategies and International Trade, to provide necessary facilities to commence a tyre manufacturing plant with a production capacity of 03 million tyres per annum, as a BOI project, with an investment of US$ 75 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Resettlement of Internally Displaced Families reside in the Welfare Centres
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-14
decision_details_body: - It is noted that by the end of March 2016, 251,000 internally displaced families who were affected by the conflict have been resettled in the  Northern and Eastern Provinces.  However, there are over 14,000 families yet to be resettled in those areas.  Presently, 1,109 displaced families reside in the 31 welfare centres in the Tellippalai Divisional Secretary's Division and it is reported that 641 families out of these families are landless. In regard to the resettlement of these landless families, the District Secretary, Jaffna has identified 65 hectares of land belonging to the Kankasanthurai Cement Corporation. Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. D.M. Swaminathan, the Minister of Prison Reforms, Rehabilitation, Resettlement and Hindu Religious Affairs, to release the above mentioned land identified for the purpose of resettling 400 landless families residing welfare centres at Tellippalai and to transfer the said land in favour of the Government, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Provincial Councils Elections Act, No.02 of 1988
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-14
decision_details_body: - According to the present Government's policy towards the increase of  female representation at least by 25% in the political decision making process, the proposal made by Hon. Faiszer Musthapha, the Minister of Provincial Councils and Local Government, to publish the Provincial Councils Elections (Amendment) Bill prepared to incorporate provisions in the Provincial Councils Elections Act, No.02 of 1988 to include not less than 30% of the total number of candidates whose names appear in the nomination paper submitted by each political party or independent group in respect of each Provincial Council to consist of female  candidates, in the Government Gazette and thereafter, to present the same in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Allocation of Land for Construction of the Approach Road to the Dedicated Economic Centre at Veyangoda from the Veyangoda Town
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-14
decision_details_body: - The Dedicated Economic Centre at Veyangoda established in the year 2007 consists of 70 business units and 06 stores and it is a highly important business centre for the trade and consumer community of the area.  Since the present approach road for the Dedicated Economic Centre is situated at a considerable distance from the Veyangoda Town, the consumers are reluctant to visit the Centre and also as there is no approach road to the Centre from the Nittambuwa - Katunayake Main Road, which runs close to the Centre, the lorry owners who use the said road for the transportation of vegetables and other items from various places such as Dambulla, Welimada, Nuwara-Eliya are also reluctant to come to the Centre. This state of affairs has adversely affected the development of the Centre and therefore, to avoid this situation, the joint proposal made by Hon. Rishad Bathiudeen, the Minister of Industry and Commerce and Hon. P. Harison, the Minister of Rural Economy, to allocate the 40 perches of land belonging to the Food Commissioner's Department situated in the area, to construct a convenient approach way  providing direct access to the Economic Centre, from the Katunayake - Nittambuwa Main Road, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Commemoration of 94th International Co-operative Day
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-14
decision_details_body: - The Co-operative Movement can be described as a movement built by the people by themselves for the purpose of enhancing their economic and social well-being. The commemorative activities of the International Co-operative Day have been carried out by the United Nations Organization since 1975.  The International Co‑operative Day of this year falls on 2nd July and as such, the proposal made by Hon. Rishad Bathiudeen, the Minister of Industry and Commerce, to declare a 'Co-operative Week' from 25th June to 2nd July 2016 and to celebrate the Co-operative Day which falls on 2nd July 2016 at the  Nelum Pokuna Theatre, in collaboration with the members of the Movement, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Agreement on Economic Cooperation between the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Republic of Bulgaria
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-14
decision_details_body: - The total trade turnover between Sri Lanka and Bulgaria, which is a  Member State of the European Union has increased up to US$ 7.75 million in the year 2015.  Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Rishad Bathiudeen, the Minister of Industry and Commerce, to sign an Agreement on Economic Cooperation between the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Republic of Bulgaria,  to search for new ways and means to enhance trade, investment and  economic ties between the two countries and to have an inter-governmental mechanism to enhance cooperation between the two countries in identified new fields, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the SAARC Agreement on Trade in Services (SATIS)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-14
decision_details_body: - The Leaders of the Member States, during the  16th SAARC Summit held in Bhutan in 2010 signed the SAARC Framework Agreement on Trade in Services (SATIS), as a further step towards expanding the regional trade to the services sector. To give effect to the Framework Agreement on SATIS, the Schedules of Commitments have to be finalized by the Individual Member Countries.  Sri Lanka falls within the Category-I, namely the Category of non Least Developed Countries and accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Rishad Bathiudeen, the Minister of Industry and Commerce, to include new areas of operatorless Rental/Leasing Services relating to ships and land transport in the Schedules of Commitments, in addition to the areas of Communications Services, Financial Services and Tourism and Travel related Services to which Sri Lanka has already agreed in the Doha Round of World Trade Organization and to open such services under the SATIS Agreement and to make necessary requests to the relevant Government Institutions, for the implementation of the Agreement, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Project for Computerization of subjects of the Department of Labour for enhancing transparency and efficiency of its activities
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-14
decision_details_body: - The responsibility of enforcing service conditions, employment terms and  employee welfare measures enacted by the Government from time to time, in compliance with the charters and recommendations of the International Labour Organization, to safeguard the human rights of employees and also protect them against occupational hazards, lies with the Department of Labour. With a view to computerizing the main subjects of the Department, the activities relating to designing of a computer software (Labour Inspection System Application - LISA) had commenced in the year 2010 with the assistance of the International Labour Organization.  The basic objectives of the above programme are to obtain accurate data, to prevent the occurrence of duplication in inspecting  institutions, to enhance the efficiency and transparency of the Department and to formulate an employee progress review system.  The Cabinet of Ministers noted the information submitted to the Cabinet by Hon. W.D.J. Seneviratne, the Minister of Labour and Trade Union Relations to the effect that after obtaining the staff and the infrastructure facilities necessary, the programme is to be completely undertaken and implemented by the Department of Labour by August 2016.

description: Renovation of the 'Seth Sevana' Government Elders Home at Mirigama and the construction of Water Tank for the Home
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-14
decision_details_body: - The ageing population of Sri Lanka constitutes 12.4% of the total population at present. The ageing population of Sri Lanka is rapidly increasing and it is anticipated that it would exceed 24.8% by the year 2041. When considering the increase of elderly population day by day, it is necessary to provide them with the opportunity of spending their lives with self-respect and dignity. The 'Seth Sevana' Elders Home at Mirigama, in which 265 elders presently reside, was established to commemorate Right Honourable D.S. Senanayake, and it is the largest elders home located in the Western Province and maintained by the Government. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. S.B. Dissanayake, the Minister of Social Empowerment and Welfare, to obtain financial provision for preliminary repairs including the water supply of the Elders Home, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Extradition Treaty between Sri Lanka and Ukraine
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-14
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by H.E the President Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Defence, with the objective of strengthening the cooperation between the two countries on extradition of criminals back to their motherlands, was approved by the Cabinet. This would provide Sri Lanka with the opportunity of requesting the authorities of Ukrain, to transfer the persons who have engaged in illegal acts in the country and sought refuge in Ukraine.

description: Housing Development Programme for families suffering from renal failure and living in abject poverty
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-07
decision_details_body: - The Joint proposal made by H. E. the President Maithripala Sirisena and Hon. Sajith Premadasa, the Minister of Housing and Construction, to initiate and implement a Housing Programme with the basic infrastructure facilities for the families suffering from renal failure and living in  abject poverty, in view of the 'National Housing Week' commencing from the National Housing Day which falls on 23rd June, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Disposal of garbage accumulated in certain areas of the Western Province due to the recent floods
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-07
decision_details_body: - Hon. Faiszer Musthapha, the Minister of Provincial Councils and Local Government informed the Cabinet that the Joint Mission Programme initiated to dispose the garbage accumulated in certain areas of the Western Province expeditiously, including the Kolonnawa Divisional Secretariat Division, due to   recent floods, in collaboration with the Sri Lanka Army, Civil Security Department, Provincial Council of Western Province, Local Government Authorities, Department of Agrarian Development and Sri Lanka Land Reclamation & Development Corporation, was implemented successfully during the past 7 days disposing of around 5,440 Tons of garbage, during the period and that it has been decided to extend the implementation period of the above Joint Mission Programme up to 2016-06-12, as around 2,000 Tons of accumulated garbage is yet to be disposed.

description: Memorandum of Understanding for Cooperation between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Turkey on Diplomatic Training, Exchange of Information and Documentation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-07
decision_details_body: - The objective of entering into the above agreement is to  strengthen and consolidate the close and friendly relations between Sri Lanka and  Turkey, through the development of mutually beneficial cooperation on diplomatic training, the exchange of information and documentation on international law and other academic disciplines that are relevant to the practice of diplomacy and international relations, in the spheres of political, economic, cultural or otherwise. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Mangala Samaraweera, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, to enter into the above  Memorandum of Understanding between the Foreign Ministry of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Foreign Ministry of the Republic of Turkey, during the forthcoming visit of Hon. Mevlut Cavusoglu, the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Turkey to Sri Lanka in June 2016, pertaining to diplomatic training and exchange of information and documentation, was  approved by the Cabinet.

description: Registration of Deaths and Missing Persons
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-07
decision_details_body: - A necessity has arisen to provide for the Registration of Persons who are missing and their whereabouts unknown, especially those who are reported missing in the course of, consequent to, or in connection with the conflict in the Northern and Eastern provinces and/or its aftermath or in connection with the political unrest, and/or civil disturbances, and due to enforced disappearances. Such registration and issuance of 'Certificates of Absence' to the relatives of such missing persons will enable their relatives  to manage the properties and assets of the missing person, temporarily obtain provisional guardianship of children of the missing person, make applications for the benefits under the social welfare schemes and make representations before the relevant authorities and make requests on behalf of the missing person. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Vajira Abeywardena, the Minister of Home Affairs, to  amend the Registration of Deaths (Temporary Provisions) Act, No.19 of 2010, with a view to issuing the 'Certificates of Absence' regarding missing persons or for the cancellation of the Certificate of Absence in the event of the missing person being found to be alive or deceased or the  issuance of a certificate of death with regard to the person concerned, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Consultancy Services for Design Review and Construction Supervision of Civil Works on Extension of Southern Expressway Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-07
decision_details_body: - The Southern Expressway Extension Project consists of four main sections. The project which is of a total length of 96 km, covers Section one, from Matara to Beliatta (30 km), Section two, from Beliatta to Wetiya (26 km), Section three, from Wetiya to Andarawewa (15 km) and Section four, from Mattala to Hambantota via Andarawewa (25 km). The Government has already entered into four (04) Agreements with the China EXIM Bank to obtain funds for the four (04) civil work contracts involved in all the stages of this project and the proposal made by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, to enter into a Framework Agreement with the Government of People's Republic of China and a Loan Agreement with the China EXIM Bank to finance the consultancy services for the supervision of civil works of the project and design review, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Purchasing of 42,000 Metric Tons of Urea by the two State Fertilizer Companies
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-07
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Duminda Dissanayake, the Minister of Agriculture, to purchase 42,000 Metric Tons of Urea through the two State Fertilizer Companies,  to continuously address the fertilizer requirements of the farmer community of the country, at a reasonable price, as per the recommendation of the Special Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of a building containing the operation theatre and ward  in the District General Hospital, Chilaw
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-07
decision_details_body: - The District General Hospital, Chilaw, which is the main hospital in the  Puttalam District of the North Western Province, provides patient care services to the people of Chilaw as well as the people of the surrounding areas. It has been found necessary to demolish the existing deteriorating operating theatre building and construct a modern operating theatre and a ward in the same location, to conduct the surgical work of the hospital in the stipulated manner and therefore, Hon. (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition & Indigenous Medicine informed the Cabinet to the effect that the Contract for the purpose has been awarded to the State Development & Construction Corporation.

description: Southern Transport Development Project - Contract Package No.1 - Construction of Section from Pinnaduwa to Kodagoda (30.80 to 45.00 km) -  utilization of the balance amount of the loan
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-07
decision_details_body: - Steps have been taken to rehabilitate 11 local roads, coming under  the project, by utilizing the balance amount of the loan received from the China EXIM Bank, for the construction of the South section of the Southern Expressway, from Pinnaduwa to Godagama and having taken into  consideration that the period of validity of the loan will expire within a limited time,  the proposal made by Hon. Lakshman Kiriella, the Minister of Higher Education and Highways, to manage the required funds with a view to completing the said road rehabilitation activities, expeditiously, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Provision of Gift Vouchers instead of Clothing Material for School Uniforms - 2017
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-07
decision_details_body: - For the first time, provision of gift vouchers instead of clothing material for school uniforms was implemented at the end of the school term in December in the year 2015. Parents were able to provide their children with school uniform material with the stipulated standard and quality as the Government anticipated and thus save the cost and time incurred by the Government previously, on storing, packing, transporting and quality controlling of the school uniform material. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Akila Viraj Kariyawasam, the Minister of Education, to add a reasonable additional amount to the vouchers, in consideration of the increase of the market prices of clothes, based on the past year experiences and to pass the benefit over to the students in the Government schools and Government assisted schools and the student Bhikkus and lay students in the Government approved pirivenas and to continue to implement the programme in the same manner, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Policy Framework and National Plan of Action to address Sexual and Gender-based Violence (SGBV)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-07
decision_details_body: - The Government has given priority to the enactment and enforcement of new laws for elimination of abuse and violence against women and children. Accordingly, the policy framework and the action plan to address gender-based violence,  drafted under 09 fields, namely child affairs, disaster management, education, economic development and employment, foreign employment, empowerment and prevention, health, justice and law reforms and media, with the views and concurrence of Public Institutions, International and local Non-Governmental organizations, Community based organizations and representatives of the Civil organizations, presented to the Cabinet by Hon. (Mrs.) Chandrani Bandara, the Minister of Women and Child Affairs, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of Mundeni Aru River Basin Development Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-07
decision_details_body: - The development project proposed to be implemented in relation to Mundeni Aru River Basin, which is considered a River Basin where the water resources are mostly underutilized, located in the South-East region of Sri lanka, covers the districts of Ampara and Batticaloa in the Eastern Province. Under this project it is expected to increase the  extent of the present cultivable area of 3,950 hectares after constructing  the  two multi-purpose reservoirs with a capacity of 75 million Cubic Meters and 80 million Cubic Meters respectively across Galodai Aru and Mahaoya and to provide fresh irrigation water to 2,800 hectares. Amalgamation of the Rugamwewa - Kithulwewa is also included in the project and flood control, generation of hydro electricity and providing of drinking water to 44 Grama Niladhari Divisions in the Batticaloa district will also be done  under this project. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Vijith Vijayamuni Zoysa, the Minister of Irrigation and Water Resources Management, to implement the Mundeni Aru River Basin Project utilizing local and foreign funds, was approved by the Cabinet, as a matter of principle.

description: Kumbukkan Oya Reservoir Project in Monaragala District
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-07
decision_details_body: - Use of the fertile lands and water resources productively in the Monaragala district, which still is a backward district, for the benefit of the people, would cause to eliminate the poverty in the area. A reservoir with a capacity of 48 million Cubic Meters will be built across Kumbukkan Oya reservoir through the above project and it is expected to provide irrigation for 4,280 hectares of new lands in Buttala, Monaragala and Siyambalanduwa areas and for 1,255 hectares of agricultural lands already cultivated.  It would also pave the way for providing drinking water to Monaragala, Nakkala, Kumbukkana, Okkampitiya and Buttala areas and generate electricity, as well. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Vijith Vijayamuni Zoysa, the Minister of Irrigation and Water Resources Management, to implement the Kumbukkan Oya Reservoir Project by obtaining funds locally as well as from foreign countries, was approved by the Cabinet, as a matter of Principle.

description: Lower Malwathu Oya Reservoir Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-07
decision_details_body: - The implementation of the proposed Lower Malwathu Oya Reservoir Project, would directly benefit the people in the districts of Anuradhapura, Vavuniya and Mannar and it would pave the way for the successful cultivation of 12,425 hectares of arable land in the Yodha Weva and Akathimuruppu Irrigation Scheme of Mannar in both Yala and Maha Seasons where no proper irrigation facilities are available. The Environmental Assessment Report and the Archaeological Evaluation Report of the project  are presently being reviewed and the plans are afoot for resettling of 160 low-income families living in the project area. Since the project has been identified as a very productive investment according to the feasibility study report of the project and as such, the joint proposal made by Hon. Vijith Vijayamuni Zoysa, the Minister of Irrigation and Water Resources Management and Hon. Duminda Dissanayake, the Minister of Agriculture, to implement the Lower Malwathu Oya Reservoir Project expeditiously, in order to increase the food production of Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet, as a matter of principle.

description: Provide relief for the people who are affected by Moragahakanda - Kaluganga Development Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-06-07
decision_details_body: - Moragahakanda - Kaluganga Development Project which was commenced in the year 2007 as a Mahaweli Development project, with the objective of providing a solution for the shortage of water which affects the agricultural activities in the North Central Province and supplying drinking water for the people living in Anuradhapura, Polonnaruwa, Trincomalee and Matale districts is the largest multipurpose River Valley Development Project being implemented in the Island. Around 65% of its construction activities have already been completed and 2,512 families affected in the Naula and Laggala - Pallegama Divisional Secretariat Divisions due to the acquisition of lands for the project, have to be removed from the area expeditiously, as it has been planned to fill the reservoir with water prior to the start of rain in Maha Season in 2016. Out of them, 984 families have already been compensated and the proposal made by H.E the President Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to grant compensation following a reasonable method for the removal of the remaining 2,228 families affected on account of the project, so as to complete the project as designed, within the stipulated time frame, was approved by the Cabinet, as a matter of principle.

description: Relief Measures to be adopted for the urgent disaster situation arisen 	throughout the Island due to adverse weather conditions
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-17
decision_details_body:
- The heavy rains, winds and the landslides which prevailed in the Island during the previous days have affected 18 districts. According to reports as of 2016-05-16, 128,428 members of 31,062 families have been severely  affected and as a result several people have died and several others have been reported missing. It is also reported that 12 houses totally and 201 houses partially, have been damaged. The welfare centres established island-wide by the National Disaster Management Services Centre are 104 and 77,265 persons belonging to 16,968 families take shelter in them.  Providing of facilities including cooked food  to them have already commenced. Under the National Insurance Programme for Natural Disasters implemented with effect from 2016-04-01, Rs.20 million has been granted to the National Disaster Management Centre through the National Insurance Trust Fund (NITF) and the activities pertaining to the distribution of money required to provide relief  as per  the requests made by the District Secretaries of the Districts where the disastrous situations exist are also being carried out.  

Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Anura Priyadarshana Yapa, the Minister of Disaster Management, to increase the Rs.150/- provided to a person for cooked meals per day during an urgent disaster situation up to Rs.225/- and to allocate additional provision to provide relief for matters which are not covered under the present insurance scheme, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Revision of CESS levied on Export of Rubber
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-17
decision_details_body: - For the purpose of encouraging the consumption of natural rubber produced in Sri Lanka, by the local value added industries, a CESS of around Rs.15/- per kg is charged for export of rubber as raw rubber. Presently, 80% of the natural rubber produced in the country is consumed by the local industrialists while about 20% is exported as raw rubber. Due to the decrease of price of rubber in Sri Lanka, concurrently with the decrease of the price of rubber in the world market, the planters including the small scale rubber estate owners are now in dire straits and it has been predicted  that the existing low price of rubber will prevail until the year 2020. Under the circumstances, with a view to increasing the price of rubber, to provide relief to rubber planters by creating competition between the rubber exporters and the local producers of rubber products  for raw rubber, the proposal made by Hon. Navin Dissanayake, the Minister of Plantation Industries to reduce the CESS  levied on export of raw rubber from  Rs. 15/- to Rs.4/- per kg, in accordance with the recommendation of the Cabinet Committee on Economic Management, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Penal Code to increase the Minimum Age of Criminal Responsibility
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-17
decision_details_body: - The Penal Code of Sri Lanka specifies that nothing is an offence which is committed by a child under eight (08) years of age. However, in accordance with international recognition, the minimum age of criminal responsibility varies from the ages twelve (12) to fourteen (14). The psychiatrists and the experts in the related fields hold the view that the above minimum age limit of 08 years, operating in Sri Lanka, is a far too young age to bear the responsibility of a crime. Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Wijayadasa Rajapaksa, the Minister of Justice, to amend the Penal Code, so as not to impose punishment at the commission of any offence by a child below the age of 12 years and to impose punishment for the respective offence charged in respect of a child above 12 years and below 14 years, only if the Magistrate exercises the discretion that the child has the required degree of cognitive maturity to form the requisite intent to commit such offence, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Holding of the Fourth General Assembly of the Asian Food and Agriculture Cooperation Initiative (AFACI) in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-17
decision_details_body: - The Asian Food and Agriculture Cooperation Initiative (AFACI), which is an International organization, established with the aim of contributing towards the economic development of the Asian regional countries, through the technical co-operation for the sustainable agriculture and agriculture and food production, consists of 14 member countries, at present. This organization provides technical and financial assistance for different agricultural projects in Sri Lanka and presently, under this scheme, 11 research projects are being operated in Sri Lanka. At present, Sri Lanka holds the Chairmanship of this organization and accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Duminda Dissanayake, the Minister of Agriculture, to conduct the fourth General Assembly of the organization, which has been scheduled to be held from 17th to 21st of May 2016, in Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Organizing International Religious Conferences in Sri Lanka in 2016 and 2018
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-17
decision_details_body: - The South Asia and the South East Asia have always been home to a  multi-religious and multi- ethnic population since the past and at present, due to extremist activities, the harmony of this region is threatened.  In this backdrop, the need to build and sustain a thriving dialogue among the different religions, with a view to establishing and strengthening a background that tolerates other cultures and religions, has emerged.  Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister, Ranil Wickremasinghe, to conduct an International Conference on Theravada Buddhism in the year 2018, under the supervision of the Ministries of National Policies and Economic Affairs; Foreign Affairs; and Buddhasasana and to hold the International Conference on Islam and Democracy in South Asia and South East Asia on the 17th, 18th and 19th November, 2016 in Colombo, under the supervision of the Ministries of National Policies and Economic Affairs; Foreign Affairs; and Posts, Postal Services and Muslim Religious Affairs, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Anuradhapura South Phase II Integrated Water Supply Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-17
decision_details_body: - The proposed Anuradhapura South Phase II Integrated Water Supply Project, to be implemented covering Nachchaduwa, Thalawa, Rambawa, Mihinthale, Tirappane small town, pocket areas located in the Anuradhapura Municipal Council area and the Nuwaragampalatha Central and  Nuwaragampalatha East Divisional Secretariat Divisions, will generate benefits to around 280,956 people therein. Hence, the proposal made by Hon. Rauff Hakeem, the Minister of City Planning and Water Supply, to award the Tender relating to the implementation of the Project, as per the recommendation made by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of  a 10MW Solar Power Plant at Vavuniya
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-17
decision_details_body: - It is essential to develop the renewable energy generation, in order to cope with the increasing energy demand. It has been proposed to establish a 10 MW solar power plant at Vavuniya, at an investment of US$ 14.5 million by M/S Vydex (Lanka) Power Corporation (Pvt) Ltd. and it is expected to receive a contribution of 19 Gwh of power to the annual energy requirement. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Malik Samarawickrama, the Minister of Development Strategies and International Trade, to transfer a land in extent of 22 hectares at Kaththarasinna kulam, Nedun kulam, Vavuniya, to the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka, as a free grant, as per the provisions of the State Lands Ordinance, to be leased out to the said company, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Collection of Data on Housing Requirements
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-17
decision_details_body: - The Ministry of Housing and Construction is working on preparing  a long term programme, on the instructions of H.E the President and the Hon. Prime Minister, with a view to fulfilling the national housing requirement, which is a major problem encountered by Sri Lanka.   In the process, it is essential to obtain the accurate and updated information on the housing requirement of Sri Lanka.  As a period of 05 years has already lapsed since the  last census on population and housing was conducted, a survey on housing at District and Divisional levels has to be  carried out expeditiously to recognize the present housing requirement in Sri Lanka. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Sajith Premadasa, the Minister of Housing and Construction, to secure the assistance of the District, Provincial and Rural level Government officials headed by District Secretaries and Divisional Secretaries, to obtain the accurate and updated information/data required to design the National Housing Programme expected to be implemented by the Ministry of  Housing and Construction, with a view to accomplishing all the housing requirements in Sri Lanka, by the year 2025, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Introduction of New Technology with the Objective of Enhancing the Quality of Inputs used in the Multiday Fishing Vessels
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-17
decision_details_body: - The subsidy schemes for the Maritime Fishing Industry continuously implemented  by the Government of Sri Lanka since 1950, has been subject to changes in keeping with the topical requirements. The Government has allocated a sum of Rs.1,600 million for the year 2016 to introduce small and medium scale technology for fishing industry and a major portion of these provisions will be utilized to modernize the multiday fishing boats operating in the Exclusive Economic Zone  (EEZ) of the country to be on par with the modern technology. Regulations were imposed in year 2011 making it compulsory to install transponders in offshore multiday boats and the installation of this accessory is essential in issuing fitness certificates for the fishing vessels. Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Mahinda Amaraweera, the Minister of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources Development, to provide the fishermen with 2400 transponders  and other  technological equipment required to increase the efficiency and  effectiveness of the fishing industry, for the purpose of ensuring  effective implementation of these regulations, under the subsidy programme implemented by the Government,  was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the Comprehensive Transport Management Plan in the Western Region Megapolis
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-17
decision_details_body: - 	It has been a felt need to provide urgent solutions, in order to minimize the crisis situation prevalent presently in the field of transport, especially to ease the traffic congestion in the Western Region. In the process, short term interventions as well as the other major interventions such as introduction of new technologies which should be implemented in medium and long term basis has to be made.  Accordingly, it has been proposed to implement a number of measures such as introduction of flexible  and staggered working hours, new parking arrangements,   updating of signal light network, improvement of intersections with wide accommodation, improvement of school and office transport services, restructuring of public bus service, modernizing and improving the quality and services of buses, establishment of multi-modal transport hubs, railway electrification and modernization, use of inland water transport and road capacity improvements through the Transport Plan to be implemented under the Western Region Megapolis Master Plan.  Accordingly, the joint proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala de Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation and Hon. Patali Champika Ranawaka, the Minister of Megapolis and Western Development, to implement the above mentioned activities, projects and feasibility studies  identified under the Western Region Megapolis Master Plan, in association with the relevant line Ministries and other institutions, was approved in principle by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of the Asian Institute for Science of Technology (AIST)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-17
decision_details_body: - Out of the students who sit the G.C.E (A/L) Examination annually, only around 22% are selected for the universities and as such, a large number of students leave the country annually to avail themselves the opportunities for higher education. However, most of these students do not return to Sri Lanka. In this background, it is intended to establish a higher educational institute by the name of 'Asian Institute for Science of Technology' (AIST) as a public - private investment, which could generate foreign exchange while providing educational opportunities for both local and foreign students.  Japan, who is a leading development partner of Sri Lanka has come forward to grant financial aid for this project. It is anticipated to establish a 'Technology Village' associated with AIST by the year 2025 and leading Japanese industrial partners will be invited to set up their production centres, research and development centres, high-end design centres etc; Special training programmes will be implemented for the students of this Institute, in the fields such as Nanotechnology, Electrical and Electronics, Information and Communication Technology (ICT), Telecommunication and Robotics, to enable them to enter into the industrial job market. Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Susil Premajayantha, the Minister of Science, Technology and Research, to establish AIST in a land at Malabe in extent of 100 acres, which has been proposed for the City for Science and Technology to be set up under the Western Region Megapolis Plan and to obtain the relevant technological and  financial aid from the Japanese Government as well as from the other donor funding agencies, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development of Batticaloa Airport
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-17
decision_details_body: - As per the Government's policy on developing the civil aviation facilities in Sri Lanka,  the Cabinet has granted approval in the year 2015,  to construct a new terminal building and to renovate the Airport Runway, Taxiway and the Apron at the Batticaloa Airport, in order to develop the said Airport, to enable it to commence the operations of commercial passenger services. Accordingly, around 80% of the work has already been completed and as such, the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala de Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, to get the balance work done through the Civil Aviation Authority, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Access to the Annex VI of the International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships (MARPOL 73/78 Annex VI)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-17
decision_details_body: - Air emissions from ships show a continuous increase and the Protocol of 1997 to the International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships (MARPOL 73/78) was entered into force in International level  since 2005, with a view to preventing air pollution caused by ships. Sri Lanka became a party  to this Convention which comprises of 05 Annexes, in the year 1997. In order to establish the International Regulations for the Prevention of Air Pollution from ships, the Annex VI has been added newly to the said Convention. Due to the present development activities associated with the shipping and ports sector in the country,  Sri Lanka has been subject to adverse effects of air emissions caused by ships and as such, it has become necessary to reduce such air emissions to minimize the effects on health and environment. Accordingly, the proposal made by H.E. the President, Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to accede to the Annex VI newly added for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships (MARPOL 73/78 Annex VI) and to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft legislation to give effect to the said regulations  in Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Inter-Ministerial Committee on Human Rights
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-10
decision_details_body: - The policy of the Government of Sri Lanka is to uphold, promote and protect the human rights of the people of the country. Several steps are presently being taken by the Government in that regard and this includes steps for the fulfillment of voluntary treaty obligations and measures to address human rights concerns which will complement the ongoing reconciliation process, and strengthen freedom and democracy, thus creating the necessary background for economic development.  The Human Rights Action Plan implemented for the Years 2012 to 2016, will come to an end this year and therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Mangala Samaraweera, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, to appoint an Inter-Ministerial Committee on Human Rights, to prepare the National Human Rights Action Plan for the next five years  from 2017 to 2021 and to address all human rights related concerns, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Bilateral Agreement between Ukraine and Sri Lanka on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-10
decision_details_body: - It is of paramount importance to provide International Legal Assistance in Criminal matters in the process of preventing such crimes. The Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters Act, No. 25 of 2002 provides to enter into Bilateral Agreements with foreign countries to provide assistance to those countries by Sri Lanka and vice versa on Mutual Assistance in Criminal matters. Accordingly, with a view to improving the effectiveness of the law enforcement of both parties in the matters of investigation, prosecution, prevention of crime and confiscation of money generated out of criminal proceeds,the proposal made by Hon. (Dr) Wijayadasa Rajapaksa, the Minister of Justice, to enter into an Agreement on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal matters,  between Sri Lanka and Ukraine, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Cross Country Pipeline Project (from Colombo Port to Kollonnawa Oil Terminal)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-10
decision_details_body: - Considering the necessity of expeditious implementation of the Cross Country Pipeline from Colombo Port to Kollonnawa Oil Terminal, the proposal made by Hon. Chandima Weerakkody, the Minister of Petroleum Resources Development, to implement the said project following the Government to Government (G2G) procedure, recommended as the most appropriate procurement procedure by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Upgrading of Health Facilities in selected Hospitals under Chinese Financial Assistance
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-10
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. (Dr) Rajitha Senarathne, the Minister of Health Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine, for the purchase of the essential medical equipment and to construct buildings for the selected hospitals, covering provincial hospitals as well, resulting in the improvement of health facilities in all the provinces in the country, within a financial limit of US$ 85 million, agreed to be provided by the Chinese Government, altering the scope of the above project designed in the year 2010, to suit the present conditions, with a view to upgrading the health facilities in the Northern and Eastern provinces which had been severely affected due to the conflict which continued for three decades, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Matara Stage IV Water Supply Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-10
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet Committee on Economic Management, having considered the urgent need and the importance of  implementing the Matara Stage IV Water Supply Project, has recommended to implement the project, under the loan assistance of National Development Bank, with a view to providing  safe drinking water to the people living in 231 Grama Niladhari Divisions of Matara and suburbs. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Rauff Hakeem, the Minister of City Planning and Water Supply, to award the contract for the implementation of the project, as per the recommendation made by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of the double track between Polgahawela and Kurunegala on the Northern Railway Line
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-10
decision_details_body: - Renovation of the railway lines of Northern and Thalaimannar, under the Indian Line of Credit, has by now been completed to a  considerable extent and the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala de Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, for utilizing the balance amount of US $ 30 million, estimated to be remaining unspent after completion of the project, to construct an additional railway track between Polgahawela and Kurunegala, parallel to the existing one, with an upgraded signaling system, with a view to reducing the travelling time of Northern Railway line, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Memorandum of Understanding between the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and Portugal on Recognition of Certificates issued to Seafarers
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-10
decision_details_body: - A Seafarer holding a Certificate of Competency to serve on a ship that flies a flag of a foreign country, is required to obtain a Certificate of Recognition issued by the state in which the relevant ship is registered,  in addition to the Certificate he possesses.  In order to issue such Certificates, the relevant countries should have entered into a Convention or a Memorandum of Understanding and Sri Lanka has already entered into such agreements with 29 countries. Entering into such agreements will pave the way for a considerable number of Sri Lankan Seafarers who hold Certificates of Competency to have job opportunities in foreign vessels. The Government of Portugal has expressed its willingness to enter into an agreement with Sri Lanka pertaining to the issuance of such Certificates and accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Arjuna Ranatunga, the Minister of Ports and Shipping, to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding with Portugal on Certificates of Recognition issued to Seafarers, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Introduction of New Energy Performance Standards and Energy Labeling for Fluorescent Lamps and Fluorescent Lamp Ballasts
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-10
decision_details_body: - Electricity sector of the country is advancing rapidly with the growth of industrial and commercial sectors and the provision of 100% electricity supply in the country through the extension of the electricity grid to rural areas. At present, the household sector and the business sector consume 37% and 27% respectively of the total electricity consumption of the country. A substantial quantity (approximately 30%) of energy consumption of both these sectors is expended in double capped tubular fluorescent lamps and fluorescent lamp ballasts. It is estimated that by introducing energy performance standards to encourage import/manufacture of energy efficient double capped tubular fluorescent lamps and fluorescent lamp ballasts, about 85 GWh of electricity could be saved annually. Accordingly, in order to regulate the quality of the double capped tubular fluorescent lamps and fluorescent lamp ballasts making it mandatory to display such performance standards on energy for the information of the public, the proposal made by Hon. Ranjith Siyambalapitiya, the Minister of Power and Renewable Energy, to publish the Energy Performance Standards of Appliances (Double Capped Tubular Fluorescent Lamps and Fluorescent Lamp Ballasts) Regulations in the Government Gazette, in accordance with the powers vested in the Minister under the provisions of the Sri Lanka Sustainable Energy Authority Act, No. 35 of 2007  and to present such regulations thereafter in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendments to the Tea Control Act, No. 51 of 1957
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-10
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Navin Dissanayake, the Minister of Plantation Industries, to amend the Tea Control Act, No. 51 of 1957, strengthening the powers of the Minister to make regulations pertaining to reclaimable tea,   using the term 'ප්‍රතික්ෂේපිත තේ' (re-claimed tea) which is more appropriate, instead of 'කසළ තේ', the word presently used in Sinhala, and increasing the maximum fine that can be imposed against any person who is guilty of an offence under the Act from Rs.50,000/- to Rs.500,000/-, and also increasing the maximum amount that can be charged on settling and offence, from Rs.10,000/- to Rs.500,000/-,  was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Economic Empowerment of Women through Apparel based Mini Factories
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-10
decision_details_body: - The Economic Empowerment of Rural Women Programme of the Ministry of Industry and Commerce envisages to encourage the access of small and medium scale entrepreneurs to the International market and to provide employment opportunities to rural women. In this connection, under a programme implemented by the Sri Lanka Textile and Apparel Institution, a training on dress making will be provided by the qualified trainers, to the  rural women selected on a transparent methodology, giving priority to women of the displaced families and those who had become widows due to war. Further, the entrepreneurship development and training will be provided by the National Enterprise Development Authority and the Industrial Development Board. At the same time, the National Design Centre and the National Craft Council will provide design support and training. The sale of apparels so produced will be done through linking national level purchasers and exporters with the Divisional level manufacturers. This programme is proposed to be implemented in the Eastern and Uva Provinces and the areas identified in the selected districts. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Rishad Bathiudeen, the Minister of Industry and Commerce, to implement this programme, to establish 150 cooperative / partnership based business model mini apparel factories   during the year 2016, through organizing the women who successfully completed their training, as a first stage, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of a Building Complex for the Technical College, Vavuniya
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-10
decision_details_body: - The Technical College established in Vavuniya District, of the Department of Technical Education and Training, functioning under the Ministry of Skills Development and Vocational Training, offers 19 Technical Training Courses to the youth and the annual student intake is around 500. The space and other  facilities available in the Technical College are inadequate and as such, the proposal made by Hon. Mahinda Samarasinghe, the Minister of Skills Development and Vocational Training, to construct a building complex for the  said College, which comprises of lecture halls, workshops, residential quarters for officers, computer labs, a library and a water tank with other infrastructure facilities at an estimated cost of Rs.114 million, and to implement Capacity Building Programmes for the staff, at an estimated cost of Rs.04 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Completion of the activities of the Phase II of the Colombo Dental Institute Development Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-10
decision_details_body: - In order to meet the increasing demand for dental health care services and also to cater to the needs of teaching facilities relevant to the dental medical field, it was planned to develop the Colombo Dental Institute as  the State of the Art Technology in two phases. Accordingly,  the first phase of the project has been completed by now and under the  second phase it is proposed to construct a nine storey building, enhancing the  facilities of the Out Patient Department (OPD), operation theaters, wards, X-Ray Department,  stores, administrative and other units and establishing new facilities at the Laboratory.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon.(Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine, to complete  the activities of the second phase of the Colombo Dental Institute Development Project, at an estimated cost of Rs.1,200 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Revision of fines for offences related to railway passenger tickets
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-10
decision_details_body: - Although the railway offers transport facilities to passengers at extremely concessionary rates compared to other passenger transport services, it has been reported that a considerable number of railway passengers still evade obtaining tickets and ride in or upon carriages of a higher class than that for which they had paid their fare.  Considering the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala de Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, to amend the present fine on offences in regard to railway tickets, with a view to providing a safe and efficient railway service, enhancing the revenue of the Department of Railways and discouraging the passengers who travel in trains without obtaining tickets, the Cabinet approved to increase the existing maximum  fine of Rs.1,500/- up to Rs.3,000/-.

description: Submission of the Annual Report of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka for the Year 2015 in Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-10
decision_details_body: - The Annual Report of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka for the Year 2015, prepared to be presented in Parliament, in accordance with the provisions of the Monetary Law Act, which includes the state of the economy, accounts and operations of the Central Bank, major administrative measures adopted regarding the Monetary Policy, major legislative enactments and statistical appendix relating to the past year,  was submitted to the Cabinet by Hon. Prime Minister Ranil Wickremasinghe, in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs and the Cabinet granted approval to present same in Parliament.

description: Grants provided by the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) for the Maritime Safety Capacity Improvement
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-10
decision_details_body: - The Government of Japan has agreed to provide 02 units of 30 meters long  patrol vessels and other necessary assistance for the development of the capabilities of Sri Lanka Coast Guard through further enhancing their operations around the Sri Lankan coastal areas.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Prime Minister Ranil Wickremasinghe, in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs, to enter into a Grant Agreement with the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) to obtain a grant of Japanese Yen 1,830,000,000 (approximately Rs.2,400 million) for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Corporate Legal Reforms in Corporate Bankruptcy Laws
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-05-10
decision_details_body: - It has been observed that the provisions available in the Insolvency Ordinance, No.24 of 1884 are not at all sufficient to deal with the issues pertaining to the modern day ailing business ventures. Also the necessity of introducing   a new set of laws relating to bankruptcy has arisen in order to restructure the State Owned Enterprises. If suitable and effective laws to handle bankruptcy situations could be enacted, Sri Lanka will be able to gain a higher place in the 'Ease of doing business' index. Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe, the Prime Minister, to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft legislation to amend the Companies Act, No.07 of 2007, with a view to introducing a Bankruptcy Law  which suits the present day requirements, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Revision of Salaries of the Members of the Three Armed Forces
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-04-26
decision_details_body: - The Public Administration Circular No.03/2016 dated 2016-02-25 was  issued in accordance with the decision taken by the  Government to add the special allowances  and the interim allowance of Rs.10,000/- granted for public servants in addition to their basic salaries, in stages. Similarly, the Circular instructions pertaining to the revision of salaries of the officers in the State Corporations, Statutory Boards and the Government owned Companies have already been issued concurrently. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, to issue Circular instructions, for the revision of the salaries of the members of the Three Armed Forces, in concurrence with the above salary revision, made in accordance with the recommendations of the National Salaries and Cadre Commission, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Re-orientation of SriLankan Airlines (SA)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-04-26
decision_details_body: - The SriLankan Airlines, initially founded, as 'Air Ceylon Limited' in the year 1947, was incorporated thereafter as a limited liability company as  'Air Lanka Limited', in the year 1979. According to the 10 year management contract entered into with the Emirates Airlines in 1998, 40% of  the shares of the Air Lanka Limited were divested to the Emirates Airlines and at the same period 'Air Lanka' was renamed as 'SriLankan Airlines'. The SriLankan Airlines, as a whole,  successfully functioned as a profit making entity, paying taxes to the  Government, during the period between 1998 to 2008 when the Emirates was handling the administrative activities of SriLankan Airlines. Subsequently, in the year 2010, operational activities of the Airlines were re-vested with the Government and presently, it is functioning with continuous operational losses due to many reasons including unsound management. As per the analysis conducted by the Ministry of Finance, the total liabilities of SriLankan Airlines as at 2015-12-31 stands at Rs.461 billion. Therefore, a suitable partnership has to be sought for taking over of the operational activities of the SriLankan Airlines with the objective of re-orienting the SriLankan Airlines, having redeemed it from the financial crisis. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe, the Prime Minister, for the Government of Sri Lanka to take over all the liabilities of SriLankan Airlines, to enable it to reorient on its own, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining the Approval of the Cabinet to print the school textbooks to be distributed for the year 2017 free of charge  without following the Open Procurement Procedure
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-04-26
decision_details_body: - The joint proposal made by Hon. Akila Viraj Kariyawasam, the Minister of Education and Hon. Gayantha Karunathilaka, the Minister of Parliamentary Reforms and Mass Media, to award the tender for printing of 30% of school textbooks, to be distributed free of charge among the students during the year 2017, to State Printing Corporation and the Department of Government Printing, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Commencement of 'Consultancy Services for Development of Basin Investment Plans for Selected Basins' under Climate Resilience Improvement Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-04-26
decision_details_body: - The improvement of infrastructure facilities required for enhancing the capability of facing the hazards that could occur due to climate change is carried out under this project. Accordingly, under the first component of the project, it is anticipated to improve the infrastructure facilities of 10 basins selected on a priority basis, to identify the vulnerabilities of flood and drought that may occur in future and to mitigate such vulnerabilities. Further, under the second component of the project, it is proposed to improve the irrigation and transport infrastructure facilities damaged due to flood and landslides that occurred recently, and to renovate the sites/premises, where the school buildings prone to landslides are situated, using buffer walls. Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Vijith Vijayamuni Zoysa, the Minister of Irrigation and Water Resources Management, to award the consultancy contract for the activities of the first component, as  recommended by the Cabinet Appointed Consultants Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding of Consultancy Contract for National Transmission and Distribution Network Development and Efficiency Improvement Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-04-26
decision_details_body: - The National Transmission and Distribution Network Development and Efficiency Improvement Project is implemented under the loan facilities provided by the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA). Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Ranjith Siyambalapitiya, the Minister of Power and Renewable Energy, to award the consultancy contract for the construction of a 400kV transmission line and the development of a 11kV underground electricity distribution line in the areas of Dehiwala, Mount Lavinia and Battaramulla, under the project, as recommended by the Cabinet Appointed Consultants Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Tender for  the Supply of 950,000 Vials of Biphasic Isophane Insulin (Human) Injection BP, 1000 IU / 10ml
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-04-26
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon.(Dr) Rajitha Seneratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine, to award the tender for the  purchase of the above drug used for the treatment of diabetic patients, as  recommended by the Procurement Appeal Board, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Tender for the Supply of 27,000 Vials of Concentrated Monoclonal Purified and Detergent Treated Dried Factor VIII Fraction 200 IU - 350 IU
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-04-26
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon.(Dr) Rajitha Seneratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine, to award the tender for the purchase of the above drug used for the treatment of haemophilia patients, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of Hostels for the University Students under the Expeditious Project of Construction of Hostels
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-04-26
