Sri Lanka ratified the United Nations Protocol  to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, especially Women and Children (Palermo Protocol) in 2015.  The Protocol acts to prevent and combat trafficking in persons, to provide for the physical and psychological recovery and reintegration  of victims of trafficking and to promote co-operation among states, in order to meet those objectives. Accordingly, recognizing the importance of following a multi-stakeholder approach to prevent the heinous crime of human trafficking, the 'Five Year National Strategic Plan to Monitor, Combat Human Trafficking (2015-2019)' developed by the National Anti-Human Trafficking Task Force, submitted to the Cabinet by Hon. (Dr.) Wijayadasa Rajapaksa, the Minister of Justice, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the Food Production National Programme (2016 - 2018)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-02-03
decision_details_body: - In accordance with the observations made at the meeting chaired by  H.E. the President, held with the representatives of the private sector who engaged in business activities related to agriculture and food production sector, in order to successfully implement the Food Production National Programme, the proposal made by Hon. Duminda Dissanayake, the Minister of Agriculture, to implement the proposals of making mandatory the obtaining of clearance from the Department of Agriculture when importing any crop being promoted for cultivation under this programme, by an importer, to Sri Lanka as a consumer item, prior to ordering such items; if the said crops are imported at the instances where the local production is inadequate, the provision of opportunities to the private companies as well as the institutions who engaged in promotion of crop cultivation under the above National Programme, to import such crops as consumer items; in order to ensure that the each food product so imported as consumer items possesses health safeness and high standard, introduction of a new methodology to examine the quality of such goods, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Memorandum of Understanding between the Ministry of Power & Renewable Energy of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy of the Federal Republic of Germany on Co-operation on Sustainable Development in the Energy Sector of Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-02-03
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Ranjith Siyambalapitiya, the Minister of Power and Renewable Energy, to sign the Memorandum of Understanding for the Co-operation on Sustainable Development in the Energy Sector of Sri Lanka, consists of the development of electricity generation projects in  renewable energy, research and development in relation to enhancing  renewable energy electricity absorption capacity into the national electricity grid, development of the plants and equipment used in the renewable energy based electricity generation, manufacturing of such plants and equipment with the use of local raw materials, introduction of  clean technologies for thermal power generation, training and education in relation to renewable energy development, between the Ministry of Power & Renewable Energy of Sri Lanka and the Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy of the Federal Republic of Germany, during the state visit of H.E. the President, to the Federal Republic of Germany, on the 16th and 17th February of this year, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Revoking the Homeopathy Act, No. 07 of 1970, and getting a new	Act 	passed in its place
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-02-03
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has already been granted to repeal the Homeopathy Act, No. 07 of 1970 and pass a new Act in its place. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine, to present the  Homeopathy Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman that provides for the establishment of the Homeopathic Medical Council, registration of  Homeopathic practitioners and Homeopathic pharmacists, registration and regulation of Homeopathic institutions, promotion, fostering and regulation of the Homeopathic system of medicine, in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The establishment of a National Science Centre
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-02-03
decision_details_body: - The National Science Centre will be established in the proposed Science City to be constructed at Malabe as 'a National icon of Science',  with the state of the art exhibits and facilities of international standards, which will empower and inspire our people to drive Sri Lanka towards prosperity through science, technology and innovation. Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Susil Premajayantha, the Minister of Science, Technology and Research, to establish the National Science Centre of Sri Lanka consists of exhibition galleries in the areas such as wonders of the nature, agriculture, the earth, climate change and natural disasters, marvels of the human body, industrialization and technological revolutions, space and astronomy, indigenous and traditional knowledge and the pioneers in the field of science, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Allocation of a land to establish a Regional Centre of the Open	University of Sri Lanka, at Badulla
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-02-03
decision_details_body: - The Open University of Sri Lanka has been established for the purpose of providing a quality higher education to those who miss the university entrance as well as the other higher education opportunities.  It has been planned to establish a Regional Centre of that University in the Badulla District. This will provide special opportunities for the school leavers  and the youth in the Uva Province, especially in the Badulla District to pursue their higher studies.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Lakshman Kiriella, the Minister of Higher Education and Highways, to vest the land in extent of 02 acres, 02 roods and 3.2 perches  at Hingurugamuwa of the Badulla Divisional Secretariat of the Badulla District, identified as suitable for the establishment of the Regional Centre, to the Open University of Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The draft Bill to amend the Criminal Procedure Code Act
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-02-03
decision_details_body: - At present, the accumulation of  the Court productions largely in the Court premises has become a serious issue. Therefore, in order to provide for the disposal of relevant court productions prior to finalization of cases, the proposal made by  Hon. (Dr.) Wijayadasa Rajapaksa, the Minister of Justice, to publish the Bill prepared to amend the Sections 431 and 432 of the Criminal Procedure Code and present same in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of the three Warehouse complexes in the districts of Polonnaruwa, Killinochchi and Ratnapura
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-27
decision_details_body: - Several initiatives have been taken up in the budget proposals of the year 2016, to enhance the productivity of the agricultural sector and to ensure the food security of the country; and in addition to that, Rs.1000 million has been allocated by the Government to construct three warehouse complexes in the Districts of Polonnaruwa, Killinochchi and Ratnapura, with a view to providing storage facilities, in compliance with higher standards, to the farmers during  the periods of excessive harvest, to store their products such as paddy, maize,  gingelly, pepper, black gram etc.  Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance,  to award the consultancy contract for the construction of the said warehouses, to the Central Engineering Consultancy Bureau (CECB), with the objective of expeditiously completing the project on the construction of warehouse complexes and  generating the maximum benefits to the farmers, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Asian Development Bank funded integrated road investment Program  - Obtaining approval to award the contracts for the two rural road civil works - contract packages in the Sabaragamuwa Province
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-27
decision_details_body: - The above road development programme operates with the funds provided by the Asian Development Bank; and selected roads in the Provinces of Southern,  Sabaragamuwa, Western, Central, Wayamba and North Central, are developed under this programme. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Lakshman Kiriella, the Minister of Higher Education and Highways, to award the contracts for the rehabilitation of 143km of the rural roads in the Kegalle District of the Sabaragamuwa Province, in accordance with the recommendation of the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Repairing 1000 nos. passenger buses of the Sri Lanka Transport Board, with the objective of providing a more efficient and comfortable bus service to the general public
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-27
decision_details_body: - Due to the lack of adequate public transport facilities,  the general public are trending more towards the use private modes of transport, instead of public transport modes, for their day-to-day travelling requirements. This  situation has directly led to the increase of  traffic congestion on main roads and the rise in the number of traffic accidents. Finding a solution for this issue has become a main responsibility of the Sri Lanka Transport Board. Therefore, arrangements have been made to operate 6000 buses in the year 2016, to provide a better transport service to the general public. The maintenance of a fleet of at least  6900 buses,  in good condition, is essential in order to operate  6000 buses. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala De Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, to enhance the quality of SLTB buses through the repair of 1000 buses with  a lifespan of over 10 years, on priority basis,  by using the necessary spare parts and to procure such spare parts through the open bidding process, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Calling for Tenders to select suitable operators, for the operation of the core category duty free shops, at the Bandaranaike International Airport
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-27
decision_details_body: - Duty-free shops are of special significance in airport mercantile operations and  up to now,  the right to maintain core category duty-free shops at both arrival and departure terminals of the Bandaranaike International Airport, has been granted as a monopoly, to two operators. No Tender procedure or calling for competitive bids,  has been followed in the selection of contractors in this regard.  Therefore, with a view to securing a higher return to the Airport and the Airport and Aviation Services (SL) Limited, the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala De Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation,  to appoint a Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee and a Technical Evaluation Committee, for the purpose of inviting bids in a more transparent manner in compliance with the Tender procedure, for the operation of these shops for a contract period of five years, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding the contract for the consultancy services for reviewing and approving of design and construction supervision of the construction of head works of the Kaluganga Reservoir to the Central Engineering Consultancy Bureau (CECB)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-27
decision_details_body: - Kaluganga Reservoir is designed to be constructed across Kaluganga, at a location downstream in Pallegama area of the Laggala electorate in  Matale District.  It is one of the main components of the Moragahakanda Kaluganga Project.  Therefore, the proposal made by H.E. the President, Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to award the contract for the consultancy services for design review, approval and construction supervision of the head works of the Kaluganga Development Project, to the Central Engineering Consultancy Bureau for an estimated sum of Rs. 443 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The Re-organization of the National Equipment & Machinery Organization
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-27
decision_details_body: - The National Equipment & Machinery Organization was established in the year 1991, with a view to providing appropriate equipment and machinery to implement the construction industry islandwide on an economically stable basis. There was a high demand from the District Secretaries/Government Agents, Divisional Secretaries, Local Authorities, Gramodaya Centres, Community Development Councils and even small scale private contractors, who were carrying out the regional and village level infrastructure development work at that time, to obtain the equipment and machinery provided by this organization and as such,  arrangements were made to supply them through 54 machinery and equipment depots. Thereafter, in 2011, this organization was   brought under the   the State Engineering Corporation  and since the objectives of the two institutions did not complement each other, the NEMO went into a decline. Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Sajith Premadasa, the Minister of Housing and Construction, to re-organize the National Equipment & Machinery Organization as an institution administered by a separate management committee, as done during its commencement in 1992, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Imposition of the special trade levies on the import of Mackerel fish for the production of canned fish
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-27
decision_details_body: - Annually, around 20,000 metric tonnes of canned fish are imported to this country to fulfill the local demand for canned fish.  In order to save the foreign exchange of more than Rs.5 billion annually expended for the purpose, the Government has encouraged the local production of canned fish and as a result, since 2012, four local factories are engaged in the process of producing canned fish and releasing the same to the local market. The number of direct employment opportunities generated under this process is about 150. In order to encourage the production of local canned fish, the levy on imported canned fish was raised up to Rs. 100/- per Kg., in the year 2013 and steps were taken to reduce the same to Rs. 50/- per Kg. in the year 2015, with the objective of providing concessions to the consumers. Conditions were imposed to the effect that every imported can of fish weighing 425 gms should contain 280 gms of drained solids; the maximum retail price of such a can should be Rs.140/-; an imported can of fish weighing 155 gms should contain 105 gms of drained solids; and that the maximum retail price of such a can should be Rs.70/-. However, the consumers have not had the anticipated relief and instead,  the sale of canned fish in excess of the maximum retail price; the importation of canned fish rising up to 40,000 MTs with tax reduction in year 2015; and the expenditure of foreign exchange exceeding Rs.10 billion, has  incurred. Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Mahinda Amaraweera, the Minister of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources Development,  to grant the concessionary levy on the import of  Mackerel fish, introduced to provide relief to the consumer, only to the local manufacturers of canned fish, on a permit basis and to grant the concessionary levy on the import of canned fish, only to those with the stipulated standard, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Allocation of the Waters Edge Hotel Premises at Battaramulla to M/s Waters Edge Ltd.
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-27
decision_details_body: - The “Waters Edge Limited” was incorporated as a fully owned subsidiary company of the Urban Development Authority (UDA) in 2009, for the maintenance and development of the Waters Edge premises, vested with the Authority in accordance with a judgment of the Supreme Court.  A new company fully owned by the UDA was established in 2014 by the name of 'Waters Edge Hotel Developers Limited', for the purpose of constructing and developing resident hotel facilities including a condominium complex, in the  Waters Edge premises. The contract for the construction has been awarded to a private company selected  through Tender procedure. Although the relevant contractor had started on the construction work, at present the said work has been suspended. The new Board of Directors of the Waters Edge Limited has decided to resume the above construction project. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Patali Champika Ranawaka, the Minister of Megapolis and Western Development,  to allocate the hotel premises of the Waters Edge, in extent of 23 Acres - 01 Rood and 36.05 perches, to M/s Waters Edge Ltd. on a 99 year lease term and transfer the contract of the construction with the relevant private company, to the M/s Waters Edge Ltd. for the new construction, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Intellectual Property Act, No. 36 of 2003, to facilitate access to the published works by the visually impaired or otherwise print disabled people
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-27
decision_details_body: - According to statistics, the number of visually impaired or partially impaired persons  living in Sri Lanka by 2011, was around 983,000 and it has been estimated  that  this number  has increased up to one million by 2015 . The number of visually impaired people living in the world is 285 million. Hence, facilities  to access the printed or published works, should be provided for those who are visually impaired or otherwise print disabled. The “Marrakesh Treaty”, administered by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), has guided its member states to introduce a standard set of exceptions to relax the limitations on  copyright rules in order to permit the reproduction, distribution and dissemination of published work in formats accessible to print disabled people. Accordingly, the Intellectual Property Act, No. 36 of 2003, has to be amended, by  incorporating a set of exceptions on the existing copyright laws, prior to the ratification of the Marrakesh Treaty by Sri Lanka.  Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Rishad Bathiudeen, the Minister of Industry and Commerce,  to draft necessary legislation for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining financial assistance for the implementation of the Kelani right bank water supply Project Phase II
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-27
decision_details_body: - The Kelani right bank water treatment plant provides water to the  urban areas north of Colombo , with a full capacity level of 180,000 m3.   - Due to the rapid development of this area at present,  the location of the Airport, the Export-processing zones in Biyagama and Katunayake and the buildings of the defence forces, the current demand for water supply has increased. . Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance,  to enter into an agreement with the Credit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank of France, to obtain a buyer's credit facility of around Euro 96 million, with a view to increasing the capacity of the said water treatment plant by  constructing  a new water treatment plant of 180,000 m3,  and providing infrastructure facilities including the  laying of main pipelines distributing treated water and a  watertransmission line of 25 km, the construction of the Wee Oya Reservoir and the supply and installation of inflatable rubber balloons as a salinity barrier, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Natural Mineral Resources Policy for Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-27
decision_details_body: - A  formal document on the spread and  extent of diverse resources of minerals in Sri Lanka, has  not yet been prepared. The potential  value of these existing resources has increased, due to reasons such as the creation of  high-end  products through the use of such resources and the expansion of technical knowledge in utilizing the same. Many of the mineral resources available in Sri Lanka are exported without value addition and for this reason,  we have not been able to derive the highest economic benefits  from these resources. Although a one (01) kg of Ilmenite, found in the area of Pulmuddai, yields only Rs.40/-, when it's value-added as pharmaceutical grade Titanium Dioxide, it will receive  Rs.450,000/- per kg. Therefore, considering the above matters, the proposal made by Hon. Susil Premajayantha, the Minister of Science, Technology and Research, to appoint a Cabinet Sub‑Committee, for the purpose of formulating a National Policy for Sri Lanka on Natural Mineral Resources, with a view to  putting an end to the exportation of local mineral resources without any value addition, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Granting legal status to the National Building Research Organization (NBRO)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-27
decision_details_body: - The National Building Research Organization (NBRO) was established in the year 1984, with the amalgamation of the Building Research Institution administered by the State Engineering Corporation and the Soil Laboratory of the  Department of Buildings. Then, in 1993, it was reorganized as a separate institution,under the Institute of Construction, Training and Development (ICTAD), of the Ministry of Housing and Construction. This institution mainly depends on its own earnings and acts as the National Centre in the management of landslides and geographical irregularities. The grant of legal recognition, to this organization with more than 25 years of experience, will  enable it to deliver its services in a more excellent manner.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Anura Priyadharashana Yapa, the Minister of Disaster Management, to draft necessary legislation to rename this institution, which renders services such as the identification of “at-risk” areas in Sri Lanka, issuance of early warnings, issuance of landslide risk evaluation reports, consultancy services and assessment of damages, as the “National Building Research Organization” and establish it through an Act of Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Bandaranaike International Airport Development Project - Phase II Stage 2
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-27
decision_details_body: - With the initiatives taken by the Government for the rapid development of the country, in order to better the connectivity with the world and for the promotion of the Tourism industry, the enhancement of the passenger handling capacity of the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) is a vital need.  Accordingly, with a view to enhancing the passenger capacity of the BIA, the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala De Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, to enter into a loan agreement with the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), to obtain the funds required for the Stage 2 - Phase II of the Bandaranaike International Airport Development Project which includes the construction of the state of the art main terminal building of 180,000 m2,  the construction of an  elevated roadway to  enter the said building and  the provision of  electricity, water, sewerage systems, vehicle parks, sub-runaways and the other infrastructure facilities, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the United Nations World Food Programme  during the period 2016 - 2017
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-27
decision_details_body: - The World Food Programme (WFP) formally established its collaboration with the Government of Sri Lanka in the year 1968 and since then, various programmes relevant to the areas such as nutrition, sustainable development, climate change and food security are being implemented in Sri Lanka by the said Programme.  A joint proposal for the period of two years from 2016 to 2017 has been developed by the relevant Ministries and agencies, to eradicate the problems pertaining to the food security and malnutrition in association with this Programme, while eleven districts which cover the Provinces of North, East, Uva and Central have been identified for the provision of relief under this Programme. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Prime Minister, Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe, in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs, to implement this Programme during the period of two years from 2016 to 2017, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Capacity Building Project for Sri Lanka's Forensic Science Agencies and Officials
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-27
decision_details_body: - Digital evidence and DNA analysis  which are considered as the two main sources of modern forensic science,  play a vital role in the investigation of many criminal cases.  Accordingly, the Cabinet noted the information submitted by the Prime Minister, Hon. Ranil Wickramasinghe, in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs that in order to widen the capacity of acquiring Digital evidence and conducting DNA analysis in the country, a project for the enhancement of the capacity building of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) and the Government Analyst's Department (GAD), in the said fields,  will be implemented under a grant aid equivalent to US$ 3.2 million provided by the Korean International Cooperation Agency (KOICA).

description: Amendment to the Criminal Procedure Code Act, No.15 of 1979
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-20
decision_details_body: - The right of access to a lawyer for any person suspected of having committed an offense is recognized as a basic element of a fair trial.  Therefore, immediately after recording the first statement of the person arrested by the police, he should be given the opportunity of consulting an Attorney-at-Law on his or her choice.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Wijayadasa Rajapakse, the Minister of Justice, to amend the Criminal Procedure Code Act, to make necessary provisions so as to recognize the right possessed by a person arrested to obtain advice from an Attorney-at-Law at his choice and to provide the service of an Attorney-at-Law of the Legal Aid Commission in case the person arrested pleads that he is unable to retain an Attorney-at-Law, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining the Membership of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank  (AIIB)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-20
decision_details_body: - The main intention of establishing the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is to provide financial support for infrastructure development and the regional connectivity, particularly in Asia.  Sri Lanka signed the  Articles of Association of this Bank on 29th June 2015, in Beijing, China, as a founding member.  By now, 57 countries including 37 Asian regional countries and 20 non?regional countries have agreed to render support for this Bank.  The authorized capital of the Bank is US$ 100 billion and the regional countries are to contribute 75% of the total capital while the non?regional countries are to contribute the balance 25%.  As per the agreement entered into by the founding member countries, each member country will be allocated a share/a quota based on the economy (Gross Domestic Production) of such country.   Accordingly, the subscribed contribution allocated for Sri Lanka is US$ 268 million. Based on the proposal submitted by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, the Cabinet granted approval to draft a Bill enabling the Government of Sri Lanka to formally become a member of the AIIB  ratifying the above agreement.  The approval was also granted to ally with the Group G, the constituency to be led by Indonesia, since Sri Lanka has to ally with  a regional country, in order to ensure a representation in the Director Board of the Bank.

description: Implementation of Sports & Physical Health Promotion National Week
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-20
decision_details_body:
- It has been revealed that less than 25% of the school children in Sri Lanka takes part in sports and when it comes to higher education, that percentage further declines to a position as low as 8%.  As a result, the percentage vulnerable to non-communicable diseases due to wrong food habits, doping substances and smoking has gone up and it is found that 68% of deaths of persons below 65 years of age occur due to non-communicable diseases.  Accordingly, in order to popularize sports and physical health among the entire community, the proposal made by Hon. Dayasiri Jayasekara, the Minister of Sports, to declare and implement a 'Sports and Physical Health Promotion National Week' from 25th to 30th January 2016, throughout the island, in association with the relevant Ministries and all the Provincial Councils, was approved by the Cabinet. 





*  Monday the 25th January	-	Sports and Physical Fitness Promotion Day for Government and Public Service.

*  Tuesday the 26th January 	-	 Sports and Physical Fitness Promotion Day for Education, Higher Education and Highways, Youth and Women's Affairs .

*  Wednesday the 27th January - 	Sports and Physical Fitness Promotion Day for Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine.

*  Thursday the 28th January 	- 	Sports and Physical Fitness Promotion Day for Security Forces and Private Enterprises.

*  Friday the 29th January 	-	Sports and Physical Fitness Promotion Day for Sports Organizations, Sports Associations and Sports Federations.

*  Saturday the 30th January	-	Sports and Physical Fitness Promotion Special Day.

description: Requesting proposal from the Investors for the business opportunities identified to be implemented under the Hambantota Port Development Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-20
decision_details_body: - An Initial Environmental Examination has been conducted by the University of Moratuwa,  with regard to the proposed industries to be implemented within the industrial zone at the Port of Hambantota.  It has been recommended by the said study that the coal related industries should not be established in the area.  Therefore, the Sri Lanka Ports Authority has already prepared a business plan for the identification of business ventures that could be commenced under the Hambantota Port Development Project.  It has been planned to implement the business opportunities so identified, as Public - Private Partnerships.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Arjuna Ranatunga, the Minister of Ports and Shipping, to appoint a Negotiating Committee and a Project Committee to request for proposals from the investors, to evaluate the same and to conduct negotiations, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Agreement for the Transfer of Sentenced Persons between the Government of Sri Lanka and the Islamic Republic of Iran
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-20
decision_details_body: - Official discussions between the delegations of the Government of Sri Lanka and the Government of Islamic Republic of Iran, to enter into an agreement on the transfer of sentenced persons between the two countries, were held in December 2015.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Wijayadasa Rajapaksa, the Minister of Justice, to enter into this agreement during the forthcoming official visit of the Minister of Justice of Iran to Sri Lanka and to make necessary arrangements for the ratification of the same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Accelerated Irrigation Development Project in the Moneragala District ('Wellassa Navodaya')
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-20
decision_details_body: - Moneragala District is considered as the second largest district in the country and majority of its population is engaged in agriculture as their livelihood. Therefore, it has been planned to implement an accelerated development programme to rehabilitate the existing irrigation infrastructure of that area.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Vijith Vijayamuni Zoysa,  the Minister of Irrigation and Water Resources Management, to implement the 'Wellassa Navodaya' Accelerated Irrigation Development Project designed with the main objective of uplifting the standard of living of the farmers in the said district, through increasing the agricultural productivity, during the period of four years from 2016-2019, was approved in principle by the Cabinet.

description: Irrigation System Development Project of the Polonnaruwa District
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-20
decision_details_body: - The Polonnaruwa District is one of the largest paddy cultivating areas in Sri Lanka and the total extent of paddy cultivating lands exceeds 80,000 acres.  However, in recent past, the paddy cultivation in the district has undergone a set back due to situations such as floods and prolonged dry spells.  To address the issues encountered by the farmers of the Polonnaruwa District, the Irrigation Department has proposed to implement a six year Irrigation Development Plan commencing from the year 2016.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Vijith Vijayamuni Zoysa, the Minister of Irrigation and Water Resources Management, to implement the said development plan, at an estimated investment of Rs.7 billion, during the period of six years from 2016 to 2021 under 3 phases, namely, short term, medium term and long term, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Contributions to African - Asian Rural Development Organization  (AARDO)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-20
decision_details_body: - The main objective of the African - Asian Rural Development Organization (AARDO), which has been established in 1962, is to make better understanding among the member countries on problems and issues and to explore the opportunities and collaborative efforts, for  sustainable agricultural and rural development.  Sri Lanka has obtained the permanent membership of this organization in the year 2013. The Cabinet approved the proposal made by Hon. Duminda Dissanayake, the Minister of Agriculture, to make the annual contribution to that organization, taking into consideration the benefits could be gained by Sri Lanka, being a permanent member of this organization.

description: Making Accreditation mandatory in taking Technical Decisions
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-20
decision_details_body: - In order to ensure that the laboratories including medical laboratories, certification bodies and inspection bodies provide services with due standards to the clients, the Sri Lanka Accreditation Board (SLAB) grants accreditation to the said bodies in compliance with the international and national standards.  Although this Board completes 10 years of existence, the number of accreditation granted by the said Board up to now is only about 100. The main reason for that low performance is the accreditation conducted by the SLAB is implemented only at the discretion of the client.  Inadequacy of the assistance rendered by the regulatory bodies for the implementation of accreditation has also been a reason for this situation.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Susil Premajayantha, the Minister of Science, Technology and Research, to provide necessary provisions to make the conformity assessment procedures and accreditation mandatory for the areas such as quality, environment, food safety, occupational health and safety, energy, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Join hands with a Private Investor to reorganize Mahaweli Livestock and Agri Business (Pvt) Ltd. as a Public - Private Partnership
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-20
decision_details_body: - The Mahaweli Livestock and Agri Business (Pvt) Ltd. established in the year 1999 is a company fully owned by the Mahaweli Authority of Sri Lanka. Carrying out activities related to areas such as livestock management, milk production, agri-crop cultivation and providing required knowledge and extension services to the farmers are among the main objectives of establishing this company.  At present, two farms owned by this company are situated in Girandurukotte and Damminna areas.  Consequent to the  changes made in the management and reduction of unnecessary and wasteful expenditure, the company which was running at a loss for a number of years has now reached a status of non-loss making.   However, due to the deterioration of the capital assets and the machinery, a capital  investment is essential for the sustainability of the company.  Accordingly, the proposal made by H.E. the President, Maithripala Sirisena in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to select a suitable investor through public-private partnership to conduct the affairs of the company, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding the construction activities of the Kataragama Circuit Bungalow for the migrant workers, to the State Engineering Corporation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-13
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. (Mrs.) Thalatha Atukorala, the Minister of Foreign Employment, to award the contract for construction of a circuit bungalow in Kataragama, for the Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment, to the State Engineering Corporation functions under the Ministry of Housing and Construction, at an estimated cost of Rs.141 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding of consortium consultancy and construction contracts to the Government Institutions
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-13
decision_details_body: - The Ministry of Megapolis and Western Development has planned to implement the “Sukhitha Purawara” town development programme, to address the major issues of traffic congestion, unavailability of parking facilities, road safety, health problems, housing issues and lack of spaces for recreational activities, caused due to the haphazard development in the secondary cities in the Western Province. Accordingly, projects for the development of strategically important townships in the Western Region,  at an estimated cost of Rs.6 billion, are to be implemented within the year 2016. Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Patali Champika Ranawaka, the Minister of Megapolis and Western Development, to assign the projects identified under the above programme, that can be commenced immediately, to the Government Institutions engaged in construction field, on design and build basis, following the competitive bidding method and to award the projects that involve time consuming processes such as land acquisition, to the private consultants and contractors, following the open competitive bidding method, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding the Tender for the purchase of 210,000 Vials of Enoxaparin Sodium Injection 4,000 IU in 0.4 ml Prefilled Syringe / Vial & 322,500 Vials of Enoxaparin Sodium Injection 6,000 IU in 0.6 ml Prefilled Syringe / Vial
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-13
decision_details_body: - Enoxaparin Sodium Injection is used to treat heart diseased patients.  As per the recommendation of the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine,  to purchase 210,000 Vials of Enoxaparin Sodium Injection 4,000 IU in 0.4 ml Prefilled Syringe / Vial & 322,500 Vials of Enoxaparin Sodium Injection 6,000 IU in 0.6 ml Prefilled Syringe / Vial, was approved by  the Cabinet.

description: Awarding the Tender for the purchase of 20,000 Vials of Human Immunoglobulin for IV use 2.5 - 3.0 g Vial
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-13
decision_details_body: - Human Immunoglobulin for IV use is utilized to treat patients with immune deficiencies. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine,  to award the Tender for the purchase of 20,000 Vials of Human Immunoglobulin for IV use 2.5 - 3.0 g Vials, as per the recommendation of the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding the Tender for the purchase of 150,000 Vials of Meropenem Injection 500 mg Vial & 310,000 Vials of Meropenem Injection 1 g Vial
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-13
decision_details_body: - The Meropenem injection is used as an antibiotic for infections. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine, to award the Tender for the purchase of 150,000 Vials of Meropenem Injection 500 mg Vial and 310,000 Vials of Meropenem Injection 1g Vial, as per the recommendation of the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding the Tender for the purchase of 30,000 Vials of Human Immunoglobulin for IV use 5-6g Vial
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-13
decision_details_body: - Human Immunoglobulin for IV use is utilized to treat patients with immune deficiencies. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine, to award the Tender for the purchase of 30,000 Vials of Human Immunoglobulin for IV use 5 - 6g Vials, to the lowest responsive bidder, as per the recommendation of the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Outsourcing of heavy repairs of Passenger Coaches to outside parties with the objective of providing a more efficient and comfortable train service to the general public
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-13
decision_details_body: - The Sri Lanka Railways at present, utilizes coaches hauled by locomotives and diesel multiple units, for the transportation of passengers. Approximately 450 Nos. of passenger coaches are required for the service currently maintained by the department and such coaches have to undergo heavy repairs biennially. Those repairs are presently being carried out at the Central Railway Workshop at Ratmalana. Since the heavy repairs in the coaches are excessive, it has been difficult to undergo monthly repairs of sufficient coaches and release them. Accordingly, with a view to providing a more safe and comfortable railway service to the public, the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala De Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, to invite competitive bids from the reputed local industrialists, to undertake the heavy repairs of 200 passenger coaches and locomotives and release them expeditiously for service, while continuing the present repairs carried out by the employees of the Railways, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The initiation of a sustained programme for Administrative Reforms
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-13
decision_details_body: - The  Sri Lankan Government's Development Plan to be implemented in the medium term for reaching the developed country status was disclosed through the Economic Policy Statement recently made by Hon. Prime Minister in Parliament.  In order to achieve the objectives expected from the said plan, the existence of an efficient, active and modernized Governmental machinery is an essential factor. The one of the major causes for the higher progress achieved in the economic development recently by the countries such as Singapore and Malaysia is the existence of an efficient and modernized administrative mechanism.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Sarath Amunugama, the Minister of Special Assignments, to recommend the measures to be taken to introduce administrative reforms which create the background for the establishment of such an administrative mechanism in the country, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: "The Nearest School is the Best School" National Programme (2016-2020), intended to create a generation of students imbued with Virtues, Wisdom and Vigour through development of a System of Smart Focal Schools
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-13
decision_details_body: - "The Nearest School is the Best School" National Programme (2016-2020) is scheduled to be implemented, to achieve the objectives of the five-fold education manifesto of the Government, under the theme of 'ensuring equity in education, in order to create an aesthetically minded, creative and philanthropic child, who is imbued with virtues, wisdom and vigour', for the process of uplifting the education qualitatively and quantitatively. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Akila Viraj Kariyawasam, the Minister of Education, to develop 650 schools by selecting one or two schools from each Divisional Secretariat division, to develop capacity of the Principals and the Deputy Principals of these schools, by providing them with foreign and local training, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Strengthening the Plantation Management Monitoring Division
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-13
decision_details_body: - The land ownership of 465 large scale estates belong to the Janatha Estates Development Board and the Sri Lanka State Plantation Corporation, which have been on a lease out to 23 Regional Plantation Companies, still remains with the Government and the protection of the interests of the Government is executed through the Plantation Management Monitoring Division functions under the Ministry of Plantation Industries. Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Navin Dissanayake, the Minister of Plantation Industries, for the strengthening of the Plantation Management Monitoring Division, in order to increase the productivity and level of quality of the plantations in these estates, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Kalutara Town Centre Development - Construction of the proposed Commercial Complex in Kalutara
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-13
decision_details_body: - It is proposed to construct a Commercial Building Complex consists of 140 stalls and 39 office rooms, linking the Bus Stand and the Railway Station,  under the Kalutara Town Centre Development Programme. The estimated cost for the purpose is Rs.200 million. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Patali Champika Ranawaka, the Minister of Megapolis and Western Development, to assign the above construction work to the Sri Lanka Land Reclamation and Development Corporation (SLLR&DC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Project for the Relocation of Manning Market,  Pettah in Peliyagoda
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-13
decision_details_body: - According to the Colombo City Development Plan (2008 - 2020) prepared by the Urban Development Authority (UDA), the areas of Pettah and Fort have been identified as an integrated development zone.  According to the said plan, the former St. John's Fish Market was relocated in Peliyagoda and it has been identified to shift the Manning Market which is famous for wholesale vegetables and fruits to the same area,  for the purpose of utilizing the area where the Manning Market is presently situated, for the provision of public transport facilities. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Patali Champika Ranawaka, the Minister of Megapolis and Western Development, to relocate the present vegetable and fruit market in Pettah, in a plot of land in extent of 25 acres in Peliyagoda, owned by  the UDA, with all facilities, at an estimated cost of Rs.4 billion, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Accession to  the Protocol to Eliminate Illicit Trade in Tobacco Products
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-13
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka is the first Asian country to ratify the Framework Convention for Tobacco Control presented by the World Health Organization (WHO), and became a party to the said Convention in 2003 as the fourth  in the world to do so. The use of tobacco products is a major risk factor for many non-communicable diseases, especially Cardiovascular conditions.  It has been confirmed that a considerable percentage of illicit tobacco products is available in Sri Lanka, in addition to the registered / licensed tobacco products. There is a tendency of using such illicit products of low cost by the certain members of low income families and minors. This situation poses serious threats on the people's health.  Therefore, the accession to the above protocol would make it possible to  implement an effective controlling mechanism to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine,  for the accession to the Protocol to Eliminate Illicit Trade in Tobacco Products, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Formulation of an Act on Sustainable Development
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-13
decision_details_body: - 'Sustainable Development' means the development that meets the needs  of the present, without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. The global community has adopted 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), covering areas and sectors especially identified to be achieved by all countries in the world by the year 2030. The Government of Sri Lanka is also bound to act with a view to achieving the said targets.  Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister,  Ranil Wickremasinghe, in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs, to draft necessary legislation for the purpose of making legislative provisions required to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Rationalization of the existing inconsistencies of the Geographical Boundaries, used as a basis in providing services by various Government institutions
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-13
decision_details_body: - In the Sri Lanka's present Regional Administrative Structure, the smallest administrative unit is the Grama Niladhari Division (GND). At present, there are 14,021 GNDs and such GNDs have been grouped into 331 Divisional Secretariats (DSs) and 25 Districts. However, it has been observed that the general public and such other parties who expect the services of the Government institutions, have to face difficulties due to the establishment of their regional units by the most of such government institutions which provide various services, deviating from the existing administrative boundaries, taking into consideration only the  requirements and comfort of such institutions.  Functioning of 160 Electorates, 336 Local Government Bodies, 340 Medical Officer of Health (MOH) areas and 311 Education Divisions presently in Sri Lanka, on the basis of geographical boundaries, can be pointed out as examples.  Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister, Ranil Wickremasinghe, in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs, to formulate a programme by the Ministry of National Policies and Economic Affairs, in association with the Ministry of Home Affairs and with the participation of all stakeholders, to remove the existing inconsistencies occurred due to the regional units established by various Government institutions, by rationalizing geographical boundaries on the basis of the Grama Niladhari Division, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Introduction of Guidelines for the construction and maintenance of Government  and Semi-government buildings as eco-friendly Green Buildings
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-13
decision_details_body: - Buildings are being rapidly constructed within the present development process and it is essential to design such buildings in an eco-friendly manner. For that purpose, the concept of 'Green Buildings' has been introduced to reduce the use of energy, water and other utilities, while creating a healthy atmosphere inside buildings. Thereby, healthy, happy and comfort environment could be created, while reducing greenhouse gas emissions and improving the level of air quality internally and externally. Within the development process of Sri Lanka, which has been planned to implement in an eco-friendly manner, action should be taken to make the built environment comfortable and to mitigate the adverse effects on the environment by the building industry. In order to achieve the said target, it has been proposed to launch a programme to construct buildings in Sri Lanka in an eco-freindly manner from the year 2016. Accordingly, the proposal made by H. E. the President, Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to appoint an Officials Committee to peruse the Guidelines already drafted, for the purpose of construction and maintenance of Government and Semi-government buildings as eco-friendly 'Green Buildings', as an initial step of that programme and to prepare an Action Plan for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The Programme for the Management of Hazardous Wastes and Chemicals emitted to the Environment of Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-13
decision_details_body:
- With the objective of mitigating the harmful effects on environment and human health, by the management of hazardous chemicals and wastes in Sri Lanka, the proposal made by H.E. the President, Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to combine the following four (04) projects and to implement them as a single programme, under the Ministry of Mahaweli Development and Environment, during the period of 2016 - 2020, while achieving the financial and institutional efficiency and to establish a Project Operations Committee comprising of the representatives of the relevant institutions to direct and monitor the project activities, was approved by the Cabinet. 

*	The project on management and disposal of polychlorinated biphenyl waste and equipment which contain that chemical, in an eco-friendly manner.

*	The project to create background for the  ratification of  Minamata Convention on Mercury and to take necessary action to achieve the objectives of that Convention. 

*	he project for the implementation of the Sub-regional Action Plan for the management and mitigation of polybrominated diphenyl ethers. 

*	The project for the manufacture  and recycling of Lead Acid Batteries in Sri Lanka, in an eco-friendly manner.

description: Disposal of stocks of paddy purchased by the Paddy Marketing Board during the Maha Season 2014/15 and Yala Season 2015
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-06
decision_details_body: - Since the paddy purchasing programme for Maha Season 2015/16 has to be commenced at the end of this month, to arrange the necessary storage facilities for the purpose, it is essential to expeditiously dispose the existing paddy stocks collected in the stores.  Accordingly, the proposal made by the Prime Minister, Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe, on the recommendation of the Cabinet Committee on Economic Management and the decision taken by the Cabinet Sub?Committee on Cost of Living, to authorize the Paddy Marketing Board to keep 54,000 Metric Tons of Nadu paddy as a buffer stock and to immediately sell the remaining 264,180 Metric Tons of Nadu Paddy and the joint proposal made by Hon. Malik Samarawickrema, the Minister of Development Strategies and International Trade; and Hon. P. Harison, the Minister of Rural Economy  in relevance to the above proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: An Accelerated Programme for the Development of Middle Income Housing & Infrastructure facilities
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-06
decision_details_body: - The Government has given a highest priority for the development of housing and human settlements and as such a pledge was made to launch an accelerated programme for the construction of 500,000 affordable housing units in the urban and suburban areas, for the lower and middle income families including the public servants and the private sector employees, through the Five Point Plan presented to the general public by the Hon. Prime Minister at the last General Election.   Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Sajith Premadasa, the Minister of Housing and Construction, to implement an accelerated programme to develop housing and infrastructure for the middle income families, was approved by the Cabinet, taking into consideration the recommendation of the Cabinet Committee on Economic Management.

description: The 6th South Asian Conference on Sanitation (SACOSAN) to be held in Bangladesh from January 11 - 13, 2016
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-06
decision_details_body: - The South Asian Conference on Sanitation (SACOSAN) is held on a biennial basis in the SAARC countries. The objective of this Conference is to accelerate the process of promoting the sanitation and hygiene and enhancing the quality of the lives of the people in South Asia.  Obtaining the political cooperation towards maintaining a better sanitation in the region is also expected from this Conference. The Sixth Session of this Conference is to be held in Bangladesh from 11th to 13th January, 2016.   The Cabinet noted the information submitted by Hon. Rauff Hakeem, the Minister of City Planning and Water Supply, that necessary action has been taken to enable the participation of a group representing Sri Lanka in this Conference, comprising of government officials, development partners, civil society organizations and school children.

description: Absorption of Officers of the Government Service into the Staff of the Election Commission
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-06
decision_details_body: - The Chairman and the other members of the Election Commission, established by the 19th Amendment to the Constitution, have been appointed on the recommendations of the Constitutional Council and the said Commission is effective from 2015-11-17.  As such, the proposal made by H.E. the President, Maithripala Sirisena, to assign the staff  served in the Department of Elections at the time of the establishment of the Election Commission, to the said Commission, to carry out the duties vested in it, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of a New Building for the Residential Project Manager's Office of Kirindi Oya Major Irrigation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-06
decision_details_body: - Due to the acquisition of the land where the Residential Project Management Office of the Kirindi Oya major irrigation situated, for  the construction of the Lunugamvehera bus stand, the said office has to be relocated in another place in that area.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Vijith Vijayamuni Zoysa, the Minister of Irrigation and Water Resources Management, to construct the said office in a plot of land in extent of 80 perches, released from a land belonging to the National Livestock Development Board and to award the contract for the construction of that office to the State Engineering Corporation functions  under the Ministry of Housing and Construction, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Upgrading of Health Facilities in the selected Hospitals under Chinese Assistance
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-06
decision_details_body: - The above project would upgrade the health facilities and substantiate the equity of healthcare services by providing priority and urgently required medical equipment, non-medical equipment, other utility equipment and infrastructure facilities to the hospitals situated in all provinces in Sri Lanka.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine, to implement the said project for the improvement of the health facilities of the hospitals identified, as per the recommendations made by the Cabinet Appointed Negotiating Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: 'Let's Awaken Polonnaruwa' - District Development Programme  2016 - 2020
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-06
decision_details_body: - The approval of the Cabinet has been granted to implement a Five Year Plan pertaining to the 'Let's Awaken Polonnaruwa' District Development Programme 2016 - 2020, for the upliftment of the living standards of the people living mainly in Polonnaruwa district and the  districts adjoining the Polonnaruwa district. The Government of the People's Republic of China has agreed to provide funds required for the projects pertaining to the areas such as drinking water, highways, railways, agriculture and irrigation identified as priority and essential projects under that programme. Accordingly, the proposal made by H.E. the President, Maithripala Sirisena, to proceed with the activities relevant to the above projects, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Release of Lands for Resettlement in Jaffna District
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-06
decision_details_body: - The resettlement of internally displaced people due to the conflict, in their places of origin is very important in building reconciliation and durable peace.  That fact has also been highlighted in the recommendations of  the Lessons Learnt and Reconciliation Commission (LLRC).  Due to non releasement of their lands for resettlement, a considerable number of families in Jaffna District, still live either in the Welfare Centres or with their friends or relatives.  Accordingly, taking into consideration the proposal made by Hon. D.M. Swaminathan, the Minister of Prison Reforms, Rehabilitation, Resettlement and Hindu Religious Affairs, the Cabinet approved to gradually release the lands identified as suitable for the resettlement of above families, without causing any hinderance to the national security.

description: Amendment of Pradeshiya Sabhas Act for the Welfare of Estate Workers
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-06
decision_details_body: - It has been identified that there is a great necessity of removing the existing legal impediments, for the successful implementation of the programmes conducted by the Government, with a view to providing the public utilities required for the estate settlements. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Faiszer Musthapha, the Minister of Provincial Councils and Local Government, to draft necessary legislation to amend the relevant provisions of the Pradeshiya Sabhas Act, No.15 of 1987, enabling the provision of public utility services required for the estate settlements, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: “Ratama Eliyai - Andura Duralai”- Implementation of the Programme of 'National Electricity Endowment'
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-06
decision_details_body: - 100% of electrification coverage has been established in the districts of Colombo, Gampaha, Kalutara, Galle, Matara and Hambantota under the Rural Electrification Projects.  An electrification coverage of nearly 90% or more also has been established in all the other districts. The target of the Government is to achieve 100% electrification coverage in the country by 2016. However, it has been revealed that about 200,000 houses have not yet obtained electricity connection, though the access to electricity is available. The main reason identified in this regard is the economic incapacity of the house owners to meet the initial expenditure involved in obtaining the electricity connections. Since the electricity is an essential factor to uplift the standard of living of the people and to improve the education of the children of low income families, the proposal made by Hon. Ranjith Siyambalapitiya, the Minister of Power and Renewable Energy, to provide loan facilities with the housing units with no electricity connections, subject to a maximum of Rs.40,000/- to obtain electricity connections to the said houses and to obtain funds required for the purpose from the Samurdhi Development Bank, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Trade Facilitation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-06
decision_details_body: - It is of paramount importance to streamline the relevant procedures pertaining to the Customs and the International Trade, in achieving the Sri Lanka's expectation of becoming a Maritime Commercial Hub. The final text of the proposed Agreement on the Trade Facilitation was adopted at the 09th  WTO Ministerial Conference held in Indonesia in December 2013, with the objective of further expediting and making easy the customs clearance and cross-border procedures followed pertaining to the import and export of goods. Member States of the organization adopted the protocol amendment in November 2014, to incorporate that Agreement into the Marrakesh Agreement, establishing the WTO and the said Agreement has to be ratified by the Member States.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Rishad Bathiudeen, the Minister of Industry and Commerce, to ratify the said Agreement, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The Southern Expressway Extension Project - Construction of  Section 2 of the Project - (Section from Beliatta to Wetiya)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-06
decision_details_body: - The Southern Expressway Extension Project extends from Matara to Hambantota and it consists of four major sections. The total length of the Expressway (from Matara to Hambantota) is 96 km. The proposal made by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, to enter into loan agreements to obtain a loan of US$ 360.29 million, which amounts to the 85% of the funds required for the construction of the second section of the said project (from Beliatta to Wetiya - 26 km),  from the EXIM Bank of China under the Preferential Buyer Credit (PBC) facility and the balance of 15% which amounts to US$ 63.58 million from the Hatton National Bank, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The progress of the project for the payment of 30% of the Employees’ Provident Fund
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-06
decision_details_body: - Releasing of pre-benefits amounting to 30% from the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) for housing activities and medical facilities was commenced in the mid 2015, in terms of the provisions of the Employees' Provident Fund Act, No.15 of 1958 as amended by the Act, No.2 of 2012. The Cabinet noted the information submitted by Hon. W.D.J. Seneviratne,  the Minister of Labour and Trade Union Relations, that 70,269 applications have been received up to now to obtain such benefits and sum of Rs. 5.5 billion has been released by now for 7,537 applications so received, that the action is being taken to provide benefits for the remaining applications without any delay, and that it has been planned to implement this process more productively in future.

description: Programme for Introducing the ‘Virusara' Privilege Card for War Heroes
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2016-01-06
decision_details_body: - It has been decided to introduce a privilege card known as 'Virusara', so that the War Heroes of the Tri- Forces, the Police and the Civil Security Department, who laid their lives, found missing and who were disabled during the active service for building peace and  upholding the sovereignty of Sri Lanka and their dependents could obtain privileges.  Through this card, they would be able to have special privileges when purchasing consumer items and obtaining services in number of fields such as health, education, banking, insurance and leasing.  Accordingly, as the first phase of this programme, this card will be provided to 50,000 War Heroes. The Cabinet noted the information submitted by H.E. the President, Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Defence, that the ceremony for awarding the privilege card to the 5,000 of War Heroes and their dependents, will be held on 2016.01.25 at the Temple Trees under the patronage of H.E. the President, and with the participation of Hon. Prime Minister and the State Minister of Defence.

description: The Law to Introduce National Minimum Wage for Employees of the Private Sector
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-12-23
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Ravindra Samaraweera, the Acting Minister of Labour and Trade Union Relations, to obtain the approval for the Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman, in relation to the introduction of a National Minimum Wage for the employees of the Private Sector, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Increase of Wages of Private Sector Employees
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-12-23
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Ravindra Samaraweera, the Acting Minister of Labour and Trade Union Relations, to obtain the approval for the Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman, in relation to the increase of wages of the Private Sector employees, as recommended by the Budget Proposals of 2016, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Award of Contract for upgrading Tissamaharama Water Supply Scheme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-12-23
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet granted approval on 2015-11-18 to upgrade the Tissamaharama Water Supply Scheme, at a cost of Rs.393 million, on a proposal made by Hon. Sajith Premadasa, the Minister of Housing and Construction. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Rauff Hakeem, the Minister of City Planning and Water Supply, for the National Water Supply and Drainage Board to undertake the construction work comes under its purview under the said project and to handover the other construction work to the State Development and Construction Corporation, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The proposed Memoranda of Understanding to be signed between the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Government of Pakistan
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-12-23

description: Police Hospital Expansion Project at Narahenpita - Completion of the Balance Work
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-12-23
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Sagala Ratnayaka, the Minister of Law & Order and Southern Development, to award the Contract for the completion of the balance work remaining under the Police Hospital Expansion Project at Narahenpita, in accordance with the recommendation of the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Supply, Installation & Commissioning of Air Traffic Management System at Bandaranaike International Airport, Katunayake
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-12-23
decision_details_body: - The Air Traffic Management System presently being used at the Bandaranaike International Airport, Katunayaka is utilized for the controlling of the air traffic in the high traffic density air space around the Airport. In order to assure safe air traffic controlling around the Airport which suits the present day needs, the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala de Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, for the supply, installation and commissioning of an Air Traffic Management System, at an estimated cost of Rs.320 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Increase of the limit of monetary value in respect of the disputes to be referred to compulsory mediation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-12-23
decision_details_body: - It was provided in the Section 7 (a) of the Mediation Boards Act, No.72 of 1988, that the disputes in relation to movable or immovable property or a debt, damage or demand, which do not exceed Rs.25,000/- in value should be referred to compulsory mediation. That compulsory limit was increased up to Rs.250,000/- by the Mediation Boards (Amendment) Act, No.04 of 2011. In order to increase this monetary limit up to Rs.500,000/- on present requirements, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Wijayadasa Rajapaksa, the Minister of Justice, to amend the Mediation Boards Act, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Proposed Ratification of ILO Convention (C 122) of 1964 on Employment Policy
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-12-23
decision_details_body: - The International Labour Organization (ILO) adopted 'the Convention C 122 on the Employment Policy' and its accompanying 'Recommendation R 122' in 1964. The Convention C 122 basically calls upon the ratifying states to declare and pursue an active policy designed to promote full, productive and freely chosen employment, in consultation with the workers' and employers' representatives. 'The National Human Resources and Employment Policy of Sri Lanka' launched in the year 2013 provides the framework for full, productive and freely chosen employment. The ratification of the Convention C 122 will further strengthen the functioning of the labour standard system as well as the social policy of the country. Further, it will be important for the governance as well. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. W.D.J. Seneviratne, the Minister of Labour and Trade Union Relations, to ratify the ILO Convention C 122 on Employment Policy (1964), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Ratification of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-12-23
decision_details_body: - 'The International Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities' was adopted in the year 2006 by the United Nations General Assembly, in keeping with the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) and the International Conventions on Human Rights. Sri Lanka has become a signatory to that Convention in the year 2007 and having considered that the enforcement of that Convention in Sri Lanka would be more important for the best interests of the persons with disabilities, the proposal made by Hon. S.B. Dissanayake, the Minister of Social Empowerment and Welfare, to ratify the said Convention, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Promoting conservation of Bio-Diversity in environmentally sensitive land tracts and maintenance of services of Ecosystems
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-12-23
decision_details_body:
- 'The Project to Promote Conservation of Bio-diversity in Environmentally Sensitive Land Tracts in Sri Lanka and Maintenance of Services of Ecosystems' was granted to Sri Lanka by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and Global Environment Facility (GEF), and the main objective of the said project is to declare environmentally sensitive land tracts as a mechanism to ensure that the development activities implemented in the areas of high environmental importance, in a manner that conserves bio-diversity and the services of ecosystems and to identify two pilot areas for establishing and maintaining such mechanism. Accordingly, the proposal made by H.E. the President, Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to implement this project in the following pilot areas, within a period of 5 years, utilizing the grant of US$ 2.62 million, was approved by the Cabinet:  

*	The environmentally sensitive land tract in Kalawewa - Ipalogama, Palagala, Kekirawa and Galnewa Divisional Secretariat Divisions in the Anuradhapura District.  

*	The environmentally sensitive land tract in Wilpattu - Wanathavilluwa Divisional Secretariat Division in the Puttalam District.

description: Green Fishery Harbour Project - Mirissa
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-12-23
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by H.E the President, Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to implement the 'Green Fishery Harbour Project' prepared by the Marine Environment Protection Authority, at an investment of Rs.30.4 million of local funds, with a view to building the sustainability of the fisheries and tourism industries associated with the Mirissa Fishery Harbour through converting the said harbour, which is one of the major harbours situated in the Southern Province, into a Green Fishery Harbour, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Ministry of Finance of Sri Lanka and Export Credit Bank of Turkey (TURK Exim Bank)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-12-16
decision_details_body: - In order to strengthen the journey towards country's development, it has become necessary to attract new development partners and enhance the  number of existing development partners. Accordingly, with a view to strengthening the bilateral relationship between Sri Lanka and Turkey, which is an active member of G-20 group of developed countries and currently holds the presidency of that group, through financial cooperation, it has been proposed to sign a MoU between Sri Lanka and Export Credit Bank of Turkey.  Under this MoU, the TURK Exim Bank will agree to provide a credit line in an amount of US$ 350 million  for the implementation of priority development projects of the Government of Sri Lanka.
