Anura Priyadarshana Yapa, the Minister of Disaster Management, to implement the project for 'improving the forecasting capabilities of the Department of Meteorology to minimize the impact of frequent weather hazards', was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Galagedara and Mawathagama Water Supply Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-11
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Rauff Hakeem, the Minister of City Planning and Water Supply, to implement the above project with a view to providing safe drinking water to the people of Galagedara and Mawathagama areas and also to proceed with the activities related to it, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Bilateral Air Service Agreement between Sri Lanka and Serbia
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-11
decision_details_body: - Serbia, an upper middle income country in the Eastern Europe contributes largely to its national income through the Tourism Industry and has entered into bilateral Air Service Agreements with 13 countries of the European Union. Considering the increasing demand in the tourism sector in Sri Lanka, it appears that the aviation links that Serbia has created with other countries can also be used to develop Aviation and  Tourism industry in Sri Lanka.  Especially, by granting permission to aeroplanes of Serbia to arrive and depart from the Mattala Airport, under the proposed bilateral agreement, will pave the way for the utilization of that Airport in an effective manner. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala de Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, to sign the already initialed Air Services Agreement between Sri Lanka and Serbia in officer level, by an accredited representative and thereafter, to give effect to the said agreement, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: 'Awakening Polonnaruwa' Development Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-11
decision_details_body: - Development of transport facilities connecting Polonnaruwa and the other cities situated in close proximity to Polonnaruwa has been identified as a priority under the 'Awakening Polonnaruwa' Development Project. Although there are trains run across the Polonnaruwa District currently, the trains are not popular among general public due to reasons such as taking a long time to travel and inadequate train operations. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala De Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, to conduct a comprehensive feasibility study for the rehabilitation of the Railway Network from Maho to Batticaloa and from Gal-oya to Trincomalee and for the development of the Railway Stations so as to provide essential facilities with the general public, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Signing of a Memorandum of Understanding on Technical Cooperation between Sri Lanka and Thailand for the Development of Human Resources  in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-11
decision_details_body: - The bilateral technical cooperation between the Government of Sri Lanka and the Government of Thailand plays a significant role in the development of Human Resources in Sri Lanka. The Thailand International Development Cooperation Agency (TICA) has prepared a five year Development Cooperation Programme in collaboration with the Government of Sri Lanka, to provide scholarships and training programmes in the areas of Agriculture, Food Technology, Rural Development and Sufficiency Economy, Tourism Management and Diplomatic Training to Sri Lanka, during the period of 2015-2019.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Prime Minister Ranil Wickremasingh, in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs, to sign a Memorandum of Understanding with the Government of Thailand, to promote Technical Cooperation Programmes between the two countries, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Government Intervention to stabilize the price at Colombo Tea Auction
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body:
- Due to the crises in the countries that buy tea from Sri Lanka, the demand for our tea has gone down and the price of tea in comparison with that of 2014, has been declining considerably from the beginning of this year. Although, the production cost of a kilogram of tea, generally, is Rs.450/-, the price per kilogram of tea had dropped to Rs.385.51 by August at the tea auction. This situation had adversely affected all stakeholders engaged in the tea plantation sector including the regional plantation companies. In order to provide relief for the tea plantation sector, a scheme was implemented to pay a guaranteed price for green leaves produced by tea smallholders at the cost of Rs.6000 million while loans were given to factory owners for their working capital on  concessionary terms, as well. In a situation where the price of tea falls steadily, providing the above concessions alone is not practical, and the Government has to intervene in order to increase the price of tea at the auction. 

	When a similar drop in tea prices occurred in 2008 as a result of the World Economic Crisis, the fall of tea prices was controlled satisfactorily by the Government through purchasing tea at the auction. Taking into consideration the proposal made by Hon. Navin Dissanayake, the Minister of Plantation Industries, to provide the necessary funds by the Government to purchase good quality tea at a price of Rs.430/- per kg, through the Sri Lanka Tea Board, was approved by the Cabinet. The Government will cease to purchase tea in this manner, once the price of a kilogram of tea reaches the level Rs.450/- at the tea auction.

description: 18. Introduction of a New Protective Label (sticker) for all Liquor Bottles manufactured in Sri Lanka or imported to Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body: - Since liquor is heavily taxed by the Government, illegally blended and packed liquor evade tax and enter into the market. In the circumstances, many consumers resort to more harmful liquor. Furthermore, since the liquor produced after paying taxes is expensive, the availability of a substitute in illegally produced liquor adversely affects Government's revenue. Therefore, in order to prevent counterfeit products being brought to the market, the proposal made by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, to make it mandatory to affix a protective label (sticker) on every legally manufactured liquor bottle, under the supervision of the Department of Excise and also to make the importers aware that it is mandatory to affix protective labels on imported liquor within the Customs itself prior to issuance to the market, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining a Technical Cooperation Grant of eruo 7 million from the 	Government of Federal Republic of Germany
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body: - The Government of the Federal Republic of Germany has agreed to provide a Technical Cooperation Grant amounting to euro 7 million for the implementation of three projects, namely, the Management project of Wilpattu National Park and the Buffer Zone around it, Education Project for Social Integration and the Small and Medium Scale Enterprise Development Project and as such, the proposal made by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance to sign the exchange notes between the two countries for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)/World Bank held in Lima, Peru, from 8th to 11th October 2015
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body:
- Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, informed the Cabinet that a delegation comprised of the Senior Officials of the General Treasury and the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) headed by him,  participated at the above mentioned annual meetings representing Sri Lanka and that discussions were held during said meetings on the future global economic outlook with emphasis on the issues relating to  emerging markets and the economic issues relevant to developing countries. The Hon. Minister also informed the Cabinet that adverse effects such as slow growth in the production sector of the economies of respective countries and the political crises faced by most countries have been identified as the reasons for the major issues faced by the developing countries and that the importance of adopting policies properly listed according to priority by the developing countries, in order to face risks such as financial instability, unemployment and income disparity that may arise due to global economic development falling behind the expected level, was also emphasized. 

	The Minister of Finance, further informed the Cabinet that many fruitful discussions were held with the Finance Ministers of the countries which are important stakeholders of our foreign trade as well as with the senior officials of the World Bank and IMF.

description: The Issuance of a Commemorative Stamp to mark the 60 years of Sri Lanka-Thailand Diplomatic Relationship
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body: - The year 2015 marks 60 years from the commencement of diplomatic relations between Sri Lanka and Thailand.  As per a proposal made by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, arrangements have been made to issue two commemorative stamps each, by the Postal Department of Sri Lanka and the Postal Institute of Thailand to commemorate this event.  These stamps be issued based on 'Buddhism', which is a common theme for both  countries, by which it is expected to develop mutual conviviality between the people of the two countries.  The first day issue of these stamps was held on the 02nd November, 2015 in Thailand by the Postal Institute of Thailand, concurrent to the official visit of His Excellency the President of Sri Lanka to Thailand while it is to be held in Sri Lanka by the Postal Department on 20th November, 2015.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. M.H.A. Haleem, the Minister of Posts, Postal Services and Muslim Religious Affairs,  to sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in respect of the issuance of the commemorative stamps, between the Postal Department of Sri Lanka and the Postal Institute of Thailand, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Considering the Higher National Diploma in Accountancy (HNDA) awarded by the SLIATE as an alternative qualification for the B.Com Degree
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body:
- Due to the cancellation of the Public Administration Circular No.46/90, issued in the year 1990, that considered the Higher National Diploma in Accountancy (HNDA) awarded by the Sri Lanka Institute of Advanced Technological Education (SLIATE) as an alternative qualification to the Bachelor of Commerce Degree, through the Public Administration Circular No.10/2014 last year, the students who have completed the said Course are facing a considerable difficulty when applying for jobs in the public sector. This has caused an unrest among the students who follow the said Diploma, since the demand for the said Diploma holders from the private sector for job opportunities has also decreased, based on this precedent. 

	Since a very small number of 23,500 students are enrolled annually at state universities out of the 142,000 students who qualify for university entrance based on G.C.E. (A/L) results, a large number of students who had studied under the Commerce stream and lost university admission despite having very high results, follow the said Course given their economic background. Considering this situation, the proposal made by Hon. Lakshman Kiriella the Minister of Higher Education and Highways,  to re‑enforce the Public Administration Circular No.46/90, by which the Higher National Diploma in Accountancy (HNDA) is treated as an alternative qualification to the Bachelor of Commerce (B.Com) Degree, with effect from 2014‑04‑23 was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining Financial Assistance from the International Fund for Agricultural Development for the Implementation of the Smallholder Tea and Rubber Revitalization (STARR) Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body: - With the objective of sustainably developing the small scale tea and rubber cultivation sector, the Government has commenced a Revitalization Programme in the said sector, with the financial assistance of the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD). Under this programme, aiding the increase of tea harvest in currently cultivated 5,500 hectares of lands in the Matara, Galle, Ratnapura, Badulla and Kandy District, is anticipated. This programme will also contribute to the increase of the rubber harvest of 3,000 hectares of new rubber estates in the Moneragala and Ampara Districts. The total investment for this project is US$ 65.4 million, of which US$ 25.7 million will be provided by the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD). Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Ranil Wickramasinghe, the Prime Minister, in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs to enter into an Agreement with the IFAD for said purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Green Power Development and Energy Efficiency Improvement Investment Programme - Construction of Kappalthurai Grid Substation and the Augmentation of Kerawalapitiya, Trincomalee and Katunayake Grid Substations
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Ranjith Siyambalapitiya, the Minister of Power and Renewable Energy,  to award the contract for the construction of Kappalthurai Grid Substation and the augmentation of Kerawalapitiya, Trincomalee and Katunayake Grid Substations, under the Green Power Development and Energy Efficiency Improvement Investment Programme, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Green Power Development and Energy Efficiency Improvement Investment Programme - Construction of Kalutara,Kesbewa, old Anuradhapura Grid Substations and the Augmentation of New Anuradhapura Grid Substations
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Ranjith Siyambalapitiya, the Minister of Power and Renewable Energy,  to award the contract for the construction of Kalutara,  Kesbewa an old Anuradhapura Grid Substations and  the augmentation of New Anuradhapura Grid Substation, under the Green Power Development and Energy Efficiency Improvement Investment Programme, to the lowest responsive bidder, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Supply of Official Uniforms and other Clothing Materials for the Sri Lanka Police - 2015
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Tilak Marapana, the Minister of Law & Order and Prison Reforms, to purchase the official uniforms required for the Sri Lanka Police for the year 2015, from the local textile manufacturers, as recommended by the Local Textile Allocation Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Asian Development Bank Assisted Greater Colombo Water & Waste Water Management Improvement Investment Programme - Ambatale Water Supply System Improvement and Energy Saving Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Rauff Hakeem, the Minister of City Planning and Water Supply, to award the contract for the laying of water supply pipelines along a distance of 09 km. from Ambatale to Ellie House reservoir, under the Ambatale Water Supply System Improvement and Energy Saving Project under the Greater Colombo Water and Wastewater Management Improvement Investment Programme assisted by the Asian Development Bank (ADB), as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the University of Ruhuna Township Development 	Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body:
- The Government has planned to develop a University Township with all amenities found in a modern University, treating the University of Ruhuna which is situated in the Wellamadama area in close proximity to the Matara town, as its centre.  Accordingly, it has been planned to develop two subprojects under this project, namely the development of Ruhuna University Township and the common amenities therein and the development of a Marine and Fresh Water Aquariums and related infrastructure, at an estimated investment of Rs.2,512.8 million 

	The following development programmes are proposed to be implemented under the proposed first subproject:

*	demarcation and the declaration of the boundaries of the University Township;

*	construction of an irrigation canal connecting the Kumbalgama Lake and the Devundar Lagoon and the establishment of a walking track along one of its banks; and

*	construction of a swimming pool in the University Township and development of sports and recreational facilities around the area.

	Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Lakshman Kiriella, the Minister of Higher Education and Highways, to implement the first subproject under the Ruhunu University Township Development Project, at an investment of Rs.556.6 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding of contracts for the buildings constructed at the University of Kelaniya, Peradeniya  and  the Postgraduate Institute of Medicine
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body:
- The proposal made by Hon. Lakshman  Kiriella, the Minister of Higher Education and Highways, to award the following contracts,  as recommended by the Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committees (CAPCs), was approved by the Cabinet: 

(i)	the contract for the development of the Postgraduate Institute of Medicine - Rs.1,412.4 million; 

(ii)	the contract for the construction of a building complex  for the Department of Industrial Management of the Faculty of Science, University of Kelaniya to facilitate the introduction of new degree courses in the field of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) - Rs.430.1 million; and

(iii) the contract for the development of the Faculty of Agriculture of the University of Peradiniya - Rs.342.3 million.

description: Vesting the Ownership of Farms maintained in the State Lands by National Livestock Development Board, with the said Board, on Long Term Lease Basis
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body: - The National Livestock Development Board (NLDB) maintains 13 farms on State lands throughout the Island  in order to provide quality support services to the farmers and entrepreneurs for the development of the livestock sector in Sri Lanka. However, the ownership or the lease rights of such lands have not yet been vested on the said Board and the said lands remain as State lands.  As such, the joint proposal made by Hon. P. Harison, the Minister of Rural Economy, and Hon. M.K.A.D.S. Gunawardana, the Minister of Lands, to transfer the lands on which the NLDB farms are situated, to the National Livestock Board on long term lease basis, enabling the implementation of necessary plans designed to more productively develop and expand the said farms, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the Food Production National Programme 2016-2018
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body: - Approval was granted by the Cabinet on 2015-10-14 for the implementation of the 'Food Production National Programme 2016-2018' presented by H.E. the President. Accordingly, a National Programme has been prepared by the Ministry of Agriculture with a view to ensuring food security, reducing imports through producing additional food crops locally and thereby saving foreign exchange as proposed in the said programme.  In order to ensure food security in the country under this national programme, it has been proposed to identify and implement two main components namely improvement of crop production and implementation of programmes on 14 identified main sectors that are essential for agricultural development. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Duminda Dissanayake, the Minister of Agriculture, to implement the above mentioned programme during the period of 2016-2018 and to secure provisions required for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Introduction of Locally Manufactured Smart Meters to the Energy 	Sector in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body: - During the recent past, the Energy Sector in Sri Lanka has gained an enormous advance and by now action has been taken to provide almost 100% electricity coverage by providing an uninterrupted electricity supply throughout the Island for the entire 24 hours. The Global Electricity Technology is being modernized daily and immense advantages could be gained to the national economy by making the generation, distribution and consumption of power more efficient through the adoption of advanced technological methods. In this regard, the introduction of Smart Electric Meters to the local Energy Sector is an essential priority. The use of Smart Electric Meters helps for the better management of electricity demand and at the same time it provides services such as making the consumers aware of the voluntarily control of electricity consumption and regulating the operation of machines with remote air conditioners. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Ranjith Siyambalapitiya, the Minister of Power and Renewable Energy, to commence a project to manufacture and develop Smart Electric Meters required for the domestic market, at a cost of Rs.49.2 million, as a joint project of Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) and the University of Peradeniya, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment of Fisheries (Regulation of Foreign Fishing Boats) Act, No.59 of 1979
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body: - The Fisheries (Regulation of Foreign Fishing Boats) Act, No.59 of 1979 provides for the regulation, control and management of fishing and related activities of foreign boats in Sri Lankan waters.  However, it has become necessary to introduce a new Act to amend the existing provisions, due to significant changes that have taken place in this field internationally and regionally, during the past three decades or so.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Mahinda Amaraweera, the Minister of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources Development,  to amend the Fisheries (Regulation of Foreign Fishing Boats) Act, No.59 of 1979, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Gampaha, Attanagalle and Minuwangoda Integrated Water Supply Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Rauff Hakeem, the Minister of City Planning and Water Supply, to implement the above project at a total cost of US$229.5 million and Rs.3,910 million,  providing benefits to the people living in the areas of Gampaha, Attanagalle and Minuwangoda and to secure the required funds for the purpose,  was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of Third Phase of the Greater Colombo Water and Waste Water Management Improvement Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-11-05
decision_details_body: - The Greater Colombo Water and Waste Water Management Improvement Programme is implemented under three (03) phases through the multi-tranche financing facilities of the Asian Development Bank (ADB)  and Government funds. It is expected to increase the efficiency of the water supply in Greater Colombo through this programme. The total investment of third Phase is US $168.46 million and out of that an amount of US $40.46 million will be contributed by the Government of Sri Lanka.  The proposal made by the Hon.  Ranil Wickremasinghe, the Prime Minister, in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs, to obtain the balance of US $128 million, as a concessionary loan from the Asian Development Bank (ADB), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Increasing Excise Duty on Cigarettes and Liquor
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-10-28
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance to present the Gazette Notification issued to increase the Excise duty on cigarettes, arrack and locally produced and foreign liquor, in Parliament, in terms of Section 3 of the Excise (Special Provisions) Act No.13 of 1989, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Preparation of Western Region Megapolis Master Plan
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-10-28
decision_details_body: - The preliminary works such as collection of data, preparation of preliminary plans and the drafting of legislation, pertaining to the preparation of the Western Region Megapolis Master Plan have been completed by now and the proposal made by Hon. Patali Champika Ranawaka, the Minister of Megapolis and Western Development,  to obtain the service of the local and foreign experts who provide consultancy for the project, for a further period of four (04) months, in order to further proceed with the project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Asian Development Bank funded Integrated Road Investment Programme - Award of contracts for four civil work contract packages in the Sabaragamuwa Province
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-10-28
decision_details_body: - The Integrated Road Investment Programme (i-Road Project) is implemented with the objective of improving the connectivity among the selected Rural Centres through rehabilitation of National Roads, Provincial Roads and processing           By-Roads and Access Roads.  The proposal made by Hon. Lakshman Kiriella, the Minister of Higher Education and Highways, to award the four contracts, under this programme, pertaining to rehabilitation and improvement of 75 km of rural roads in the Kegalle District at a cost of Rs.1,972 million and 255 km of rural roads in the Ratnapura District at a cost of Rs.6,425 million, as per the recommendation made by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development of Infrastructure facilities of the Universities and Higher Education Institutes to cater the Degrees related to the Subject of Technology
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-10-28
decision_details_body: - Out of the students who have sat for the G.C.E. Advanced Level for the first time under the Technology Stream, 1,800 students are to be admitted to the Universities in the year 2016 as the first batch, who have gained eligibility for the University entrance and the facilities required for the purpose have to be established in the Universities. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Lakshman Kiriella, the Minister of Higher Education and Highways, to allocate provision to construct the buildings necessary and to purchase the equipment necessary for the Universities of Rajarata, Colombo, Wayamba, Ruhuna and Sri Jayawardenepura, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding Consultancy Contract on Project Programme Management, Design and Supervision for the Implementation of Mahaweli Water Security Investment Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-10-28
decision_details_body:
- The following projects have been planned to be implemented to avoid the water shortage in the Northern Province and the Eastern Province under the Mahaweli Water Security Investment Programme funded by the Asian Development Bank: 

*	transferring the Mahaweli water from Kaluganga - Moragahakanda Reservoirs through the 65km long Upper Elehera Canal to be distributed through the newly constructing North Central Canal Project.

*	transferring the excessive Mahaweli water of Dambulu Oya and Nalanda Reservoir to the Upper Mee Oya basin and the Hakwatuna Oya basin to address the water shortage in the North Western Province through the newly constructing North Western Province Canal Project.

* 	Increasing the height of the  Anicut situated at Minipe across the Maharani river and rehabilitate the 74 km long Minipe Left Bank Canal.

The proposal made by H.E. the President, Maithripala Sirisena, in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment to award the consultancy service contract for the management, design and supervision of programmes relevant to these projects as per the recommendations made by the Cabinet Appointed Negotiation Committee (CANC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the Second Phase of the Pipe Laying Project  from Andaragasyaya underground  tank to Gonnoruwa as a solution to the acute drinking water issue in the Hambantota District
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-10-28
decision_details_body: - Nearly 12,000 people belonging to 3,000 families of Bandagirya, Keliyapura, Ketanwewa, Gonnoruwa, Andarawewa, Kuda Indiwewa and Handilla areas in Hambantota District are experiencing various economic, social and health problems from a long period of time due to the acute shortage of water in the area. As a sustainable solution to this problem, the activities are being carried out by the Government to provide 250 new water connections at a cost of Rs. 465 million as the first phase of the construction of a water system for the distribution of water from underground water tank constructed under the Ruhunupura Water Supply Project. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Sajith Premadasa, the Minister of Housing and Construction, to implement the second phase of that project enabling to provide water facilities for 11,272 people through constructing a pipe borne water system with further 2,818 water connections from the Andaragasyaya underground water tank at a cost of Rs. 214.93 million, as a solution  to the problem of acute shortage of water exists in the areas which do not get water facilities from the above first phase, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding between the Ministry of Agriculture of Sri Lanka and the Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation of Egypt for Co-operation in the field of Agriculture and other related fields
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-10-28
decision_details_body: - Although, the Egypt is a country consisting of dry and arid climatic zones, and with limited arable land areas, the agriculture field has become a prominent sector in the country.  Therefore, there is a possibility of applying the new technology and knowledge used by them in the field of agriculture, for the agricultural development in the dry zone areas of our country too, as appropriate.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Duminda Dissanayake, the Minister of Agriculture, to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding between the Ministry of Agriculture of Sri Lanka and the Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation of Egypt, in order to exchange information and experiences in the fields of crop production, food processing, advertising, marketing and the use of machinery for agricultural activities, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development Projects to be implemented in the Health Sector
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-10-28
decision_details_body: - The Government has taken steps to establish a strongly developed Public Healthcare System in the country by providing a free health service to each and every citizen regardless of their ability to pay.  Almost 100% of the preventive services, 90% to 95% of inpatient care services and about 50% of the ambulatory care services are provided through the Health Care Institutes of Public Sector which are maintained from the public funds. The new government has given a high policy priority for the improvement of the health sector and it is due to allocate 3% of the Gross Domestic Product for the health sector in the year 2016 in contrast to the 1.8% of allocation made in the year 2015. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. (Dr.) Rajitha Senaratne, the Minister of Health, Nutrition and Indigenous Medicine, to implement number of projects pertaining to the improvement of curative care, hospital supportive systems, human resources and infrastructure development within the Mid Term Budgetary Framework 2016 - 2018, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of the National Research Council as a Statutory Entity
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-10-28
decision_details_body: - The execution of the task of planning, coordinating and facilitating research in Science and Technology so as to build a vibrant national  scientific and technological community in the country is expected from the National Research Council (NRC). This institute has not been established by a Parliamentary Act in the year 2007, but through a directive made by the then President in terms of the powers vested with him by the Constitution. The proposal made by Hon. Susil Premajayantha, the Minister of Science, Technology and Research, to draft necessary legislation to establish the NRC as a statutory entity through an Act of Parliament, in order to conduct its affairs in a more formal manner, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Assigning Two Blocks of Lands belonging to Mahaweli Authority of Sri Lanka on which Sri Lanka Transport Board (SLTB) Embilipitiya Depot is situated,  to the SLTB
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-10-28
decision_details_body: - Embilipitiya Depot was established in the year 1975 in a land belonging to the River Valleys Development Board, and subsequently in the year 1981 that land has been brought under the Mahaweli Authority of Sri Lanka.  The ownership of the land has not yet been formally and legally vested with the Sri Lanka Transport Board (SLTB).  Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. Nimal Siripala De Silva, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, to vest the two blocks of land where the said Depot is situated, with the Sri Lanka Transport Board, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Building Complex for the Faculty of Health Care Sciences in the Eastern University
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-10-28
decision_details_body: - The Faculty of Health Care Sciences of the Eastern University was established in 2004 with 06 study departments and currently about 425 students read for the Bachelors degree courses in Medicine, Surgery (MBBS) and Science Nursing in this faculty which is situated in the Batticaloa District. Presently, this Faculty functions at a temporary building taken over from the Paddy Marketing Board. The Ministry of Higher Education and Highways has prepared estimates to construct a new building complex for this Faculty and a sum of US$ 47.3 million (Rs.6,617.5 million) is required for the purpose. Out of this sum, Kuwait Fund for Arab Economic Development (KFAED) has agreed to provide US$ 34 million, as a concessionary loan and as such, the proposal made by the Prime Minister, Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe in his capacity as the Minister of National Policies and Economic Affairs, to enter into the relevant agreement for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Request for Proposals for the Construction of Houses for the Families affected by the Conflict
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-22
decision_details_body: - The Ministry of Rehabilitation, Resettlement and Hindu Religious Affairs has been entrusted with the responsibility of constructing houses for the conflict affected families in the Northern and Eastern Provinces on a priority basis. The necessity of fulfilling the shelter requirements in the conflict affected areas has also been emphasized in the recommendations of the Lessons Learnt and Reconciliation Commission (LLRC).  Accordingly, it has been identified that a further 137,529 houses have to be constructed in addition to the 44,000 houses which are being constructed under the sponsorship of the Indian Government. Therefore, the proposal made by Hon. D.M. Swaminathan, the Minister of Rehabilitation, Resettlement and Hindu Religious Affairs, to request for proposals from both local and foreign parties interested in the construction of houses for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Use of Information Technology (IT) in order to implement Safety Net and Social Welfare Programmes Effectively
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-22
decision_details_body: The Government annually allocates a considerable amount of funds for social welfare, safety net programmes and pensions.  These programmes are designed to protect citizens from the economic risks.  These programmes provide benefits to the elderly or retired, the sick or invalid, dependents, mothers, the unemployed, the work-injured, school children etc. The proposal made by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, to make use of Information Technology for the monitoring and management of all welfare programmes under a Centralized Unit to ensure that these programmes achieve their set objectives, the efficient management of  subsidy dispensed by these welfare programmes and the distribution of  subsidies to the right beneficiaries, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Improving the Infrastructure Facilities of the Government Information Technology and Communication
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-22
decision_details_body: The Government of Sri Lanka has taken many progressive measures introducing Information and Communication Technology (ICT) to the Government Institutions. Such initiatives have contributed towards bringing in awareness of ICT and increased use of ICT equipment and solutions in the Government Institutions.  However, the internet links in most of the Ministries and Government Institutions function extremely slow and as a result it has become difficult to collaborate with other Government Institutes in sharing documents and in the process of approval.  Due to the instability of the network connection, most of the Government officers have found it difficult even to sending messages via e-mail.  At the same time, one of the key constraints attributed by all Government Institutions as a major deterrence towards implementing ICT solutions is the unavailability of proper Government Computing Infrastructure facilities which host services for Information Technology (IT) systems, connectivity and secure data communication. However, a large amount of money is spent from the Government Budget to maintain such IT connectivity.  One of the primary objectives of the Ministry of Finance is to establish a mechanism to enable the efficient use of Government Funds and it is linked with the implementation of IT solutions as well.  Therefore, it is utmost important to provide proper computing infrastructure facilities to the Government Institutions. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, to design and implement a digital infrastructure for high speed internet connection, secured communications for efficient collaboration within the Government by upgrading its Lanka Government Network (LGN) through the Information and Communication Technology Agency of Sri Lanka (ICTA) being the apex ICT Institution of the country, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Prevention of Child Abuse
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-22
decision_details_body:
- The proposal made by the Prime Minister Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe, to appoint a Ministerial Committee comprising of the following, to make proposals on the suitable action to be taken to prevent daily increasing  child abuses,  was approved by the Cabinet. 

*	Hon. Thilak Marapana, Minister of Law & Order and Prison Reforms (Chairman)

*	Hon. Wijayadasa Rajapaksa, Minister of Justice 

*	Hon. (Mrs.) Chandrani Bandara, Minister of Women and Child Affairs 

*	Hon. (Mrs.) Wijayakala Maheswaran, State Minister of Child Affairs

*	Hon. (Mrs.) Sudharshani  Fernandopulle, State Minister of City Planning and Water Supply

description: Obtaining the Approval of Parliament for the Gazette Notifications Published
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-22
decision_details_body: The proposal made by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance,  to present the Gazette Notifications issued in accordance with the decisions taken time to time by the Government with regard to various tax revisions made for the welfare of the people or with regard to the collection of  revenue for the purpose, in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: 68th Independence Day Celebration
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-22
decision_details_body: The proposal made by Hon. Vajira Abeywardena, the Minister of Home Affairs, for the appointment of a Ministerial Committee under the Chairmanship of the Prime Minister Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe and with the participation of other relevant Ministers, to make policy decisions and provide guidance with regard to the conducting of the 68th Independence Day  Celebration which falls on 04th February 2016, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The Cabinet Sub-Committee on Economic Management and the Cabinet Sub-Committee on Cost of Living
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-22
decision_details_body: - Appointment of the Cabinet Sub-Committee on Economic Management under the Chairmanship of the Prime Minister Hon. Ranil Wickremasinghe and comprised of the relevant Ministers, to make recommendations to the Cabinet with regard to the proposals on overall economic development of the country, and the appointment of the Cabinet Sub-Committee on Cost of Living under the Chairmanship of Hon. Malik Samarawickrema, the Minister of Development Strategies and International Trade and comprised of the relevant Ministers, to make recommendations to the Cabinet with regard to the matters affect the living condition of the people of the country, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: To provide a Nutritional Food Package worth of Rs. 20,000/- with the Pregnant Mothers
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-22
decision_details_body: - The programme on provision of a Nutritional Food Package worth of Rs. 20,000/- to the Pregnant Mothers was commenced under the 100 Day Programme of the Government and  by now, the programme is in progress successfully. Having considered the proposal made by Hon. (Mrs) Chadrani Bandara, the Minister of Women and Child Affairs, the Cabinet approved the provision of further Rs.1,500 million to the Ministry, in addition to the Rs.1,500 million already allocated for year 2015, for the continuous implementation of this project.

description: 50,000 accelerated Housing Development Programme implemented by the National Housing Development Authority
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-22
decision_details_body: - 'Shelter for All' ('Samata Sevana') 50,000 Housing Programme launched under the 100 day programme of the Government operates in accordance with the community participatory method and as of now, construction activities of 35,290 houses are in progress.  The estimated cost for the entire project is Rs.5,000 million and out of which a sum of Rs.1,328.45 million has already been incurred by now. The proposal made by Hon. Sajith Premadasa, the Minister of Housing and Construction, to secure the funds further required to complete this programme, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Programme on renovation of 25,000 houses to mark the World Habitat Day - 2015
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-22
decision_details_body:
- United Nations Organization has declared the first Monday of the month of October every year as the 'World Habitat Day'.  Accordingly, this year's World Habitat Day falls on Monday the 05th of October and the theme followed this time is "Public Spaces for All".  

	It has been observed by the Ministry of Housing and Construction that there are many families reside for a long time in houses where only the preliminary construction work has been done and without having plastered the walls, in the housing construction process being implemented in various parts of the country and as a result issues have arisen such as reduction of economic value of houses, weakening of the strength of the houses by exposing them to elements of weather and causing  health problems like respiratory failures of  children and elderly living in these houses. 


	As such, in simultaneous to the World Habitat Day Celebration, the Ministry of Housing and Construction anticipates to implement a series of  islandwide programmes, in association with the institutions affiliated to the Ministry, other public institutions and organizations. The period from October 5th to 12th is to be declared as the "Habitat Week".  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Sajith Premadasa, the Minister of Housing and Construction, to implement the proposed programmes under the direction of the Ministry, to mark the World Habitat Day – 2015, to select 25,000 houses comprised of 1,000 from each district of which walls need to be plastered and to obtain Rs.250 million to implement the renovation programme through providing only the building materials worth of Rs.10,000/- maximum for each selected house, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Registration of Vehicles of Ministries, Departments and Government Institutions
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-22
decision_details_body:
- The Cabinet noted the information submitted to the Cabinet by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance with regard to the vehicles owned by each Ministry, Department and other Government Institutions. 
	
	Accordingly, the Cabinet further noted that the registered vehicles owned by the Ministries, Departments and other Institutions of the Government are 59,160 in number and out of these vehicles, a considerable number is found still being used by the Ministers, Deputy Ministers, Members of Parliament and who were engaged in various capacities in the last regime, but not functioning any more in such positions.  As such, the Cabinet decided to instruct the Secretaries to the Ministries, to take necessary action to retrieve the Government owned vehicles which are still being used by various persons without official entitlement, without delay.

description: The Establishment of a Joint Committee for Consular Affairs between the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the United Arab Emirates
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-22
decision_details_body:
- The formal diplomatic relations between Sri Lanka and United Arab Emirates (UAE) has commenced in 1979 and in recent years, the relationship has developed, encompassing a number of fields such as employing Sri Lankan employees, culture and education, in addition to trade and investment. Presently, about 250,000 Sri Lankans are employed in the UAE and Sri Lanka anticipates to further extend the existing partnership with the UAE to create more employment opportunities for Sri Lankans, especially in the 'Skilled Category'. At the first session of the Joint Commission between Sri Lanka and the United Arab Emirates held on 26th and 27th of January 2014 at Dubai, the two parties have agreed to establish a Joint Consular Committee, with a view to providing consular protection and assistance to the citizens of both countries.
	The objective of the establishment of this Committee is to strengthen and develop the cooperation in the Consular field between the two countries.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Mangala Samaraweera, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, to sign the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on the Establishment of a Joint Committee for Consular Affairs between the Democratic Republic of Sri Lanka and the United Arab Emirates and also to take appropriate action for the effective implementation of  the MOU, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Minimizing Waste in the use of Public Funds
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-22
decision_details_body:
- The Hon. Prime Minister having focused the attention of the Cabinet that the Government should demonstrate its commitment for frugality in spending public funds, the Cabinet decided to take action as follows to minimize waste in the use of public funds: 

that, foreign travels undertaken by Cabinet Ministers, State Ministers, Deputy Ministers, all other elected Representatives and Public Officers should be restricted as far as possible.

that, when undertaking foreign travels of essential nature, restriction of the members of the delegation, only to those whose participation is absolutely necessary at such events. 
 
that , after a formal assessment on the security to be provided to the dignitaries, people's representatives and officials at present, who have been provided with security escort, to take action to reduce the  security staff and the number of vehicles provided to them to a bare minimum. 

that to make applicable all the above mentioned guidelines to the Provincial Authorities, Defence Forces, State Owned Enterprises, Statutory Boards and Government Owned Companies as well.

description: Appointment of Advisors to Hon. Ministers
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-16
decision_details_body:
- The Secretary to the Cabinet having drawn the attention of the Cabinet of Ministers the need to have a policy decision with regard to the appointment of Advisors/Consultants and making payments to Advisors/Consultants so appointed, the Cabinet decided as follows: 

to consider only the experts who possess an in depth knowledge of the subject matter and functions of the Ministry and are viewed by the Minister as persons who can provide advise that cannot be expected from serving senior officers of that Ministry, for appointment as advisors to Ministers. 

only one Advisor/Consultant could be appointed to each Minster, but however, a maximum of only two Advisors/Consultants could be appointed to the Minister of a Ministry which has a wide purview and entrusted with two or more portfolios, subject to the approval of the Cabinet.  


In making monthly payments to the Advisors/Consultants so appointed, the attention should be focused on their fulfillment of a   high level of  academic  or professional qualifications pertaining to the subject matter of the relevant Ministry, on their contribution in pioneering programmes or projects of an innovative nature pertaining to the subject matter of the relevant Ministry, on themselves being persons who have held senior positions in the private sector drawing very high remuneration immediately prior to the appointment or who have held  senior most positions in the public service.

description: Colombo Port City Development Project - Extension of Agreement by a period of six months
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-16
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by Hon. Arjuna Ranatunga, the Minister of Ports and Shipping,  to extend the agreement signed on 2014-09-16 in respect of the Colombo City Development Project between the Government of Sri Lanka and the relevant Project Company by six months with effect from 2015-09-16 which is the date of expiry of that agreement, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Hemmathagama Water Supply Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-16
decision_details_body: The approval of the Cabinet Sub-Committee on Economic Affairs has also been received for the above project which is implemented utilizing Rs.3,303.26 million of Government funds and Euro 81.96 million of foreign funds. The people of the Divisional Secretariat Divisions of  Mawanella, Aranayake and Rambukkana will be benefited from this project. The proposal made by Hon. Rauff Hakeem, the Minister of City Planning and Water Supply, to proceed with the activities of the project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Management of Paddy Harvest in the Yala Season 2015
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-16
decision_details_body:
- Approval of the Cabinet was granted for the implementation of the following recommendations made by the Cabinet Sub-Committee appointed under the chairmanship of the Minister of Finance with a view to drawing up a plan to supervise the paddy harvest programme of the Yala Season 2015 and to providing concessions efficiently to farmers, in accordance with the decision taken at the Cabinet Meeting held on 2015-09-09. 

*	The 120,000 Mt of paddy anticipated to be purchased at the initial stage of the paddy purchasing programme to be increased by 40,000 Mt up to 160,000 Mt.

*	Allocation of additional financial provision of Rs.1,906 million required for the purpose.

*	In order to have of adequate storage facilities for the purchase of paddy in the upcoming Maha season of 2015/2016, disposal of Government owned excess paddy stocks through Paddy Marketing Board following the Government Procurement Procedure while maintaining the required buffer stock.

*	Minimizing the irregularities taking place in the purchase of paddy to enable the purchase paddy from more farmers.

*	Taking necessary action to strengthen the small and medium scale paddy millers who are now inactive, for extensive participation of the private sector in the paddy purchasing while implementing the Government paddy purchasing programme.

*	Creating a competition in the paddy purchasing through providing special temporary storage facilities for bulk purchasers who do not possess adequate storage facilities.

*	Encouraging the investments of the private sector for the production of bio - fuel making use of the surplus paddy available in the country after a successful paddy harvest during both the Yala and Maha seasons.  

*   	Encouraging the industries engaged in value added productions utilizing rice flour. 

*	Popularizing of new varieties of paddy suitable for the export market among farmers, as a long term solution.

*	Taking necessary steps for crop diversification, by introducing other field crops except paddy, for a season.

description: 'Programme on Strengthened Partnership for Social Integration' and 'Programme on Increased and Equitable Economic Growth'
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-16
decision_details_body: The Government of the Republic of Sri Lanka has signed two agreements in the year 2011, with the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) to obtain grant assistance for financing the 'Programme of Strengthened Partnership for Social Integration' and 'Programme of Increased and Equitable Economic Growth in the Emerging Regions'. Taking into consideration the current social, economic and political  background, the proposal made by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, to amend the name of the 'Programme of Strengthened Partnership for Social Integration' as 'Strengthened Partnership for Democratic Reforms and Social Integration' and to increase the contribution provided by USAID for that programme by further US$ 3.49 Million up to US$ 10.73 million and to amend the name of the 'Programme of Increased and Equitable Economic Growth in the Emerging Areas' which is important in provinces such as North, North Central, Eastern and Uva as 'Increased Equitable Economic Growth and Public Finance Management' and to increase the contribution provided by USAID by further US$ 3 million to obtain a sum of US$ 14.71 million for the programme, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: 'Wana Ropa' - National Tree Planting Proramme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-16
decision_details_body:
- The declining of forest cover is a special environmental issue faced by Sri Lanka and a target is set to increase the prevailing 29% of forest cover up to 32% from further 6,000 hectares through the implementation of three year National Programme on Environment Conservation during the period from 2016 - 2018.  Similarly, an effective liaison will be made in order to secure the sustainability of the Tree Planting programmes are being already implemented by the state and the non-state parties, with a view to enhancing the forest cover of Sri Lanka. 

	It has also been planned to implement a national tree planting programme known as "Wana Ropa" throughout the month of October, 2015 to increase the forest cover, to enhance the quality of the forest cover, to conserve biodiversity and natural ecosystems, to utilize bare lands for effective tree planting and promotion and management of commercial forestry. Various activities will be conducted as follows for the purpose:   
*	First Week  
	
	Promotion, maintenance and protection of forestry in order to protect special ecosystems under the theme of 'Ensure Forest Conservation' ('Wana Arana – Rekawarana') 
*	Second Week
	
	Promotion of greenery and to ensure its benefits reach people through planting trees that would help to form a canopy with stems of branches in and around human settlements under the theme of 'Enhance Greenery in Human Settlements' ('Jana Hisata - Thru Sevana').
* Third Week

	To make the Non-Governmental Organization and Private Sector active partners of the National Tree Planting Mission under the theme of 'Promote Partnerships with the non-state Stakeholders' ('Thuru Kepakaru - Api Nirathuru').
*	Fourth Week

	To encourage various segments of the society to take part in creative and sustainable forestation initiatives under the theme of 'Wana Aranata - Jana Sarana'.

	This programme will be implemented through out the Island in October 2015, at Divisional Secretariat Division level and District level and it has been proposed to organize awareness workshops on environment conservation, soil conservation projects and various environmental conservation activities at regional level. Accordingly, the proposal made by H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena in his capacity as the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to implement this programme with the active participation of all Government institutions, Private and Non-Governmental institutions, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement of Fertilizer for the Year 2015 (November Delivery)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-16
decision_details_body: - The supply of fertilizer to the farmers on a subsidy scheme  under the Fertilizer Subsidy Programme is being implemented by the Department of Agriculture through the Government owned Ceylon Fertilizer Company Limited (CFC) and the Colombo Commercial Fertilizer Limited.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Duminda Dissanayake, the Minister of Agriculture, to award the relevant contracts for the supply of the necessary quantity of fertilizer, as recommended by the Special Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SSCAPC), to be distributed among farmers, for the month of November 2015, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Registration of Deaths (Temporary Provisions) Act, No.19 of 2010
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-16
decision_details_body: - In terms of the provisions of Births and Deaths Registration Act, No.17 of 1951, the authority to register Deaths has been vested  with the Registrar General's Department.  However, as the Act does not provide provisions for the registration of Deaths occurred due to unnatural circumstances such as terrorist activities, civil riots or natural disasters and where the dead bodies of persons reported missing cannot be found, the Registration of Deaths (Temporary Provisions) Act, No.19 of 2010 was introduced as a solution to that impediment. Nevertheless, at instances where the relatives of a missing person do not accept the death of  that missing person due to some reason or other, it is impossible to register such disappearances as deaths under the above Act. It is observed that family members of missing person could not obtain any of their due entitlements in such instances.  As such, the proposal made by Hon. Vajira Abeywardena, the Minister of Home Affairs, to amend the Registration of Deaths (Temporary Provisions) Act, No.19 of 2010 to enable to issue a Certificate similar to that of a Certificate of Absence issued by many countries in respect of the missing person / a person suspected to be dead, in line with the internationally accepted practice, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Epilepsy Hospital and Healthcare Centres Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-16
decision_details_body: - The Government of Sri Lanka with the assistance of the Saudi Fund for Development, commenced the construction of  a Modern State of the Art Hospital for the treatment of the Epileptic patients in Sri Lanka in the year 2008. The implementation of this project was somewhat delayed due to various reasons and by now 90.5% of the project has been completed.  The hospital is due to be opened for clinical purposes in December, 2015. The proposal made by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, to obtain the additional sum of about US$ 12 million  further required for the purpose from the Saudi Fund for Development, for providing the necessary enhanced facilities to render a greater service to the people, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Consent of Sri Lanka to Minimize the Impact of the Climate Change, in Keeping with the Kyoto Protocol
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-16
decision_details_body:
- The Protocol adopted in the year 1997 in Kyoto, Japan, by the parties that are legally bound to achieve the objectives of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), which is the major Convention collectively adopted by the International Community to discuss the issues related to climate change is known as Kyoto Protocol. 

	Although, the Green House Gas Emissions by the industrialized countries were to be reduced by at least 5.2% against the gas level emitted by such countries in 1990, during the first commitment period of this Protocol, which implemented during the period of 2008 - 2012, but the target could not be achieved by the year 2012. Therefore, at the 8th meeting of the parties held in Doha-Qatar in the year 2012, a resolution was adopted to implement a Second Commitment Period by which it is anticipated to reduce the Green House Gas Emissions by the industrialized countries at least by 18% as against their emissions in 1990, individually or collectively, during the period of 2013-2020.  

	There is a risk of facing adverse affects by the island nations like Sri Lanka due to situations such as rise of sea level occurred due to increase of global warming that may be  caused as a result of excessive emission of Green House Gases by the developed industrialized countries. 

	Through expressing concurrence for the Second Commitment Period of the Kyoto Protocol, it will be possible for the member countries like Sri Lanka to exert  the developed industrialized  countries to reduce their excessive emission of carbon and also to obtain foreign aids from the nation parties for the implementation of various projects in that regard. 

	As such, the proposal made by H.E. the President, Maithripala Sirisena in his capacity as the the Minister of Mahaweli Development and Environment, to express the consent of Sri Lanka to protect the Earth through further providing the required assistance for the proposed Second Commitment Period of the Kyoto Protocol, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Upholding the Collective Responsibility of the Cabinet of Ministers
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-16
decision_details_body:
- In terms of the Article 42(2) of the Constitution, the Cabinet of Ministers is  charged with the direction and control of the Government of the Republic of Sri Lanka and is collectively responsible and answerable to the Parliament.  However, having considered the various issues arisen due to the disregard of that hallowed tradition at certain instances and also the delays caused in implementing the decisions, which should have been implemented forthwith in the best interest of the country, the following proposals made by H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, with a view to preventing such occurrences in the future, was approved by the Cabinet. 

*	that a pledge should be made by each Member of the Cabinet of Ministers that he/she would strictly adhere to and exhibit his/her dedication to uphold and to establish a virtuous political culture newly, with due respect to the hallowed tradition of upholding the Collective Responsibility of the Cabinet of Ministers.    

*	appointment of a Ministerial Committee to formulate a Code of Ethics  in keeping with the best practices of the good governance to be followed by the Members of the Cabinet voluntarily and adoption of the Code of Ethics so formulated by the Cabinet within one month. 

	Accordingly, all Ministers made a pledge at this meeting of the Cabinet of Ministers, to the effect that the Collective Responsibility of the Cabinet will be upheld.

description: Common Programme of the National Government
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-09
decision_details_body: - Hon. Prime Minister brought to the notice of the Cabinet, the necessity of the formulation of a Common Programme for the National Government, based on the proposals which are in the best interest of the country, included in the Election Manifestos submitted by the United National Party (UNP) and other political parties including the United People's Freedom Alliance (UPFA),  at the recently concluded general election, and that it is appropriate to conduct the future activities of the government accordingly. As such, the Cabinet agreed, that the said programme should be formulated under the leadership of H.E. the President and the Hon. Prime Minister.

description: Satellite for SAARC Countries to be launched by the Government of India
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-09
decision_details_body: - Member States of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) including Sri Lanka welcomed in principle, the offer made by India to develop and launch a Satellite, at the 18th SAARC summit held in Kathmandu, Nepal, in November 2014. India will design, build and launch the satellite as a gift from India to the SAARC Member States and in order to provide the services necessary to enhance the cooperation among the SAARC member countries, the Satellite will be located at 48°E.  In this backdrop, India expects to enter into specific Bilateral Agreements with each SAARC Member State, in regard to the proposed  Orbit Frequency Coordination of Satellite. As such, the  proposal made by  Hon. Mangala Samaraweera, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, to sign the proposed Bilateral Agreement between Sri Lanka and India, during the forthcoming Indian visit of the Hon. Prime Minister, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Tender for the Lightering of Coal for Lakvijaya Power Station, Puttalam
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-09
decision_details_body: The proposal made by  Hon. Arjuna Ranatunga, the Minister of Ports and Shipping, to award the tender invited by the Ceylon Shipping Corporation Limited, for the Lightering of Coal for Lakvijaya Power Station, Puttalam, as recommended by the Procurement Appeal Board, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Increasing the Authorized Limit on the Issue of Treasury Bills
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-09
decision_details_body: - The Parliament has approved that the maximum borrowing limit of the Government through various debt instruments should be Rs.1,780 billion. Based on that approved borrowing limit, the government makes use of various debt instruments such as issuance of Bonds, Treasury Bills and Administrative Borrowings, to meet the funding requirements of the government. Within the overall borrowing limit said above, the approved limit for the issuance of Treasury Bills exists in the limit of Rs.850 billion up to date since the year 2012, in terms of the Local Treasury Bills Ordinance.  Due to striving to meet the borrowing requirements through the Treasury Bills instead of using other debt instruments, the proposal made by  Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, to increase the said limit by a further Rs.400 billion up to Rs.1,250 billion and to present the related resolution in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Review of the Government Paddy Purchase Programme – Yala Season - 2015
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-09
decision_details_body: - On the information provided by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, the Cabinet noted that the Government has made its targets to purchase 120,000 mt of paddy in Yala Season - 2015 and Rs.6 billion is arranged through the two state banks, i.e. the Bank of Ceylon and the People's Bank, for the purpose and accordingly, 102,796.91 mt of paddy has been purchased by the government by 2015-09-07 spending a sum of Rs.4,653 million and that the paddy purchasing programme in the districts of Polonnaruwa, Hambantota and Mannar are yet to be completed due to the delayed harvest. As such, the Cabinet decided to appoint a Cabinet Sub_Committee chaired by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, to submit recommendations to the next Meeting of the Cabinet, after conducting further examinations pertaining to the purchasing of paddy during the Yala Season of 2015.

description: Pre-election Budgetary Position Report -2015
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-09
decision_details_body: - In terms of the Section 16 of the Fiscal Management (Responsibility) Act, No.3 of 2003, the Secretary to the Ministry of Finance is required to present a Pre_election Budgetary Position Report to the general public, incorporating the information on the fiscal position of the economy, after the publication of Proclamation requiring the holding of the general election and thereafter, to present it in the Parliament. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, to present “the Pre_election Budgetary Position Report 2015” containing the  provisional figures of government revenue, expenditure and borrowings during the first five (05) months of the year 2015 and the information on a broad fiscal outlook for the year 2015, in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Mid Year Fiscal Position Report - 2015
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-09
decision_details_body: - In terms of the Section 10 of the Fiscal Management (Responsibility) Act, No.3 of 2003, the Minister of Finance is required to issue the  Mid Year Fiscal Position Report to the general public by 30th June of every financial year and thereafter, to table it in Parliament. Accordingly, the proposal made by  Hon. Ravi Karunanayake, the Minister of Finance, to present 'the Mid Year Fiscal Position Report - 2015' which provides analyses of the macroeconomic situation of the country and the global economic trends and a detailed explanation on fiscal developments along with the updated information on the government's fiscal position pertaining to the first four (04) months of 2015, in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the Polgahawela, Pothuhera and Alawwa Integrated Water Supply Project and the Kundasale – Haragama Water Supply Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-09
decision_details_body: - The rapid urbanization, increasing commercial activities and the industrial zones have intensified the necessity of highly standardized water supply projects. Accordingly, the Government has planned to implement the Polgahawela, Pothuhera and Alawwa Integrated Water Supply Project and the Kunadasale – Haragama Water Supply Project at an estimated cost of US$ 280.1 million. The water source of Polgahawela, Pothuhera and Alawwa Integrated Water Supply Project is Ma Oya and the four Divisional Secretariat Divisions of  Polgahawela, Alawwa, Kurunegala (Part) and Weerambugedara will be covered through this project. A distribution network of 380 km will be established, meeting the present water supply demand of 10,000 m³ per day by providing 50,000 new water connections to 250,000 houses through the  Kunadasale – Haragama Water Supply Project. Therefore, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister Ranil Wickramasinghe, to obtain funds for the implementation of the above projects, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Rationalization of Government Procurement Procedure
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-09
decision_details_body: - A vast amount of money from the Government annual expenditure is spent on the purchasing of goods and services required to provide various services to the general public, such as constructions carried out under various development projects, procurement of capital goods and pharmaceuticals, fertilizer subsidies, text books and uniforms for school children. These purchases are done according to the Government Procurement Procedure and it is observed that the government has to face inordinate delays and disadvantages due to some shortcomings found in the procedure. Hence, the proposal made by H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, to appoint a Committee comprising of the proficient retired Public Service Officials who possess experience in this field, to submit suitable proposals to make the existing Government Procurement Procedure more efficient and effective, for the utilization of the Government funds more frugally in a manner so as to prevent waste and also to avoid fraud, corruption and irregularities, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: "Let's Awaken Polonnaruwa" - District Development Programme - 2016 - 2020
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-09-09
decision_details_body:
- Polonnaruwa District which forms a part of Rajarata area of 07 Divisional Secretariat Divisions and 295 Grama Niladhari Divisions. The infrastructure facilities, which are basically limited to the urban area are inadequate to meet the present day needs of the community and the infrastructure facilities such as health, education and roads available in the rural areas are of a very low standard. Especially, the infrastructure facilities available in the Divisional Secretariat Divisions of Welikanda, Dimbulagala, Medirigiriya and Lankapura affected by conflict situation which prevailed in the North and East are in a very poor state. As such, the people in the Polonnaruwa District lead a difficult life and are becoming more inclined to avail themselves of various services they need  from the adjoining districts. 

Under the above five year programme, it has been proposed to implement number of various development projects in the district at a cost of Rs.60 billion and out of which the Cabinet approval has already been granted to implement the Drinking Water Project and the Project on construction of a Hospital for Kidney Patients. It is expected to finance number of projects under  this programme through the personal donations obtained from the local and foreign parties. 

Several projects in the sectors such as Education, Health and Rural Roads which have been identified to be implemented expeditiously under the proposed five year plan, are anticipated to be initiated in the year 2015 and it has been estimated that these projects would involve a cost of approximately, Rs.750 million. Accordingly, the proposal made by H.E. the President Maithripala Sirisena, to implement the proposed District Development Programme -  "Let's Awaken Polonnaruwa" during the period of 2016 - 2020, and to initiate the projects that should be commenced expeditiously under the programme, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement of Fertilizer for the Year 2015 (October Delivery)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-08-05
decision_details_body: - The supply of fertilizer to the farmers on a subsidy scheme  under the Fertilizer Subsidy Programme is being implemented by the Department of Agriculture. The required quantity of fertilizer will be supplied through the Government owned fertilizer companies, namely the Ceylon Fertilizer Company Limited (CFC) and the Colombo Commercial Fertilizer Limited, in par with the monthly requirement.  Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Duminda Dissanayake, the Minister of Agriculture, to award the relevant contracts for the supply of the necessary quantity of fertilizer through above companies, as recommended by the Special Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SSCAPC), to distribute among farmers, for the month of October 2015, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Rehabilitation of the Railway Track between Maho / Vavuniya
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2015-08-05
decision_details_body: - The primary objective of the Sri Lanka Railways is to provide a safe,  reliable and punctual Rail Transport Service for passengers and for freight traffic. It has been identified by the Government, that a systematic improvement of the railway track is an essential factor for achieving the said objective.
